title.zh: 卷三百〇四 列傳第一百九十二 宦官一 鄭和 金英 王振 曹吉祥 懷恩 汪直 梁芳 何鼎 李廣 蔣琮 劉瑾 張永 谷大用
title.en: Volume 304 Biographies 192: Officials 1: Zheng He, Jin Ying, Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, Huai En, Wang Zhi, Liang Fang, He Ding, Li Guang, Jiang Cong, Liu Jin, Zhang Yong, Gu Dayong
title.raw: 卷三百〇四 列傳第一百九十二 宦官一 鄭和 金英 王振 曹吉祥 懷恩 汪直 梁芳 何鼎 李廣 蔣琮 劉瑾 張永 谷大用 Volume 304 Biographies 192: Officials 1: Zheng He, Jin Ying, Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, Huai En, Wang Zhi, Liang Fang, He Ding, Li Guang, Jiang Cong, Liu Jin, Zhang Yong, Gu Dayong

sentences.zh: 明太祖既定江左，鑒前代之失，置宦者不及百人。

translations.literal: After the Ming founder had secured the lower Yangzi, he took warning from the failings of earlier dynasties and kept fewer than a hundred eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Ming founder had consolidated his hold on the lower Yangzi, he studied the mistakes of earlier dynasties and kept the number of eunuchs to under a hundred.

sentences.zh: 迨末年頒《祖訓》，乃定為十有二監及各司局，稍稱備員矣。

translations.literal: By the end of his reign, when he issued the Ancestral Injunctions, they were fixed at twelve directorates and various offices, and could only just be said to be fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of his reign, when he promulgated the Ancestral Injunctions, the establishment was fixed at twelve directorates and the various bureaus—barely enough to count as a full complement.

sentences.zh: 然定制，不得兼外臣文武銜，不得御外臣冠服，官無過四品，月米一石，衣食於內庭。

translations.literal: But the established regulations forbade them from holding civilian or military titles outside the inner court, from wearing the hats and robes of outer ministers, and limited their rank to no higher than the fourth; they received one dan of rice a month and were housed and fed in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the standing regulations barred them from holding concurrent civil or military titles in the outer administration, from wearing the headgear and robes of outer ministers, and from rising above the fourth rank; they received one picul of rice a month and were clothed and fed within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗鐫鐵牌置宮門曰：「內臣不得干預政事，預者斬。」

translations.literal: He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He once had an iron tablet engraved and set up at the palace gate: "Inner servants must not meddle in government affairs—whoever does so shall be executed.

sentences.zh: 敕諸司不得與文移往來。

translations.literal: He also ordered the various offices not to exchange written documents with them.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the various ministries not to exchange official correspondence with them.

sentences.zh: 有老閹供事久，一日從容語及政事，帝大怒，即日斥還鄉。

translations.literal: There was an old eunuch who had long served the court; one day he spoke casually about government affairs, and the emperor was furious and expelled him back to his hometown that same day.
translations.idiomatic: An old eunuch who had long served at court once spoke casually about state affairs; the emperor flew into a rage and sent him home that very day.

sentences.zh: 嘗用杜安道為御用監。

translations.literal: He once employed Du Andao as Director of Imperial Services.
translations.idiomatic: He once appointed Du Andao director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 安道，外臣也，以鑷工侍帝數十年，帷幄計議皆與知，性縝密不泄，過諸大臣前一揖不啟口而退。

translations.literal: Andao was a commoner who served the emperor for several decades as a maker of tweezers; he was privy to all the plans and deliberations in the tented camp, was by nature meticulous and secretive, and whenever he passed the great ministers he would bow once and leave without saying a word.
translations.idiomatic: Andao was an outer subject who had served the emperor for decades as a metalworker; he was privy to every plan and deliberation in the field camp, was meticulous and tight-lipped by nature, and whenever he passed the senior ministers he would bow once and withdraw without a word.

sentences.zh: 太祖愛之，然亡他寵異，後遷出為光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: The Ming founder favored him, but did not grant him any other special favor; later he was transferred out as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The founder held him in esteem but granted him no further extraordinary favor; later he was transferred out to serve as minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有趙成者，洪武八年以內侍使河州市馬。

translations.literal: There was one Zhao Cheng; in the eighth year of Hongwu he was sent as an inner attendant to buy horses in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Cheng, whom in the eighth year of Hongwu the court sent as an inner attendant to purchase horses in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 其後以市馬出者，又有司禮監慶童等，然皆不敢有所干竊。

translations.literal: Later there were also those sent out to buy horses, such as Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, but none of them dared to meddle or pilfer anything.
translations.idiomatic: Later others were sent out on horse-buying missions as well, including Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial—but none of them dared to meddle in affairs or steal.

sentences.zh: 建文帝嗣位，御內臣益嚴，詔出外稍不法，許有司械聞。

translations.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants even more severely; he issued an edict that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, the local authorities were permitted to arrest and report them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen Emperor came to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants still further, decreeing that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, local officials might arrest them and report the matter.

sentences.zh: 及燕師逼江北，內臣多逃入其軍，漏朝廷虛實。

translations.literal: When the Yan army pressed against the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants fled into its ranks and leaked the court's weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army pressed to the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants deserted into his ranks and betrayed the court's strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 文皇以為忠於己，而狗兒輩復以軍功得幸，即位後遂多所委任。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor considered them loyal to him, and Gou'er and the others were further favored because of military merit; once he came to the throne, he entrusted them with many responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor regarded them as loyal to his cause, and men such as Dog'er won further favor through military service; once he took the throne, he entrusted them with ever wider responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，內官監李興奉敕往勞暹羅國王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the inner-court official Li Xing was ordered to go and present condolences to the king of Siam.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle, Li Xing of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs was ordered to travel to Siam and convey the emperor's condolences to its king.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣太監鄭和帥舟師下西洋。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zheng He was sent with a fleet as envoy to the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court dispatched the eunuch Zheng He to lead a fleet on the voyage to the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 八年，都督譚青營有內官王安等。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, at General Tan Qing's camp there were inner officials such as Wang An.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year inner officials such as Wang An were attached to the camp of the regional commander Tan Qing.

sentences.zh: 又命馬靖鎮甘肅，馬騏鎮交阯。

translations.literal: He also ordered Ma Jing to garrison Gansu and Ma Qi to garrison Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Ma Jing to take command in Gansu and Ma Qi to take command in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 十八年置東廠，令刺事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was established and ordered to investigate matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was set up and charged with intelligence gathering.

sentences.zh: 蓋明世宦官出使、專征、監軍、分鎮、刺臣民隱事諸大權，皆自永樂間始。

translations.literal: The great powers exercised by eunuchs in foreign missions, independent campaigns, military supervision, regional garrisons, and spying on the hidden affairs of ministers and commoners all began in the Yongle years.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the great powers later wielded by eunuchs—diplomatic missions abroad, independent military campaigns, supervision of armies, regional commands, and surveillance of ministers and commoners—all had their beginning in the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖制，內臣不許讀書識字。

translations.literal: At first, the Ming founder decreed that inner servants were not allowed to read books or learn characters.
translations.idiomatic: At first the founder had decreed that inner servants were not to study books or learn to read.

sentences.zh: 後宣宗設內書堂，選小內侍，令大學士陳山教習之，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Later the Xuande Emperor established an inner school hall, selected young inner attendants, and ordered the Grand Secretary Chen Shan to teach them, thus making it a fixed institution.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xuande Emperor set up an inner school, chose young eunuchs for instruction, and had the grand secretary Chen Shan teach them—thus fixing the practice as an institution.

sentences.zh: 用是多通文墨，曉古今，逞其智巧，逢君作奸。

translations.literal: As a result many became literate, understood past and present affairs, and used their intelligence and craftiness to curry favor and commit wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence many became literate and versed in affairs past and present, then turned their wit and cunning to winning the ruler's ear and doing evil.

sentences.zh: 數傳之後，勢成積重，始於王振，卒於魏忠賢。

translations.literal: After several generations, the abuse had become entrenched, beginning with Wang Zhen and ending with Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: After several generations the abuse had piled up into an immovable weight, beginning with Wang Zhen and ending with Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 考其禍敗，其去漢、唐何遠哉。

translations.literal: Looking at the disasters they caused, how far were they from those of the Han and Tang?
translations.idiomatic: When one weighs the calamities they brought, how far did they fall short of the eunuch disasters of Han and Tang?

sentences.zh: 雖間有賢者，如懷恩、李芳、陳矩輩，然利一而害百也。

translations.literal: Though there were occasional worthy men, such as Huai'en, Li Fang, and Chen Ju, the harm they caused outweighed the benefit of one.
translations.idiomatic: Though a few worthy men appeared among them—Huai'en, Li Fang, Chen Ju, and the like—for every one such man a hundred did harm.

sentences.zh: 今摭其有關成敗者，作《宦官傳》。

translations.literal: So now I have collected the cases relevant to success and failure and composed the Biography of Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore gathered the cases that bear on success and failure and composed this Biography of Eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 鄭和，雲南人，世所謂三保太監者也。

translations.literal: Zheng He was a man of Yunnan, known throughout the world as the Three Treasures eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He was a native of Yunnan, the man the world knows as the Three Treasures eunuch.

sentences.zh: 初事燕王於藩邸，從起兵有功。

translations.literal: At first he served the Prince of Yan in the princely residence and won merit by following him in his uprising.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Prince of Yan in his princely household and won merit by following him when he raised arms.

sentences.zh: 累擢太監。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to the rank of eunuch director.

sentences.zh: 成祖疑惠帝亡海外，欲蹤跡之，且欲耀兵異域，示中國富強。

translations.literal: Chengzu suspected that the Jianwen emperor had fled overseas, wanted to trace him, and also wished to display arms in foreign lands and show China's wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu suspected that the deposed Jianwen emperor had fled overseas and wished to track him down; he also wanted to project military power abroad and display the wealth and might of the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年六月，命和及其儕王景弘等通使西洋。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongle, he ordered Zheng He and his fellows Wang Jinghong and others to serve as envoys to the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongle he ordered Zheng He, Wang Jinghong, and their companions to serve as envoys to the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 將士卒二萬七千八百餘人，多賫金幣。

translations.literal: They had more than twenty-seven thousand eight hundred soldiers and carried large quantities of gold and valuables.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded more than twenty-seven thousand eight hundred troops and carried vast stores of gold and coin.

sentences.zh: 造大舶，修四十四丈、廣十八丈者六十二。

translations.literal: They built giant ships, sixty-two of them forty-four zhang long and eighteen zhang wide.
translations.idiomatic: They built great ships—sixty-two of them measuring forty-four zhang in length and eighteen zhang in beam.

sentences.zh: 自蘇州劉家河泛海至福建，復自福建五虎門揚帆，首達占城，以次遍歷諸番國，宣天子詔，因給賜其君長，不服則以武懾之。

translations.literal: They sailed from Liujiagang in Suzhou to Fujian, then again set sail from Wuhumen in Fujian; first they reached Champa, and then in turn visited all the foreign states, proclaiming the emperor's edict, granting gifts to their rulers, and using military force to overawe those who would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: They put to sea from Liujiagang in Suzhou, reached Fujian, and sailed again from Wuhumen; they made first for Champa, then in succession called at every foreign state, proclaiming the Son of Heaven's edicts, bestowing gifts on their rulers, and where submission was refused, backing persuasion with force.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，和等還，諸國使者隨和朝見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, He and the others returned, and envoys from the various states accompanied him to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year Zheng He and his fleet returned, and envoys from many states came with him to audience at court.

sentences.zh: 和獻所俘舊港酋長。

translations.literal: He presented the captive chieftain of Old Port.
translations.idiomatic: He presented as a prisoner the chieftain of Old Port.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，爵賞有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and graded the rewards and honors accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and distributed ranks and rewards in due measure.

sentences.zh: 舊港者，故三佛齊國也，其酋陳祖義，剽掠商旅。

translations.literal: Old Port was the former kingdom of Srivijaya; its chieftain Chen Zuyi had been plundering merchant shipping.
translations.idiomatic: Old Port was the site of the former Srivijaya kingdom; its chieftain Chen Zuyi had been preying on merchant shipping.

sentences.zh: 和使使招諭，祖義詐降，而潛謀邀劫。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon him and pacify him; Zuyi feigned surrender while secretly plotting an ambush and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He sent envoys to summon and pacify him; Zuyi pretended to submit while secretly plotting to waylay the fleet.

sentences.zh: 和大敗其眾，擒祖義，獻俘，戮於都市。

translations.literal: He utterly defeated his forces, captured Zuyi, presented the prisoners, and had him executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Zuyi's forces, captured him alive, presented him as a prisoner, and had him executed in the capital marketplace.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，再往錫蘭山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year they went again to Ceylon.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year they sailed again for Ceylon.

sentences.zh: 國王亞烈苦柰兒誘和至國中，索金幣，發兵劫和舟。

translations.literal: King Alakeshvara lured He into the country, demanded gold and valuables, and sent troops to seize He's ships.
translations.idiomatic: King Alakeshvara lured Zheng He inland, demanded gold and treasure, and sent troops to seize his ships.

sentences.zh: 和覘賊大眾既出，國內虛，率所統二千餘人，出不意攻破其城，生擒亞烈苦柰兒及其妻子官屬。

translations.literal: He saw that the enemy's main force had gone out and the country was empty, so he led the more than two thousand men under his command and, catching them off guard, attacked and took the city, capturing Alakeshvara alive together with his wife, children, and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the enemy's main force had marched out and the capital lay undefended, he led his two thousand-odd men in a surprise assault, took the city, and captured Alakeshvara alive together with his wife, children, and officials.

sentences.zh: 劫和舟者聞之，還自救，官軍復大破之。

translations.literal: When those who had seized He's ships heard of it, they returned to rescue them, and the imperial troops again dealt them a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The force that had seized his ships, hearing of this, hurried back to relieve the capital; the imperial troops routed them again.

sentences.zh: 九年六月獻俘於朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he presented the prisoners at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year he presented the captives at court.

sentences.zh: 帝赦不誅，釋歸國。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned them and did not execute them, but released them and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared their lives, released them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 是時，交阯已破滅，郡縣其地，諸邦益震詟，來者日多。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaozhi had already been conquered and turned into commanderies and counties; the various states were even more alarmed and awed, and those who came increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiaozhi had been conquered and organized into commanderies and counties; the foreign states were still more awed, and embassies to court grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 十年十一月，復命和等往使，至蘇門答剌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the tenth year He was again ordered to go as envoy, reaching Samudra.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the tenth year he was again ordered abroad and reached Samudra.

sentences.zh: 其前偽王子蘇幹剌者，方謀弒主自立，怒和賜不及己，率兵邀擊官軍。

translations.literal: The former pretender-prince Suganla was plotting to murder his lord and seize power; angered that He had not included him in the gifts, he led troops to intercept and attack the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: A former pretender, Suganla, was plotting to murder his sovereign and usurp the throne; furious that Zheng He had not included him in the gifts, he led troops to ambush the imperial force.

sentences.zh: 和力戰，追擒之喃渤利，並俘其妻子，以十三年七月還朝。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely, pursued and captured Nanbuli, and took his wife and children prisoner, returning to court in the seventh month of the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He fought hard, pursued and captured Nanbuli, and took his wife and children prisoner, returning to court in the seventh month of the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，賚諸將士有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and gave the generals and soldiers rewards in due rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded the commanders and troops according to merit.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，滿剌加、古裏等十九國咸遣使朝貢，辭還。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year, Melaka, Kuli, and nineteen other states all sent envoys to court and then took their leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year Melaka, Calicut, and nineteen other states all sent envoys to court and then departed.

sentences.zh: 復命和等偕往，賜其君長。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to go with them and bestow gifts on their rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He was again ordered to accompany them home and bestow gifts on their rulers.

sentences.zh: 十七年七月還。

translations.literal: They returned in the seventh month of the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: They returned in the seventh month of the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 十九年春復往，明年八月還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year they went again, and returned in the eighth month of the next year.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the nineteenth year they sailed again and came back in the eighth month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月，舊港酋長施濟孫請襲宣慰使職，和賫敕印往賜之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year, the chief of Old Port, Shi Jisun, requested to inherit the office of Pacification Commissioner; He carried the imperial edict and seal to bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-second year Shi Jisun, chieftain of Old Port, petitioned to inherit the post of pacification commissioner; Zheng He carried the imperial patent and seal to invest him.

sentences.zh: 比還，而成祖已晏駕。

translations.literal: By the time he returned, Chengzu had already died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned, Chengzu had already passed away.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年二月，仁宗命和以下番諸軍守備南京。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongxi, the emperor ordered He and the other maritime forces to guard Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Hongxi the new emperor ordered Zheng He and the maritime troops to take up the Nanjing garrison.

sentences.zh: 南京設守備，自和始也。

translations.literal: The Nanjing guard began with He.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing garrison command dates from Zheng He's appointment.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年六月，帝以踐阼歲久，而諸番國遠者猶未朝貢，於是和、景弘復奉命歷忽魯謨斯等十七國而還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuande, because the emperor had been on the throne for a long time and the distant states still had not come to offer tribute, He and Jinghong were again ordered to travel through seventeen states including Hormuz and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuande, because the emperor had been reigning for some years while distant states had still not come to pay tribute, Zheng He and Wang Jinghong were again ordered to visit seventeen states including Hormuz and return.

sentences.zh: 和經事三朝，先後七奉使，所歷占城、爪哇、真臘、舊港、暹羅、古裏、滿剌加、渤泥、蘇門答剌、阿魯、柯枝、大葛蘭、小葛蘭、西洋瑣裏、瑣裏、加異勒、阿撥把丹、南巫裏、甘把裏、錫蘭山、喃渤利、彭亨、急蘭丹、忽魯謨斯、比剌、溜山、孫剌、木骨都束、麻林、剌撒、祖法兒、沙裏灣泥、竹步、榜葛剌、天方、黎伐、那孤兒，凡三十餘國。

translations.literal: He served under three reigns and was sent out seven times; the places he visited included Champa, Java, Chenla, Old Port, Siam, Calicut, Melaka, Brunei, Samudra, Aru, Cochin, Great Calicut, Little Calicut, Western Ocean Suoli, Suoli, Jiayile, Ababadan, Nanwuli, Ganbali, Ceylon, Nanbuli, Pahang, Kelantan, Hormuz, Billa, Liushan, Sunla, Mogadishu, Malindi, Lasa, Zafar, Shaliwanni, Jubu, Bengal, Tianfang, Leifa, Naguer, and more than thirty states in all.
translations.idiomatic: He served three emperors and sailed on seven missions, calling at more than thirty states including Champa, Java, Chenla, Old Port, Siam, Calicut, Melaka, Brunei, Samudra, Aru, Cochin, Great and Little Calicut, Western and Eastern Suoli, Jiayile, Ababadan, Nanwuli, Ganbali, Ceylon, Nanbuli, Pahang, Kelantan, Hormuz, Billa, Liushan, Sunla, Mogadishu, Malindi, Lasa, Zafar, Shaliwanni, Jubu, Bengal, Tianfang, Leifa, and Naguer.

sentences.zh: 所取無名寶物，不可勝計，而中國耗廢亦不貲。

translations.literal: The treasures he obtained were beyond counting, but China too suffered heavy expense.
translations.idiomatic: The exotic goods he brought back were beyond reckoning, yet the empire paid a price that could not be measured in coin alone.

sentences.zh: 自宣德以還，遠方時有至者，要不如永樂時，而和亦老且死。

translations.literal: From the Xuande reign onward, people from distant regions sometimes came, but on the whole not as many as in Yongle's time, and He also grew old and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuande, visitors from afar still came from time to time, but never again in the numbers of the Yongle years—and Zheng He himself grew old and died.

sentences.zh: 自和後，凡將命海表者，莫不盛稱和以誇外番，故俗傳三保太監下西洋，為明初盛事云。

translations.literal: After He, anyone sent on missions to the seas always boasted of He to foreign states; thus the common saying that the Three Treasures eunuch went down to the Western Ocean has long been counted as one of the great achievements of the early Ming.
translations.idiomatic: After him, every envoy who sailed the seas invoked Zheng He's name to impress foreign rulers; hence the popular saying that the Three Treasures eunuch sailed the Western Ocean—a byword for the glory of early Ming.

sentences.zh: 當成祖時，銳意通四夷，奉使多用中貴。

translations.literal: During Chengzu's reign, he was intent on reaching the four quarters, and those sent on missions were mostly inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengzu's day the court was bent on reaching the four quarters of the earth, and most envoys were inner-court eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 西洋則和、景弘，西域則李達，迤北則海童，而西番則率使侯顯。

translations.literal: To the Western Ocean went He and Jinghong; to the Western Regions, Li Da; to the north, Haitong; and to the Western Barbarians, Hou Xian was generally sent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He and Wang Jinghong went to the Western Ocean; Li Da to the Western Regions; Haitong to the northern frontier; and Hou Xian was usually the man sent to the western barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 侯顯者，司禮少監。

translations.literal: Hou Xian was the deputy director of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xian served as deputy director of the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 帝聞烏思藏僧尚師哈立麻有道術，善幻化，欲致一見，因通迤西諸番。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the monk Shangshi Halima of U-Tsang possessed spiritual arts and could transform things, and wanted to meet him, thereby opening communication with the western states.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that the Ü-Tsang monk known as Shangshi Halima possessed occult powers and could work wonders; wishing to see him, he opened communications with the western regions.

sentences.zh: 乃命顯賫書幣往迓，選壯士健馬護行。

translations.literal: So he ordered Xian to carry letters and gifts to invite him, and selected strong soldiers and sturdy horses to escort the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Hou Xian to carry letters and gifts to invite the monk, choosing stalwart troops and hardy horses to escort the mission.

sentences.zh: 元年四月奉使，陸行數萬里，至四年十二月始與其僧偕來，詔駙馬都尉沐昕迎之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year he received the mission; he traveled overland for tens of thousands of li and only in the twelfth month of the fourth year did he finally arrive together with the monk, whereupon an edict ordered the imperial son-in-law Mu Xin to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He set out in the fourth month of the first year, marched overland for tens of thousands of li, and only in the twelfth month of the fourth year did he return with the monk; an edict then ordered the imperial son-in-law Mu Xin to meet them.

sentences.zh: 帝延見奉天殿，寵賚優渥，儀仗鞍馬什器多以金銀為之，道路烜赫。

translations.literal: The emperor received him in Fengtian Hall and showered him with generous gifts; the ceremonial banners, saddles, horses, and utensils were mostly made of gold and silver, and the roads shone with splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him in the Hall of Imperial Heaven and heaped gifts upon him; banners, saddles, horses, and ritual vessels were mostly wrought in gold and silver, and the roads blazed with pageantry.

sentences.zh: 五年二月建普度大齋於靈谷寺，為高帝、高後薦福。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, a great Buddhist fasting rite was established at Linggu Temple to pray for blessings for the High Emperor and Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year a great Buddhist mass was held at Linggu Temple to pray for the blessings of the dynastic founders.

sentences.zh: 或言卿雲、天花、甘露、甘雨、青鳥、青獅、白象、白鶴及舍利祥光，連日畢見，又聞梵唄天樂自空而下。

translations.literal: It was said that auspicious signs such as clouds of good omen, heavenly flowers, sweet dew, sweet rain, blue birds, blue lions, white elephants, white cranes, and relic light all appeared day after day, and they also heard Buddhist chant and heavenly music descending from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Reports claimed that day after day there appeared auspicious clouds, flowers raining from heaven, sweet dew, timely rain, blue birds, blue lions, white elephants, white cranes, and radiance from the Buddha's relics, while Buddhist chant and celestial music were heard descending from the sky.

sentences.zh: 帝益大喜，廷臣表賀，學士胡廣等咸獻《聖孝瑞應歌》詩。

translations.literal: The emperor was even more delighted; court ministers submitted congratulations, and the Hanlin academicians Hu Guang and others all offered the poem Sacred Filial Auspicious Response Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more pleased; court ministers offered congratulatory memorials, and the Hanlin academicians Hu Guang and others each presented a poem entitled "Song of Sacred Filial Piety and Auspicious Response."

sentences.zh: 乃封哈立麻萬行具足十方最勝圓覺妙智慧善普應祐國演教如來大寶法王西天大善自在佛，領天下釋教，給印誥制如諸王，其徒三人亦封灌頂大國師，再宴奉天殿。

translations.literal: Halima was then granted the title Great Treasure Dharma King, All-Pervasive Wisdom, Perfect Enlightenment, Most Victorious in the Ten Directions, Wonderfully Wise, Universally Responsive, Protector of the State, Promulgator of the Teaching, Thus-Come One of the Western Heaven, Greatly Compassionate Self-Existent Buddha of the Western Heaven, with authority over all Buddhism under heaven; he received seals and patents like a prince, his three disciples were enfeoffed as great national masters of empowerment, and they were banqueted again in the Hall of Imperial Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Halima was then invested with the full title of Great Treasure Dharma King of the Western Heaven and given authority over all Buddhism in the realm, with seals and patents like those of a prince; his three disciples were enfeoffed as great national masters of empowerment, and the court feasted them again in the Hall of Imperial Heaven.

sentences.zh: 顯以奉使勞，擢太監。

translations.literal: Because of his service on the mission, Xian was promoted to eunuch director.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors on the mission Hou Xian was promoted to eunuch director.

sentences.zh: 十一年春復奉命，賜西番尼八剌、地湧塔二國。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he again received orders, and was given gifts to bestow on the Western states of Nepal and Diyongta.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was again dispatched with gifts for the western states of Nepal and Diyongta.

sentences.zh: 尼八剌王沙的新葛遣使隨顯入朝，表貢方物。

translations.literal: The king of Nepal, Shadenige, sent envoys with Xian to court and present tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Nepal, Shadenige, sent envoys to accompany Hou Xian to court with tribute of local products.

sentences.zh: 詔封國王，賜誥印。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him enfeoffed as king and given a patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as king and granted patent and seal.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月，帝欲通榜葛剌諸國，復命顯率舟師以行，其國即東印度之地，去中國絕遠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, the emperor wanted to communicate with the states of Bengal and others, and again ordered Xian to lead a fleet there; that country was in eastern India, extremely far from China.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year the emperor wished to open relations with Bengal and other states and again ordered Hou Xian to lead a fleet thither—Bengal lay in eastern India, immeasurably far from China.

sentences.zh: 其王賽佛丁遣使貢麒麟及諸方物。

translations.literal: Its king, Saifuding, sent envoys offering qilin and various local products.
translations.idiomatic: Its king Saifuding sent envoys bearing a qilin and other tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，錫予有加。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and added to the rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and increased the gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 榜葛剌之西，有國曰沼納樸兒者，地居五印度中，古佛國也，侵榜葛剌。

translations.literal: West of Bengal there was a country called Zhaonapuer, located in the middle of the Five Indies and an ancient Buddhist country; it had invaded Bengal.
translations.idiomatic: West of Bengal lay a state called Zhaonapuer, situated among the Five Indies and an ancient Buddhist land; it had invaded Bengal.

sentences.zh: 賽佛丁告於朝。

translations.literal: Saifuding reported it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Saifuding reported the invasion to the court.

sentences.zh: 十八年九月命顯往宣諭，賜金幣，遂罷兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year Xian was ordered to go and announce this and pacify them; he bestowed gold and valuables, and the troops were then withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year Hou Xian was ordered to go and proclaim the imperial will; he bestowed gold and treasure, and the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年二月復使顯賜諸番，遍歷烏斯藏、必力工瓦、靈藏、思達藏諸國而還。

translations.literal: In the second month of Xuande's second year, Xian was again sent to bestow gifts on the foreign states, traveling through U-Tsang, Biligongwa, Lingzang, Sidazang, and the other countries before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Xuande he was again sent to bestow gifts on the western states, passing through Ü-Tsang, Biligongwa, Lingzang, Sidazang, and other lands before returning.

sentences.zh: 途遇寇劫，督將士力戰，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: On the way they encountered bandits, and he directed the generals and soldiers in a fierce battle, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they were set upon by bandits; he led the troops in hard fighting and killed or captured many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 還朝，錄功升賞者四百六十餘人。

translations.literal: On return to court, more than four hundred and sixty men were recorded for merit promotion and reward.
translations.idiomatic: On his return more than four hundred and sixty men were entered on the rolls for promotion and reward.

sentences.zh: 顯有才辨，強力敢任，五使絕域，勞績與鄭和亞。

translations.literal: Xian was eloquent, strong, and bold in taking responsibility; on five missions to distant lands, his achievements were second only to Zheng He.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xian was quick-witted, physically strong, and bold in action; on five missions to the ends of the earth his achievements ranked only below Zheng He's.

sentences.zh: 金英

translations.literal: Jin Ying
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ying

sentences.zh: 金英者，宣宗朝司禮太監也，親信用事。

translations.literal: Jin Ying (Xing'an) was the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service under the Xuande emperor, and he was personally trusted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ying served as the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial under the Xuande emperor and was personally trusted.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年賜英及範弘免死詔，辭極褒美。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande, an amnesty exempting Ying and Fan Hong from death was issued, and it praised them lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuande an edict of grace exempting Ying and Fan Hong from the death penalty was issued, couched in the most flattering terms.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，與興安並貴幸。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong emperor ascended the throne, he and Xing'an were both powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong came to the throne, Ying and Xing'an alike rose to power and imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 及王振擅權，英不敢與抗。

translations.literal: By the time Wang Zhen monopolized power, Ying did not dare contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Zhen had seized control of the government, Ying no longer dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年夏旱，命英理刑部、都察院獄囚，築壇大理寺。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, there was a drought; Ying was ordered to handle prisoners in the Ministry of Justice and Censorate, and an altar was erected at Dali Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, during a drought, Ying was ordered to review prisoners held by the Ministry of Justice and the Censorate; an altar was set up at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 英張黃蓋中坐，尚書以下左右列坐。

translations.literal: Ying sat beneath a yellow canopy; ministers and those below sat on the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sat beneath a yellow canopy while the ministers ranged themselves to his left and right.

sentences.zh: 自是六年一審錄，制皆如此。

translations.literal: From then on there was a review every six years, and the system was established thus.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth a judicial review was held every six years, and this became the fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 其秋，英宗北狩，中外大震。

translations.literal: That autumn the Yingzong emperor was captured in the north, and the court and the provinces were thrown into great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor was taken captive on the northern campaign, and court and country alike were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 郕王使英、安等召廷臣問計。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng sent Ying, An, and others to summon the court ministers and ask what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cheng sent Ying, An, and others to summon the ministers and ask their counsel.

sentences.zh: 侍讀徐呈倡議南遷，安叱之，令扶呈出，大言曰：「敢言遷者斬！」

translations.literal: Reading Attendant Xu Cheng proposed moving the court south; An shouted at him, ordered that Xu Cheng be dragged out, and loudly declared: Anyone who dares speak of moving shall be executed!
translations.idiomatic: The reading attendant Xu Cheng urged removing the court south of the Yangzi; An berated him, had him dragged out, and thundered: "Whoever dares speak of moving the capital shall die!

sentences.zh: 遂入告太后，勸郕王任于謙治戰守。

translations.literal: Then he went in to inform the Empress Dowager and urged the Prince of Cheng to entrust Yu Qian with the defense of war and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in to report to the empress dowager and urged the Prince of Cheng to put Yu Qian in charge of the defense.

sentences.zh: 或曰叱呈者，英也。

translations.literal: Some said that Ying was the one who shouted at Xu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that it was Ying who had berated Xu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 也先入寇，至德勝門，景帝敕安與李永昌同于謙、石亨總理軍務。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded and reached Desheng Gate, the Jingtai Emperor ordered An and Li Yongchang, together with Yu Qian and Shi Heng, to oversee military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded and reached Desheng Gate, the Jingtai emperor ordered An and Li Yongchang, together with Yu Qian and Shi Heng, to take overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 永昌，亦司禮近侍也。

translations.literal: Yongchang, too, was a close attendant in the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang, too, was an inner attendant of the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年十一月，英犯贓罪，下獄論死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jingtai, Ying was charged with a corruption offense, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jingtai, Ying was charged with corruption, imprisoned, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 帝令禁錮之，終景帝世廢不用，獨任安。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him confined; for the rest of Jingtai's reign he was set aside and not used, with An alone remaining in favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him imprisoned instead; for the rest of the Jingtai reign he languished unused while An alone retained favor.

sentences.zh: 也先遣使議和，請迎上皇，廷議報使。

translations.literal: Esen sent envoys to negotiate peace and requested the return of the captive emperor; the court debated how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Esen sent envoys to sue for peace and ask that the captive emperor be returned; the court debated how to answer.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，令安出，呼群臣曰：「公等欲報使，孰可者？

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, sent An out, and summoned the ministers, saying: "If you wish to send a reply envoy, who is suitable?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, sent An out, and called the ministers together: "You wish to send a return envoy—who is fit for the task?

sentences.zh: 孰為文天祥、富弼！」

translations.literal: Who could be a Wen Tianxiang or a Fu Bi?
translations.idiomatic: Who among you is another Wen Tianxiang or Fu Bi?

sentences.zh: 詞色俱厲。

translations.literal: His words and expression were both severe.
translations.idiomatic: His tone and manner were fierce.

sentences.zh: 尚書王直面折之，安語塞。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Zhi rebuked him to his face, and An had nothing more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Zhi rebuked him to his face, and An was left speechless.

sentences.zh: 及遣都給事中李寔往，敕書不及迎上皇。

translations.literal: When Chief Envoy Li Shi was sent, the imperial rescript did not mention bringing back the captive emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Envoy Li Shi was dispatched, the imperial letter made no mention of restoring the captive emperor.

sentences.zh: 寔驚，走白內閣，遇安。

translations.literal: Shi was alarmed and hurried to report it to the Grand Secretariat, where he ran into An.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was alarmed and hurried to the Grand Secretariat to report this; there he met An.

sentences.zh: 安復詬曰：「若奉黃紙詔行耳，他何預！」

translations.literal: An cursed him again, saying: "You have only to carry out the yellow-paper edict—what business is it of yours otherwise!
translations.idiomatic: An berated him again: "Your duty is to carry out the yellow-paper edict—nothing else concerns you!

sentences.zh: 及易儲諸，人遂疑安預謀矣。

translations.literal: When the succession was altered, people therefore suspected that An had been involved in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was changed, people came to suspect that An had had a hand in the plot.

sentences.zh: 安有廉操，且知于謙賢，力護之。

translations.literal: An had an upright character, and because he knew Yu Qian was worthy, he protected him vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: An was upright in conduct; knowing Yu Qian's worth, he shielded him steadfastly.

sentences.zh: 或言帝任謙太過，安曰：「為國分憂如于公者，寧有二人！」

translations.literal: When some said the emperor trusted Qian too much, An replied: "For sharing the state's burdens as Yu Gong does, could there be two such men!"
translations.idiomatic: When some said the emperor relied on Qian too heavily, An replied: "Men who bear the state's troubles as Yu Qian does—are there two of them?"

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，蓋磔景帝所用太監王誠、舒良、張永、王勤等，謂其與黃厷構邪議，易太子，且與于謙、王文謀立外藩。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was restored, he had the eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, Wang Qin, and others who had served the Jingtai Emperor torn to pieces, saying they had joined Huang Gong in plotting evil schemes, changing the crown prince, and conspiring with Yu Qian and Wang Wen to install a prince from outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored to the throne, he had torn to pieces the eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, Wang Qin, and others who had served Jingtai, charging that with Huang Gong they had hatched wicked plots, changed the heir, and conspired with Yu Qian and Wang Wen to set up a prince from outside the succession.

sentences.zh: 於是給事、御史皆言安與誠、良等為黨，宜同罪。

translations.literal: Then the supervising secretaries and censors all said that An and Cheng, Liang, and the others were of one party and should be punished together.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries and censors then all urged that An was of the same faction as Cheng, Liang, and the rest and should suffer the same penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝宥之，但奪職。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned him, but stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared his life but stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 是時，中官坐誅者甚眾，安僅獲免云。

translations.literal: At that time many palace eunuchs were executed, and An alone barely escaped, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Many eunuchs were put to death at that time; An alone, it is said, barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 安佞佛，臨歿，遺命舂骨為灰，以供浮屠。

translations.literal: An was devoutly Buddhist, and as he lay dying he left instructions that his bones be pounded to ash for an offering to the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: An was a devout Buddhist; on his deathbed he ordered his bones ground to powder as an offering to the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 范弘，交阯人，初名安。

translations.literal: Fan Hong was a man of Jiaozhi; his original name was An.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hong was a native of Jiaozhi; his original name was An.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，英國公張輔以交童之美秀者還，選為奄，弘及王瑾、阮安、阮浪等與焉。

translations.literal: During Yongle, the Duke of Ying Zhang Fu returned with handsome youths from Jiaozhi and selected them for castration; Hong, Wang Jin, Ruan An, Ruan Lang, and others were among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle reign the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, brought back handsome boys from Jiaozhi and had them castrated; Hong, Wang Jin, Ruan An, Ruan Lang, and others were chosen.

sentences.zh: 占對嫻雅，成祖愛之，教令讀書，涉經史，善筆劄，侍仁宗東宮。

translations.literal: He answered questions with ease and elegance. Chengzu loved him, had him taught to read, let him study the Classics and Histories, and found him skilled with brush and writing; he served in the Eastern Palace of the Renzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with fluent grace. Chengzu favored him, had him taught to read, and set him to study the classics and histories; skilled with brush and document, he served in the crown prince's Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，為更名，累遷司禮太監，偕英受免死詔，又偕英及御用太監王瑾同賜銀記。

translations.literal: At the start of Xuande, he was given a new name, repeatedly promoted to eunuch director of the Directorate of Ceremonial, received an amnesty from death together with Ying, and later, together with Ying and the imperial-manufactories eunuch Wang Jin, was also granted a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuande he was given a new name, rose to eunuch director of the Directorate of Ceremonial, received the death-exemption edict together with Ying, and later with Ying and Wang Jin of the imperial manufactories was granted a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 正統時，英宗眷弘，嘗目之曰蓬來吉士。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, the Yingzong Emperor favored Hong and once called him a lucky man from Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong years Yingzong favored Hong and once called him a blessed guest from Penglai.

sentences.zh: 十四年從征，歿於土木，喪歸，葬香山水安寺，弘建也。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the campaign and died at Tumu; his remains were brought home and buried at Shui'an Temple on Xiangshan, which Hong had built.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he accompanied the northern campaign and died at Tumu; his body was brought home and buried at Shui'an Temple on Fragrant Hills, which Hong himself had founded.

sentences.zh: 而王瑾至景泰時始卒。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, by contrast, died only in the Jingtai period.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, by contrast, did not die until the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 瑾，初名陳蕪。

translations.literal: Jin's original name was Chen Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's original name was Chen Wu.

sentences.zh: 宣宗為皇太孫時，朝夕給事。

translations.literal: When the future Xuanzong was crown prince grandson, he served him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Xuanzong was still heir apparent as imperial grandson, Jin attended him from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 及即位，賜姓名。

translations.literal: When he came to the throne, he gave him a new name.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, he bestowed on him the name Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 從征漢王高煦還，參預四方兵事，賞賚累巨萬，數賜銀記曰「忠肝義膽」，曰「金貂貴客」，曰「忠誠自勵」，曰「心跡雙清」。

translations.literal: After returning from the campaign against the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, he took part in military affairs in every quarter, received rewards amounting to many tens of thousands, and was repeatedly given silver tallies inscribed "Loyal Liver and Righteous Gall," "Golden Marten and Noble Guest," "Loyal Self-Encouragement," and "Heart and Conduct Both Pure."
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against the Prince of Han he took part in military affairs throughout the realm, amassed rewards in the tens of thousands, and received silver tallies again and again bearing such inscriptions as "Loyal Liver and Righteous Gall," "Golden Marten and Noble Guest," "Loyal Self-Encouragement," and "Heart and Conduct Both Pure."

sentences.zh: 又賜以兩宮人，官其養子王椿。

translations.literal: He was also given two palace women, and his adopted son Wang Chun was made an official.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given two palace women, and his adopted son Wang Chun was granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 其受寵眷，英、弘莫逮也。

translations.literal: In the favor he received, neither Ying nor Hong could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In imperial favor neither Ying nor Hong could rival him.

sentences.zh: 阮安有巧思，奉成祖命營北京城池宮殿及百司府廨，目量意營，悉中規制，工部奉行而已。

translations.literal: Ruan An had inventive skill. By Chengzu's order he planned Beijing's walls, palaces, and the offices of the hundred departments; measuring by eye and working from his own design, he made everything conform to regulation, and the Ministry of Works merely carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan An was ingenious in design. By Chengzu's order he laid out Beijing's walls, palaces, and the offices of the hundred bureaus; estimating by eye and planning from his own judgment, he made everything conform to the rules while the Ministry of Works simply executed his plans.

sentences.zh: 正統時，重建三殿，治楊村河，並有功。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong, he rebuilt the Three Halls and managed the Yangcun River, and had merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign he rebuilt the Three Halls and regulated the Yangcun River, earning merit in both undertakings.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，治張秋河，道卒，囊無十金。

translations.literal: In Jingtai, while managing the Zhangqiu River, he died on the road, with less than ten taels in his purse.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai, while working on the Zhangqiu River, he died on the road with less than ten taels in his purse.

sentences.zh: 阮浪至景帝時，為御用監少監。

translations.literal: By the Jingtai Emperor's time, Ruan Lang was deputy director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingtai reign Ruan Lang had become deputy director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 英宗居南宮，浪入侍，賜鍍金繡袋及鍍金刀。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was in the Southern Palace, Lang attended him and was given a gilded embroidered pouch and a gilded knife.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingzong was confined in the Southern Palace, Lang waited on him and received a gilded embroidered pouch and a gilded knife.

sentences.zh: 浪以贈門下皇城使王瑤。

translations.literal: Lang gave them to Wang Yao, a gate attendant of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: Lang gave them to Wang Yao, an attendant at the gates of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛指揮盧忠者，險人也，見瑤袋刀異常制，醉瑤而竊之，以告尚衣監高平。

translations.literal: Lu Zhong, commander of the Brocade Guard, was a treacherous man; seeing that Yao's pouch and knife were of an unusual pattern, he got Yao drunk, stole them, and reported the matter to Gao Ping of the Directorate of Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhong, a commander of the Brocade Guard, was a vicious man; noticing that Yao's pouch and knife were of an unusual make, he got Yao drunk, stole them, and denounced him to Gao Ping of the Directorate of Imperial Wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 平令校尉李善上變，言浪傳上皇命，以袋刀結瑤謀復位。

translations.literal: Gao Ping ordered the sergeant Li Shan to file a denunciation, saying Lang had transmitted the captive emperor's order and used the pouch and knife to win over Yao in a plot to restore the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ping had the corporal Li Shan lodge a secret report claiming that Lang had conveyed the captive emperor's command and used the pouch and knife to bind Yao to a plot of restoration.

sentences.zh: 景帝下浪、瑤詔獄，忠證之，浪、瑤皆磔死，詞終不及上皇。

translations.literal: The Jingtai Emperor sent Lang and Yao to the imperial prison; Zhong testified against them, and Lang and Yao were both torn to death, though their statements never mentioned the captive emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingtai emperor had Lang and Yao thrown into prison; Zhong bore witness against them, and both were torn to pieces—yet their confessions never implicated the captive emperor.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，磔忠及平，而贈浪太監。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was restored, Zhong and Ping were torn to death, and Lang was posthumously made eunuch director.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored, Zhong and Ping were torn to pieces, and Lang was posthumously promoted to eunuch director.

sentences.zh: 王振，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少選入內書堂。

translations.literal: He was selected young and entered the inner school hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen while still young, he entered the inner school.

sentences.zh: 侍英宗東宮，為局郎。

translations.literal: He served in the Eastern Palace of the Yingzong Emperor as a bureau attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yingzong in the Eastern Palace as a bureau attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖禁中官預政。

translations.literal: At first, the Ming founder forbade palace eunuchs from taking part in government.
translations.idiomatic: At first the founder had forbidden palace eunuchs to meddle in government.

sentences.zh: 自永樂後，漸加委寄，然犯法輒置極典。

translations.literal: After Yongle, they were gradually entrusted with more responsibilities, but whenever they broke the law, they were punished with the harshest penalties.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle they were gradually given heavier responsibilities, yet any who broke the law were punished with the utmost severity.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，袁琦令阮巨隊等出外采辦。

translations.literal: During the Xuanzong reign, Yuan Qi sent Ruan Judui and others outside to procure goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande reign Yuan Qi sent Ruan Judui and others outside the capital on procurement missions.

sentences.zh: 事覺，琦磔死，巨隊等皆斬。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Qi was torn to death and Judui and the others were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Qi was torn to pieces and Judui and the rest were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又裴可烈等不法，立誅之。

translations.literal: When Pei Kelie and others also acted unlawfully, they were executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Kelie and others likewise broke the law, they too were put to death immediately.

sentences.zh: 諸中官以是不敢肆。

translations.literal: Because of this, the palace eunuchs did not dare to run wild.
translations.idiomatic: After such examples the eunuchs did not dare act recklessly.

sentences.zh: 及英宗立，年少。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne, he was still young.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong came to the throne he was still a youth.

sentences.zh: 振狡黠得帝歡，遂越金英等數人掌司禮監，導帝用重典禦下，防大臣欺蔽。

translations.literal: Zhen, crafty and sly, won the emperor's favor and was thus put over Jin Ying and several others to run the Directorate of Ceremonial; he led the emperor to use harsh laws to control his subordinates and guard against ministers' deceit and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, cunning and sly, won the young emperor's affection, rose above Jin Ying and several others to head the Directorate of Ceremonial, and taught him to rule his subordinates with harsh punishments and to guard against deception by his ministers.

sentences.zh: 於是大臣下獄者不絕，而振得因以市權。

translations.literal: Thereafter, ministers were sent to prison without end, and Zhen used the situation to barter for power.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ministers were cast into prison without cease, and Zhen traded on the terror to amass power.

sentences.zh: 然是時，太皇太后賢，方委政內閣。

translations.literal: But at this time the Grand Empress Dowager was capable and was entrusting power to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this time the grand empress dowager was wise and had entrusted affairs to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 閣臣楊士奇、楊榮、楊溥，皆累朝元老，振心憚之未敢逞。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Yang Pu were all veteran ministers across several reigns, and Zhen feared them in his heart and did not dare act freely.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Yang Pu were veterans of several reigns, and Zhen feared them inwardly and did not yet dare run riot.

sentences.zh: 至正統七年，太皇太后崩，榮已先卒，士奇以子稷論死不出，溥老病，新閣臣馬愉、曹鼐勢輕，振遂跋扈不可制。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Zhengtong, the Grand Empress Dowager died; Rong had already passed away, Shiqi stayed home because his son Ji had been condemned to death, Pu was old and ill, and the new Grand Secretaries Ma Yu and Cao Nai were weak in power, so Zhen became overbearing and uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh year of Zhengtong the grand empress dowager had died; Rong was already gone; Shiqi kept to his home after his son Ji was condemned to death; Pu was aged and ill; and the new grand secretaries Ma Yu and Cao Nai carried little weight—so Zhen grew arrogant beyond restraint.

sentences.zh: 作大第皇城東，建智化寺，窮極土木。

translations.literal: He built a vast mansion east of the imperial city and constructed Zhihua Temple, exhausting all the resources of labor and wood.
translations.idiomatic: He built a great mansion east of the imperial city and raised Zhihua Temple, lavishing labor and timber without limit.

sentences.zh: 興麓川之師，西南騷動。

translations.literal: He launched the campaign against Luchuan, and the southwest was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He launched the Luchuan campaign, and the southwest was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 侍講劉球因雷震上言陳得失，語刺振。

translations.literal: The attending lecturer Liu Qiu used a thunderstorm as the occasion to submit a memorial laying out merits and faults; his words were aimed at Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The lecturer Liu Qiu seized on a thunderstorm to submit a memorial on the state's gains and losses, his words pointed at Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振下球獄，使指揮馬順支解之。

translations.literal: Zhen had Qiu thrown into prison and ordered Commander Ma Shun to dismember him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had Qiu thrown into prison and ordered the commander Ma Shun to hack him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿薛瑄、祭酒李時勉素不禮振。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Xue Xuan and Administrator Li Shimian had long shown Zhen no respect.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, Xue Xuan, and the administrator Li Shimian had long refused to defer to Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振摭他事陷瑄幾死，時勉至荷校國子監門。

translations.literal: Zhen seized on other matters to implicate Xuan and nearly kill him; Shimian was made to wear the cangue at the gate of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen seized on other charges to trap Xuan and nearly killed him; Shimian was made to wear the cangue at the gate of the National Academy.

sentences.zh: 御史李鐸遇振不跪，謫戍鐵嶺衛。

translations.literal: When the censor Li Duo met Zhen, he did not kneel; he was demoted to garrison service at Tieling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Li Duo failed to kneel when he met Zhen and was banished to garrison duty at Tieling Guard.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉石璟詈其家閹，振惡賤己同類，下璟獄。

translations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Shi Jing cursed the eunuch in his household; Zhen hated his insulting one of his own kind and had Jing imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son-in-law Shi Jing reviled a eunuch in his household; Zhen, resenting the insult to one of his kind, had Jing thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 怒霸州知州張需禁飭牧馬校卒，逮之，並坐需舉主王鐸。

translations.literal: Angered that Zhang Xu, magistrate of Bazhou, had restrained the horse grooms and drillers, he had Zhang arrested and also implicated Xu's recommender, Wang Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Furious that Zhang Xu, magistrate of Bazhou, had disciplined the horse grooms and camp followers, he had Zhang arrested and implicated Xu's patron Wang Duo as well.

sentences.zh: 又械戶部尚書劉中敷，侍郎吳璽、陳常於長安門。

translations.literal: He also had Minister of Revenue Liu Zhongfu and the vice ministers Wu Xi and Chen Chang bound in shackles at Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the minister of revenue Liu Zhongfu and the vice ministers Wu Xi and Chen Chang shackled at Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 所忤恨，輒加罪謫。

translations.literal: Anyone who offended or enraged him was at once punished and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever crossed or angered him was promptly punished and banished.

sentences.zh: 內侍張環、顧忠、錦衣衛卒王永心不平，以匿名書暴振罪狀。

translations.literal: The inner attendants Zhang Huan and Gu Zhong and the Brocade Guard soldier Wang Yong, unable to bear it, exposed Zhen's crimes in an anonymous letter.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants Zhang Huan and Gu Zhong and the Brocade Guard soldier Wang Yong, unable to endure it, denounced Zhen's crimes in an anonymous letter.

sentences.zh: 事發，磔於市，不覆奏。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, they were torn to death in the market, without further report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered they were torn to pieces in the marketplace without even a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝方傾心向振，嘗以先生呼之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then wholly devoted to Zhen and had once addressed him as Sir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was wholly in Zhen's thrall and had even addressed him as "Sir."

sentences.zh: 賜振敕，極褒美。

translations.literal: He bestowed an imperial rescript on Zhen with extravagant praise.
translations.idiomatic: He issued him an imperial letter of lavish praise.

sentences.zh: 振權日益積重，公侯勛戚呼曰翁父。

translations.literal: Zhen's power grew heavier by the day, and dukes, marquises, and meritorious kin all called him Father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's power mounted day by day; dukes, marquises, and meritorious kinfolk all called him "Father-in-law."

sentences.zh: 畏禍者爭附振免死，賕賂輳集。

translations.literal: Those who feared calamity rushed to attach themselves to Zhen to escape death, and bribes poured in from every side.
translations.idiomatic: Men who feared ruin flocked to his patronage to save their lives, and bribes piled up on every hand.

sentences.zh: 工部郎中王祐以善諂擢本部侍郎，兵部尚書徐晞等多至屈膝。

translations.literal: Wang You, a clerk in the Ministry of Works, was promoted to vice minister by dint of flattery, and Minister of War Xu Xi and the others often went so far as to kneel before him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You, a director in the Ministry of Works, was raised to vice minister through flattery; the minister of war Xu Xi and others often knelt before Zhen.

sentences.zh: 其從子山、林至蔭都督指揮。

translations.literal: His nephews Shan and Lin were granted offices as Guard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Shan and Lin were ennobled as regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 私黨馬順、郭敬、陳官、唐童等並肆行無忌。

translations.literal: His private allies, Ma Shun, Guo Jing, Chen Guan, Tang Tong, and others, all ran wild without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His creatures Ma Shun, Guo Jing, Chen Guan, Tang Tong, and the rest acted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 久之，構釁瓦剌，振遂敗。

translations.literal: After a long time he provoked the Oirats, and Zhen was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In time he provoked the Oirats, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌者，元裔也。

translations.literal: The Oirats were descendants of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirats were descendants of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，其太師也先貢馬，振減其直，使者恚而去。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, their taishi Esen presented horses; Zhen reduced their price, and the envoy left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year their taishi Esen presented tribute horses; Zhen cut the price offered, and the envoy departed in a rage.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，也先大舉入寇，振挾帝親征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Esen launched a major invasion, and Zhen took the emperor on a personal expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Esen invaded in force, and Zhen persuaded the emperor to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 廷臣交諫，弗聽。

translations.literal: The court ministers repeatedly remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers remonstrated again and again, but he would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 至宣府，大風雨，復有諫者，振益虓怒。

translations.literal: When they reached Xuanfu, fierce winds and rain arose, and when more people remonstrated, Zhen became even more savage and furious.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanfu violent wind and rain struck; when others urged retreat, Zhen flew into still greater rage.

sentences.zh: 成國公朱勇等白事，咸膝行進。

translations.literal: When Duke Chengguo Zhu Yong and the others came to report business, they all advanced on their knees.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Chengguo, Zhu Yong, and the others came to report, they all crawled forward on their knees.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄺埜、王佐忤振意，罰跪草中。

translations.literal: Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo offended Zhen's wishes and were punished by kneeling in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo crossed Zhen's will and were forced to kneel in the grass as punishment.

sentences.zh: 其黨欽天監正彭德清以天象諫，振終弗從。

translations.literal: His ally Peng Deqing, Director of the Astronomical Bureau, remonstrated with him on the basis of the celestial omens, but Zhen still would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Even Peng Deqing, director of the Astronomical Bureau and one of his own party, warned him by the heavenly signs, but Zhen would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 八月己酉，帝駐大同，振益欲北。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the eighth month, the emperor was camped at Datong, and Zhen was determined even more to press north.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the eighth month the emperor encamped at Datong, and Zhen was all the more bent on pushing north.

sentences.zh: 鎮守太監郭敬以敵勢告，振始懼。

translations.literal: The eunuch in charge of garrison affairs, Guo Jing, reported the strength of the enemy, and Zhen finally became afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Guo Jing reported the enemy's strength, and at last Zhen took fright.

sentences.zh: 班師，至雙寨，雨甚。

translations.literal: When the army began its return march, it reached Shuangzhai in heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: The army turned back and, in pouring rain, reached Shuangzhai.

sentences.zh: 振初議道紫荊關，由蔚州邀帝幸其第，既恐蹂鄉稼，復改道宣府。

translations.literal: At first Zhen planned to take the Zijing Pass route and bring the emperor by way of Wei Prefecture to visit his own residence, but fearing that this would trample the villages' crops, he again changed course to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had first intended to march the army through Zijing Pass and bring the emperor by way of his home district of Weizhou so as to visit his mansion, but fearing the troops would trample the crops of his native place, he changed the route back toward Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 軍士紆回奔走，壬戌始次土木。

translations.literal: The soldiers had to take long detours and hurry about, and only on the renxu day did they reach Tumubao.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were forced into long detours and frantic marching, and only on the renxu day did they reach Tumubao.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌兵追至，師大潰。

translations.literal: The Oirat troops pursued them there, and the army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirat cavalry overtook them there, and the army collapsed in total rout.

sentences.zh: 帝蒙塵，振乃為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: The emperor was taken captive, and Zhen was then killed by the rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was captured; Zhen himself was killed by the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 敗報聞，百官慟哭，都御史陳鎰等廷奏振罪，給事中王竑等立擊殺馬順及毛、王二中官。

translations.literal: When the news of the defeat arrived, all the officials wailed aloud; the Grand Censor Chen Yi and others presented Zhen's crimes at court, and the supervising secretaries Wang Hong and others immediately struck down and killed Ma Shun and the two eunuchs Mao and Wang.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the disaster reached the capital the officials broke into loud lamentation; the censor-in-chief Chen Yi and others memorialized listing Zhen's crimes, and the supervising secretaries Wang Hong and others at once fell upon and killed Ma Shun and the two eunuchs Mao and Wang.

sentences.zh: 郕王命臠王山於市，並振黨誅之，振族無少長皆斬。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cheng ordered Wang Shan to be quartered in the market and had Zhen's party executed; all of Zhen's clan, young and old, were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cheng ordered Wang Shan torn to pieces in the marketplace and put Zhen's faction to death; every member of Zhen's clan, young and old alike, was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 振擅權七年，籍其家，得金銀六十餘庫，玉盤百，珊瑚高六七尺者二十餘株，他珍玩無算。

translations.literal: Zhen monopolized power for seven years; when his household was confiscated, they found more than sixty vaults of gold and silver, a hundred jade dishes, more than twenty corals six or seven chi high, and countless other rare treasures and curios.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had monopolized power for seven years; when his property was seized there were more than sixty vaults of gold and silver, a hundred jade platters, more than twenty coral trees six or seven feet high, and treasures beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 先是，郭敬鎮大同，幾造箭鏃數十甕，以振命遺瓦剌，瓦剌輒報以良馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guo Jing was stationed at Datong, he had made nearly several dozen urns of arrowheads and sent them to the Oirats on Zhen's orders, and the Oirats always replied with fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Guo Jing was garrisoning Datong, he had cast several dozen urns of arrowheads and, on Zhen's orders, sent them to the Oirats, who in return regularly sent fine horses.

sentences.zh: 及帝親征，西寧侯宋瑛、駙馬都尉井源為前鋒，遇敵陽和，敬又撓使敗。

translations.literal: When the emperor led the campaign himself, the Marquis of Xining, Song Ying, and the imperial son-in-law Jing Yuan served as the vanguard; when they met the enemy at Yanghe, Guo Jing again thwarted them and caused their defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor led the campaign in person, the Marquis of Xining Song Ying and the imperial son-in-law Jing Yuan served as vanguard; at Yanghe they met the enemy, and Guo Jing again sabotaged them and brought on defeat.

sentences.zh: 至是逃歸，亦坐誅。

translations.literal: When he fled back this time, he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When he fled back on this occasion, he too was put to death.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，顧念振不置。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was restored, he still remembered Zhen and could not let him go.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong was restored he still could not put Wang Zhen out of mind.

sentences.zh: 用太監劉恒言，賜振祭，招魂以葬，祀之智化寺，賜祠曰精忠。

translations.literal: Using the eunuch Liu Heng's suggestion, he granted Zhen sacrificial offerings, summoned his soul for burial, honored him at Zhihua Temple, and bestowed on the shrine the title Perfect Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: On the eunuch Liu Heng's advice he granted Zhen sacrificial rites, summoned his soul for burial, and established a shrine at Zhihua Temple with the plaque "Perfect Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而振門下曹吉祥復以奪門功，有寵顓政。

translations.literal: Meanwhile, Zhen's retainer Cao Jixiang, having won favor through the seizure of the gates, also monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Zhen's follower Cao Jixiang, having won favor in the seizure of the gates, likewise dominated the government.

sentences.zh: 曹吉祥

translations.literal: Cao Jixiang
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jixiang

sentences.zh: 曹吉祥，灤州人。

translations.literal: Cao Jixiang was a man of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jixiang came from Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 素依王振。

translations.literal: He had long relied on Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been dependent on Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 正統初，征麓川，為監軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengtong, when the campaign against Luchuan was launched, he served as supervising officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengtong, in the Luchuan campaign, he served as supervising eunuch.

sentences.zh: 征兀良哈，與成國公朱勇、太監劉永誠分道。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Wuliangha, he took a separate route with Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and the eunuch Liu Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the Uriyangqai he marched by a separate route with the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and the eunuch Liu Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 又與寧陽侯陳懋等征鄧茂七於福建，吉祥每出，輒選達官、跳蕩卒隸帳下，師還畜於家，故家多藏甲。

translations.literal: He also campaigned with the Marquis of Ningyang, Chen Mao, against Deng Maoqi in Fujian; whenever Jixiang went out, he would pick able officers and assault troops to attach to his tent, and when the army returned he kept them at home, so his household contained many hidden weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned with the Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao against Deng Maoqi in Fujian; whenever Jixiang went on campaign he chose able officers and assault troops for his retinue, and after the army returned he kept them at home—so his household hoarded many weapons in secret.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，分掌京營。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign, he was put in joint charge of the capital garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingtai reign he shared command of the capital garrisons.

sentences.zh: 後與石亨結，帥兵迎英宗復位。

translations.literal: Later he allied with Shi Heng and led troops to bring the Yingzong Emperor back to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Later he allied with Shi Heng and led troops to welcome Yingzong back to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷司禮太監，總督三大營。

translations.literal: He was promoted to eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service and put in overall command of the Three Great Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to eunuch director of the Directorate of Ceremonial and given overall command of the Three Great Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 嗣子欽，從子鉉、鐸等皆官都督，欽進封昭武伯，門下廝養冒官者多至千百人，朝士亦有依附希進者，權勢與石亨埒，時並稱曹、石。

translations.literal: His adopted son Qin and his nephews Xuan and Quan were all made guard commanders; Qin was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaowu, and his household retainers who had assumed official rank numbered in the hundreds and thousands. Some court officials also attached themselves to him in hopes of advancement, and his power and influence matched Shi Heng's, so they were known together as Cao and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Qin and his nephews Xuan and Duo were all made regional commanders; Qin was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaowu. Household retainers who had bought office numbered in the thousands, and some court officials attached themselves in hope of advancement. His power rivaled Shi Heng's, and the two were known together as Cao and Shi.

sentences.zh: 二人惡言官有言，共譖於帝，命吏部尚書王翺察核年三十五以上者留，不及者調用。

translations.literal: The two disliked officials speaking out, and together slandered them before the emperor. The emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Wang Ao to investigate and verify those aged thirty-five and above, who were to remain, while those below that age were to be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: The two hated remonstrating officials; together they slandered them to the emperor, who ordered the minister of personnel Wang Ao to investigate: those thirty-five and older were to remain, the rest reassigned.

sentences.zh: 於是給事何玘等十三人改州判官，御史吳禎等二十三人改知縣。

translations.literal: As a result, thirteen men including the assistant secretary He Qi were transferred to posts as prefectural vice-magistrates, and twenty-three censors including Wu Zhen were transferred to serve as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen supervising secretaries including He Qi were demoted to prefectural vice-magistrates, and twenty-three censors including Wu Zhen to county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 會有風雷雨雹之變，帝乃悟，悉還其職。

translations.literal: Then a change of wind, thunder, rain, and hail occurred, and the emperor awakened to the situation and restored all of them to office.
translations.idiomatic: Then wind, thunder, rain, and hail struck; the emperor came to his senses and restored them all to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，二人爭寵有隙，御史楊瑄、張鵬劾之，吉祥乃復與亨合，乘間醞帝。

translations.literal: Not long after, the two fell out over competition for favor; the censors Yang Xuan and Zhang Peng impeached them, and Jixiang once again allied with Heng and took advantage of the opening to make the emperor intoxicated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two quarreled over favor; censors Yang Xuan and Zhang Peng impeached them. Jixiang again joined Heng and, seizing their chance, got the emperor drunk.

sentences.zh: 帝為下瑄等詔獄，而逮治閣臣徐有貞、李賢等。

translations.literal: The emperor had Xuan and the others sent to the imperial prison, and also had the Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Youzhen, Li Xian, and others taken into custody and investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Xuan and the others thrown into prison and also arrested the grand secretaries Xu Youzhen and Li Xian for investigation.

sentences.zh: 事具賢傳。

translations.literal: The details are given in Li Xian's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in Li Xian's biography.

sentences.zh: 承天門災，帝命閣臣嶽正草罪己詔，詔語激切。

translations.literal: When the fire at Cheng Tian Gate broke out, the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Yue Zheng to draft an edict of self-reproach, and the language of the edict was intense and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out at Chengtian Gate the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Yue Zheng to draft a self-reproach edict; the language was severe.

sentences.zh: 吉祥、亨復正謗訕，帝又謫正。

translations.literal: Jixiang and Heng again had Zheng slander and vilify others, and the emperor again demoted Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang and Heng again slandered Zheng, and the emperor demoted him once more.

sentences.zh: 焰益張，朝野仄目。

translations.literal: Their flames grew ever fiercer, and both court and country looked on in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Their arrogance blazed higher; court and country watched in dread.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝覺其奸，意稍稍疑。

translations.literal: After a long while, the emperor perceived their treachery and began to suspect them.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor perceived their treachery and began to doubt them.

sentences.zh: 及李賢力言奪門非是，始大悟，疏吉祥。

translations.literal: When Li Xian strongly argued that the gate seizure was wrong, he finally awakened fully and distanced himself from Jixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian argued forcefully that seizing the gates had been wrong, the emperor at last saw clearly and kept his distance from Jixiang.

sentences.zh: 無何，石亨敗，吉祥不自安，漸蓄異謀，日犒諸達官，金錢、穀帛恣所取。

translations.literal: Not long after, Shi Heng was defeated, and Jixiang, no longer at ease, gradually harbored rebel schemes; each day he rewarded the various inner officers, letting them take gold, money, grain, and silk as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Shi Heng fell, Jixiang grew uneasy and slowly hatched a rebellion; each day he feasted the inner officers, letting them take gold, cash, grain, and silk at will.

sentences.zh: 諸達官恐吉祥敗而己隨黜退也，皆願盡力效死。

translations.literal: The various inner officers feared that if Jixiang failed, they too would be dismissed and demoted, and so all were willing to do their utmost and die for him.
