translations.idiomatic: The officers feared that if Jixiang fell they would be dismissed too, and all were willing to fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 欽問客馮益曰：「自古有宦官子弟為天子者乎？」

translations.literal: Qin asked the guest Feng Yi: "From antiquity, has there been a son of a eunuch who became emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Qin asked his guest Feng Yi: "Since antiquity, has a eunuch's son ever become emperor?

sentences.zh: 益曰：「君家魏武，其人也。」

translations.literal: Yi replied: "Your house's Wei Wu is that man."
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied: "Your house has Wei Wu—that is your precedent."

sentences.zh: 欽大喜。

translations.literal: Qin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 天順五年七月，欽私掠家人曹福來，為言官所劾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Tianshun, Qin privately seized the household servant Cao Fulai, and was impeached by the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Tianshun, Qin privately seized the household servant Cao Fulai and was impeached by the remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 帝令錦衣指揮逮杲按之，降敕遍諭群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a Brocade Guard commander to seize Gao and investigate the matter, and issued an edict that was circulated to all the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Brocade Guard commander Gao to arrest and investigate, and circulated an edict to the whole court.

sentences.zh: 欽驚曰：「前降敕，遂捕石將軍。

translations.literal: Qin was alarmed and said: "With the last edict, they went and arrested General Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was alarmed: "The last time an edict went out, they arrested General Shi.

sentences.zh: 今復爾，殆矣。」

translations.literal: If this happens again now, we are finished.
translations.idiomatic: If it happens again now, we are finished.

sentences.zh: 謀遂決。

translations.literal: The plan was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The conspiracy was then fixed.

sentences.zh: 是時甘、涼告警，帝命懷寧侯孫鏜西征，未發。

translations.literal: At that time Gansu and Liangzhou sent alarm reports, and the emperor ordered Marquis of Huaining Sun Tang to campaign west, but he had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gansu and Liangzhou sent alarms; the emperor ordered the Marquis of Huaining Sun Tang to campaign west, but he had not yet marched.

sentences.zh: 吉祥使其黨掌欽天監太常少卿湯序擇是月庚子昧爽，欽擁兵入，而已以禁軍應之。

translations.literal: Jixiang had his ally, the Vice Minister of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau and Directorate of Sacrifices, Tang Xu, choose the pre-dawn of the gengzi day of that month; Qin would enter with his troops, and he himself would answer with the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang had his ally Tang Xu of the Astronomical Bureau choose the pre-dawn of the gengzi day of that month: Qin would enter with troops while he himself would answer with the forbidden army.

sentences.zh: 謀定，欽召諸達官夜飲。

translations.literal: Once the plan was set, Qin summoned the various inner officers for a night of drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plan was set, Qin summoned the officers for a night of drinking.

sentences.zh: 是夜，鏜及恭順侯吳瑾俱宿朝房。

translations.literal: That night, Tang and the Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Jin, both stayed in the court lodging.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tang and the Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jin both lodged in the court chambers.

sentences.zh: 達官馬亮恐事敗，逸出，走告瑾。

translations.literal: The inner officer Ma Liang feared the plot would fail, escaped, and ran to tell Wu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The officer Ma Liang, fearing failure, slipped out and ran to tell Wu Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾趣鏜由長安右門隙投疏入。

translations.literal: Wu Jin urged Tang to send a memorial through the gap at the right gate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jin urged Tang to slip a memorial through the gap at the right Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝急縶吉祥於內，而敕皇城及京城九門閉弗啟。

translations.literal: The emperor quickly had Jixiang bound inside, and ordered the imperial city and all nine gates of the capital closed and not opened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly had Jixiang seized inside the palace and ordered the imperial city and all nine gates of the capital shut.

sentences.zh: 欽知亮逸，中夜馳往逮杲家，殺杲，斫傷李賢於東朝房。

translations.literal: When Qin learned that Liang had escaped, he rode out in the middle of the night to Gao's house, killed Gao, and wounded Li Xian at the eastern court chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liang had escaped, Qin rode out at midnight to Gao's house, killed Gao, and wounded Li Xian in the eastern court chamber.

sentences.zh: 以杲頭示賢曰：「杲激我也。」

translations.literal: Holding Gao's head up to Li Xian, he said: "Gao provoked me.
translations.idiomatic: Holding up Gao's head to Li Xian he said: "Gao provoked me.

sentences.zh: 又殺都御史寇深於西朝房。

translations.literal: Then he also killed Grand Censor Kou Shen in the western court chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed the censor-in-chief Kou Shen in the western court chamber.

sentences.zh: 攻東、西長安門不得入，縱火。

translations.literal: He attacked the east and west Chang'an Gates but could not break in, so he set them on fire.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted the east and west Chang'an Gates but could not break through and set them afire.

sentences.zh: 守衛者拆河壖磚石塞諸門。

translations.literal: The guards tore up bricks and stones from the riverbank and blocked the gates with them.
translations.idiomatic: The guards tore up bricks from the river embankment and blocked the gates.

sentences.zh: 賊往來叫呼門外。

translations.literal: The rebels ran back and forth shouting outside the gates.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels ran back and forth shouting outside the gates.

sentences.zh: 鏜遣二子急召西征軍擊欽於東長安門。

translations.literal: Tang sent his two sons to urgently summon the western expedition army to strike Qin at the east Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang sent his two sons in haste to summon the western expedition force to strike Qin at the east Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 欽走攻東安門，道殺瑾。

translations.literal: Qin ran to attack the east An Gate, and on the way killed Wu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin turned to attack the east An Gate and killed Wu Jin on the way.

sentences.zh: 復縱火，門毀。

translations.literal: He again set fires, and the gate was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He set fires again and burned the gate down.

sentences.zh: 門內聚薪益之，火熾，賊不得入。

translations.literal: Within the gate, they piled firewood and added to it; the flames roared, and the rebels could not get in.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate they heaped more fuel; the flames roared and the rebels could not enter.

sentences.zh: 天漸曙，欽黨稍稍散去。

translations.literal: As dawn gradually approached, Qin's followers began to disperse little by little.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn approached Qin's followers began to scatter.

sentences.zh: 鏜勒兵逐欽，斬鉉、鐸，鏜子軏斫欽中膊。

translations.literal: Tang led troops in pursuit of Qin, had Xuan and Quan beheaded, and Tang's son Yue hacked Qin in the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Tang led troops in pursuit, beheaded Xuan and Duo, and Tang's son Yue hacked Qin in the shoulder.

sentences.zh: 欽走突安定諸門，門盡閉。

translations.literal: Qin fled to break through the gates of Anying and others, but all the gates were shut.
translations.idiomatic: Qin fled, trying gate after gate in the Anding quarter, but all were shut.

sentences.zh: 奔歸家，拒戰。

translations.literal: He ran back home and put up a fight.
translations.idiomatic: He ran home and made a last stand.

sentences.zh: 會大雨如註，鏜督諸軍大呼入，欽投井死。

translations.literal: Then a heavy rain fell in sheets; Tang directed the various armies to shout and charge in, and Qin threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then rain poured down in sheets; Tang directed the armies to charge in with a great shout, and Qin threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 遂殺鐸，盡屠其家。

translations.literal: They then killed Duo and massacred his whole family.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed Duo and slaughtered his entire family.

sentences.zh: 越三日，磔吉祥於市。

translations.literal: Three days later, they tore Jixiang to pieces in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Jixiang was torn to pieces in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 湯序、馮益及吉祥姻黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Tang Xu, Feng Yi, and all Jixiang's in-laws and party were likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xu, Feng Yi, and all Jixiang's kin and party were executed.

sentences.zh: 馬亮以告反者，授都督。

translations.literal: Ma Liang, because he had reported the rebellion, was appointed a Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang, for reporting the plot, was made a regional commander.

sentences.zh: 英宗始任王振，繼任吉祥，凡兩致禍亂。

translations.literal: Yingzong first relied on Wang Zhen and then on Jixiang, and the two together brought about disaster and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong first entrusted himself to Wang Zhen and then to Jixiang; the two together brought catastrophe on the state.

sentences.zh: 其他宦者若跛兒幹、亦失哈、喜寧、韋力轉、牛玉之屬，率凶狡。

translations.literal: Other eunuchs, such as Boer Gan, Yishihha, Xi Ning, Weilizhuan, and Niu Yu, were generally vicious and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Other eunuchs such as Bo'er Gan, Yishihha, Xi Ning, Wei Lizhuan, and Niu Yu were for the most part vicious and cunning.

sentences.zh: 土木之敗，跛兒幹、喜寧皆降敵。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Tumu, Boer Gan and Xi Ning both surrendered to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tumu disaster Bo'er Gan and Xi Ning both surrendered to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 跛兒幹助敵反攻，射內使黎定。

translations.literal: Boer Gan helped the enemy counterattack and shot the inner attendant Li Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'er Gan helped the enemy counterattack and shot the inner attendant Li Ding.

sentences.zh: 既又為敵使至京，有所需索，景帝執而誅之。

translations.literal: Later he also served as an envoy of the enemy to the capital, demanding things; the Jingtai Emperor seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came to the capital as the enemy's envoy to demand goods; the Jingtai emperor seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 喜寧數為也先畫策，索賞賜，導入邊寇掠。

translations.literal: Xi Ning repeatedly plotted for Esen, demanded rewards, and led border troops to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ning repeatedly plotted strategy for Esen, demanded rewards, and guided border raiders in their plunder.

sentences.zh: 上皇患之，言於也先；

translations.literal: The retired emperor was troubled by him and spoke of it to Esen;
translations.idiomatic: The captive emperor was troubled by him and spoke of it to Esen;

sentences.zh: 使寧還京索禮物，而命校尉袁彬以密書報邊臣。

translations.literal: he was sent back to the capital to demand gifts, and the sergeant Yuan Bin was ordered to send a secret letter to the border commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was sent back to the capital to demand gifts, while the corporal Yuan Bin was ordered to send a secret letter to the border commanders.

sentences.zh: 至獨石，參將楊俊擒寧送京師，景泰元年二月磔於市。

translations.literal: When he reached Dushi, the Assistant Commander Yang Jun captured Ning and sent him to the capital, where he was torn to pieces in the market in the second month of the first year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: At Dushi the assistant commander Yang Jun captured Ning and sent him to the capital; in the second month of the first year of Jingtai he was torn to pieces in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 亦失哈鎮遼東。

translations.literal: Yishihha was stationed in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Yishihha was garrisoning Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 敵犯廣寧，亦失哈禁官軍勿出擊。

translations.literal: When the enemy attacked Guangning, Yishihha forbade the imperial troops from going out to strike back.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked Guangning, Yishihha forbade the troops to sally out.

sentences.zh: 百戶施帶兒降敵，為脫脫不花通於亦失哈。

translations.literal: The hundred-household officer Shi Daier surrendered to the enemy and became the go-between for Tuo Tuo Bu Hua and Yishihha.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred-household officer Shi Daier surrendered to the enemy and acted as go-between for Toto Bukha and Yishihha.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年冬，帶兒逃歸，巡按御史劉孜並劾亦失哈及他不法事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, Daier fled back, and the surveillance censor Liu Zi impeached Yishihha and the other unlawful matters together.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong Daier fled back, and the touring censor Liu Zi impeached Yishihha together with his other crimes.

sentences.zh: 景帝命誅帶兒，而置亦失哈不問。

translations.literal: The Jingtai Emperor ordered Daier executed, but left Yishihha uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingtai emperor ordered Daier executed but took no action against Yishihha.

sentences.zh: 韋力轉者，性淫毒，鎮守大同，多過惡。

translations.literal: Wei Lizhuan was licentious and vicious; when he was in charge at Datong, he committed many outrageous crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lizhuan was lecherous and cruel; as garrison commander at Datong he committed many outrages.

sentences.zh: 銜軍妻不與宿，杖死其軍。

translations.literal: He coveted a soldier's wife; when she would not sleep with him, he had the soldier beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He coveted a soldier's wife; when she would not sleep with him, he had the soldier beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 又與養子妻淫戲，射殺養子。

translations.literal: He also committed adultery and playing around with the wife of an adopted son and shot the adopted son dead.
translations.idiomatic: He also debauched his adopted son's wife and shot the adopted son dead.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，工部侍郎霍瑄發力轉僭用金器若王者，及強娶所部女為妾諸不法事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun, the Ministry of Works vice minister Huo Xuan exposed Wei Lizhuan's unlawful acts, including using gold vessels like a king and forcibly taking women from the units under his command as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun the vice minister of works Huo Xuan exposed Lizhuan's crimes: using gold vessels like a king, forcibly taking women under his command as concubines, and other illegal acts.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，執之下錦衣衛獄，既而宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, had him arrested and sent to the Brocade Guard prison, then later pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had him arrested and sent to the Brocade Guard prison, then later pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 牛玉事，詳《吳廢後傳》。

translations.literal: The matter of Niu Yu is detailed in the Biography of Wu's Deposed Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The affair of Niu Yu is related in full in the Biography of the Deposed Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 劉永誠

translations.literal: Liu Yongcheng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongcheng

sentences.zh: 其與吉祥分道征兀良哈者劉永誠，永樂時，嘗為偏將，累從北征。

translations.literal: Liu Yongcheng, who took a separate route with Jixiang to campaign against Wuliangha, had once served as a deputy general in the Yongle reign and had often accompanied the northern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongcheng, who went by a separate route with Jixiang against Wuliangha, had served as a deputy general in the Yongle reign and repeatedly joined northern expeditions.

sentences.zh: 宣德、正統中，再擊兀良哈。

translations.literal: During Xuande and Zhengtong he again fought Wuliangha.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns he campaigned twice against the Uriyangqai.

sentences.zh: 後監鎮甘、涼，戰沙漠，有功。

translations.literal: Later he supervised and garrisoned Gansu and Liangzhou, where he fought in the desert and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he supervised the garrisons of Gansu and Liangzhou, fought in the desert, and won merit.

sentences.zh: 景泰末，掌團營。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingtai he was put in charge of the group armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jingtai he took charge of the regiment armies.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，勒兵從，官其嗣子聚。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was restored, he led troops in attendance, and his adopted son Ju was made an official.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored he led troops in support, and his adopted son Ju was granted office.

sentences.zh: 成化中，永誠始卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Chenghua reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng died in the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 懷恩，高密人，兵部侍郎戴綸族弟也。

translations.literal: Huai'en. Huai'en was a man of Gaomi and a clan younger brother of Dai Lun, vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was a native of Gaomi and a clansman of Dai Lun, vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 宣宗殺綸，並籍恩父太僕卿希文家。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong killed Lun, he also confiscated the family of Huai'en's father Xiwen, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sheds.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong executed Lun he also confiscated the property of Huai'en's father Xiwen, minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 恩方幼，被宮為小黃門，賜名懷恩。

translations.literal: Huai'en was still young, and was taken into the palace as a small yellow gate attendant and given the name Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was still a child; he was taken into the palace as a junior eunuch and given the name Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 憲宗朝，掌司禮監。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign he was in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua reign he headed the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 時汪直理西廠，梁芳、韋興等用事。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhi was managing the Western Depot, while Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and others were in power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Zhi ran the Western Depot while Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and others held power.

sentences.zh: 恩班在前，性忠鯁無所撓，諸閹咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: Huai'en held the lead rank, was loyal and outspoken without any bending, and all the eunuchs respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en held senior rank, was loyal and unbending, and all the eunuchs respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 員外郎林俊論芳及僧繼曉下獄，帝欲誅之，恩固爭。

translations.literal: When Assistant Minister Lin Jun impeached Fang and the monk Jixiao and was thrown into prison, the emperor wanted to execute him, but Huai'en strongly argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: When the assistant minister Lin Jun impeached Fang and the monk Jixiao and was thrown into prison, the emperor wished to execute him, but Huai'en argued stubbornly against it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，投以硯曰：「若助俊訕我。」

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and threw an inkstone at him, saying: "You are helping Jun slander me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and hurled an inkstone at him: "You help Jun slander me!

sentences.zh: 恩免冠伏地號哭。

translations.literal: Huai'en removed his cap, prostrated himself on the ground, and cried aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en removed his cap, prostrated himself, and wailed aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝叱之出。

translations.literal: The emperor shouted at him to get out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shouted at him to leave.

sentences.zh: 恩遣人告鎮撫司曰：「汝曹諂芳傾俊。

translations.literal: Huai'en sent someone to tell the Commandery of Suppression: "You flatter Fang and bring Jun down.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en sent word to the prison directorate: "You fawn on Fang and destroy Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊死，汝曹何以生！」

translations.literal: If Jun dies, how can you live?
translations.idiomatic: If Jun dies, how will you answer for it!

sentences.zh: 徑歸，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: He went straight home and claimed illness, refusing to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight home and refused to rise, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 帝怒解，遣醫視恩，卒釋俊。

translations.literal: When the emperor's anger subsided, he sent a physician to examine Huai'en and ultimately released Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's anger cooled, he sent a physician to see Huai'en and at last released Jun.

sentences.zh: 會星變，罷諸傳奉官。

translations.literal: Then an astronomical anomaly occurred, and all the transmission-offering officials were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Then a celestial anomaly occurred, and all the chuanfeng appointees were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 御馬監王敏請留馬房傳奉者，帝許之。

translations.literal: The imperial stable supervisor Wang Min requested that the transmission-offering men at the horse stables be retained, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Min, supervisor of the Imperial Horse Directorate, asked that the chuanfeng staff in the stables be kept on; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 敏謁恩，恩大罵曰：「星變，專為我曹壞國政故。

translations.literal: When Min paid his respects to Huai'en, Huai'en cursed him savagely, saying: "The celestial anomaly happened because of us, to ruin the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Min came to pay his respects, Huai'en cursed him savagely: "The heavens sent this omen because of us—to ruin the government!

sentences.zh: 今甫欲正之，又為汝壞，天雷擊汝矣！」

translations.literal: Now that we have only just tried to set things right, you have ruined them again; thunder from heaven will strike you!
translations.idiomatic: Just as we tried to set things right, you have spoiled it again. Heaven's thunder will strike you down!

sentences.zh: 敏愧恨，遂死。

translations.literal: Min was ashamed and resentful, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with shame and hatred, Min died not long after.

sentences.zh: 進寶石者章瑾求為錦衣衛鎮撫，恩不可，曰：「鎮撫掌詔獄，奈何以賄進。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Jin brought a precious stone and asked to become a Brocade Guard prison commander, Huai'en refused, saying: "A prison commander handles imperial prisons; how can he be advanced by bribery?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, who had gained favor by presenting a precious stone, asked to be made prison commander of the Brocade Guard; Huai'en refused: "That office oversees the imperial prisons—how can one buy one's way into it with a bribe?

sentences.zh: 當是時，尚書王恕以直諫名，恩每嘆曰：「天下忠義，斯人而已。」

translations.literal: At that time Minister Wang Shu was known for blunt remonstrance, and Huai'en often sighed: "Among the loyal and righteous under heaven, this man alone remains."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister Wang Shu was famed for blunt remonstrance; Huai'en would often sigh: "Of all the loyal and upright men under heaven, this man alone remains."

sentences.zh: 憲宗末，惑萬貴妃言，欲易太子，恩固爭。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chenghua reign, when the emperor was misled by Empress Wan's words and wanted to change the crown prince, Huai'en strongly argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Chenghua reign the emperor, misled by Empress Wan, wished to replace the crown prince; Huai'en argued against it fiercely.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，斥居鳳陽。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and banished him to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense and banished him to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，召歸，仍掌司禮監，力勸帝逐萬安，用王恕。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor ascended the throne, he recalled him and again put him in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, where he strongly urged the emperor to expel Wan An and use Wang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne he recalled Huai'en and again placed him in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial, where he strongly urged the emperor to remove Wan An and employ Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 一時正人匯進，恩之力也。

translations.literal: The gathering of upright men at that time was due to Huai'en's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: The gathering of upright ministers at court in those days was largely Huai'en's doing.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祠額曰顯忠。

translations.literal: When he died, the shrine was granted the plaque Distinguished Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court granted his shrine the plaque "Manifest Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 同時有覃吉者，不知所由進，以老閹侍太子。

translations.literal: There was also a man named Qin Ji, and no one knew how he had risen, but as an old eunuch he served the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was Qin Ji; no one knew how he had risen, but as an aged eunuch he served the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子年九歲，吉口授《四書》章句及古今政典。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was nine years old, Ji orally taught him the chapters and verses of the Four Books and the political canons of ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was nine, Ji taught him orally the chapters of the Four Books and the political precedents of past and present.

sentences.zh: 憲宗賜太子莊田，吉勸毋受，曰：「天下皆太子有也。」

translations.literal: When the Chenghua Emperor granted the crown prince estates, Ji urged him not to accept them, saying: "The whole realm already belongs to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghua granted the crown prince estates, Ji urged him to refuse: "The whole realm will one day be yours.

sentences.zh: 太子偶從內侍讀佛經，吉入，太子驚曰：「老伴來矣。」

translations.literal: One day the crown prince was listening to a Buddhist sutra with an inner attendant when Ji entered; the crown prince, startled, said: "My old companion has come."
translations.idiomatic: Once the crown prince was reading a Buddhist sutra with an inner attendant when Ji entered; startled, the prince cried, "The old fellow is here!"

sentences.zh: 亟手《孝經》。

translations.literal: He hurriedly picked up the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: He hastily snatched up the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 吉跪曰：「太子誦佛書乎？」

translations.literal: Ji knelt and said: "Is the crown prince reciting a Buddhist text?
translations.idiomatic: Ji knelt and asked: "Is the crown prince reciting Buddhist scripture?

sentences.zh: 曰：「無有。

translations.literal: The crown prince replied: "No.
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied: "No—

sentences.zh: 《孝經》耳。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety only.
translations.idiomatic: only the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 吉頓首曰：「甚善。

translations.literal: Ji bowed his head and said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji bowed his head to the ground: "Excellent.

sentences.zh: 佛書誕，不可信也。」

translations.literal: Buddhist texts are absurd and not to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist writings are fantastic nonsense—not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 弘治之世，政治醇美，君德清明，端本正始，吉有力焉。

translations.literal: In the reign of Hongzhi, the government was pure and excellent, the ruler's virtue was clear, the root was set right, and the beginning was made correct; Ji contributed greatly to that.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi reign government grew pure, the ruler's virtue clear, and the dynasty's foundations were set straight from the start; Ji had no small part in this.

sentences.zh: 汪直者，大藤峽瑤種也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was a Yao of Dazuo Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was of Yao stock from Dazuo Gorge.

sentences.zh: 初給事萬貴妃於昭德宮，遷御馬監太監。

translations.literal: At first he attended Empress Wan in Zhaode Palace, then was promoted to eunuch of the Imperial Horse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He first attended Empress Wan in Zhaode Palace, then rose to eunuch of the Imperial Horse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年，黑眚見宮中，妖人李子龍以符術結太監韋舍私入大內，事發，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua, a dark pestilence appeared in the palace; the sorcerer Li Zilong used talismans to befriend the eunuch Wei She and secretly enter the inner palace, but when the matter was exposed, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua twelve a dark pestilence appeared in the palace; the sorcerer Li Zilong won over the eunuch Wei She with talisman arts and secretly entered the inner quarters. When the plot was exposed he was executed.

sentences.zh: 帝心惡之，銳欲知外事。

translations.literal: The emperor came to dislike it and grew eager to know what was happening outside.
translations.idiomatic: The affair disgusted the emperor, who grew keen to know what was happening beyond the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 直為人便黠，帝因令易服，將校尉一二人密出伺察，人莫知也，獨都御史王越與結歡。

translations.literal: Zhi was quick and cunning; the emperor therefore had him change clothes and, with one or two guard officers, secretly go out to observe and investigate, so that no one knew it, and only the Grand Censor Wang Yue became friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was quick and cunning; the emperor had him change clothes and slip out with one or two guard officers to spy on affairs, so that none knew—except Grand Censor Wang Yue, who cultivated his friendship.

sentences.zh: 明年設西廠，以直領之，列官校刺事。

translations.literal: The next year the Western Depot was established and placed under Zhi, with a line of officials and guards sent out to spy on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Western Depot was established with Zhi at its head, and lines of guard officers were deployed to gather intelligence.

sentences.zh: 南京鎮監覃力朋進貢還，以百艘載私鹽，騷擾州縣。

translations.literal: Qin Lipeng, the Nanjing garrison eunuch, returned after delivering tribute and loaded a hundred boats with private salt, harassing the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Lipeng, the Nanjing garrison eunuch, returned from delivering tribute with a hundred boats laden with contraband salt, harassing prefectures and counties along the way.

sentences.zh: 武城縣典史詰之，力朋擊典史，折其齒，射殺一人。

translations.literal: When the county registrar of Wucheng County questioned him, Lipeng beat the clerk, broke his teeth, and shot one man dead.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar of Wucheng County challenged him; Lipeng beat the man, broke his teeth, and shot one of his companions dead.

sentences.zh: 直廉得以聞，逮治論斬。

translations.literal: Zhi investigated and reported it; Lipeng was seized, tried, and sentenced to death by beheading.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi investigated and reported the crime; Lipeng was arrested, tried, and sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 力朋後得幸免，而帝以此謂直能摘奸，益幸直。

translations.literal: Lipeng later escaped punishment, and the emperor, seeing this as proof that Zhi could uncover criminals, favored Zhi even more.
translations.idiomatic: Lipeng eventually escaped execution, but the emperor took this as proof that Zhi could uncover wrongdoing and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 直乃任錦衣百戶韋瑛為心腹，屢興大獄。

translations.literal: Zhi then took the Brocade Guard hundred-household officer Wei Ying as his trusted agent and repeatedly initiated major prosecutions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then installed the Brocade Guard hundred-household officer Wei Ying as his trusted inside man and repeatedly opened major prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 建寧衛指揮楊曄，故少師榮曾孫也，與父泰為仇家所告，逃入京，匿姊夫董玙所。

translations.literal: Yang Ye, commander of Jianning Guard, was a grandson of the former Grand Tutor Rong. He and his father Tai had been denounced by an enemy clan and fled to the capital, where they hid at his brother-in-law Dong Yu's home.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye, commander of Jianning Guard, was a grandson of the former Grand Tutor Rong; he and his father Tai had been denounced by a hostile clan, fled to the capital, and hid at the home of his brother-in-law Dong Yu.

sentences.zh: 玙為請瑛，瑛陽諾而馳報直。

translations.literal: Yu begged Wei Ying on his behalf; Wei Ying agreed on the surface but hurried to report it to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu begged Wei Ying to intercede; Ying agreed on the surface but galloped off to report to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 直即捕曄、玙考訊，三琶之。

translations.literal: Zhi at once arrested Ye and Yu, interrogated them, and put them to the three tortures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi at once seized Ye and Yu and subjected them to interrogation under the "triple pa" torture.

sentences.zh: 琶者，錦衣酷刑也。

translations.literal: The pa was a brutal torture of the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The pa was a brutal Brocade Guard punishment.

sentences.zh: 骨節皆寸解，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: The joints were all dislocated joint by joint, and he would lose consciousness and then come back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Joint by joint the bones were wrenched apart; the victim would faint away and then be revived.

sentences.zh: 曄不勝苦，妄言寄金於其叔父兵部主事士偉所。

translations.literal: Unable to endure the torture, Ye falsely said that he had stored gold with his uncle Shi Wei, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Ye could bear no more and falsely confessed that he had deposited gold with his uncle Shi Wei, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 直不復奏請，捕士偉下獄，並掠其妻孥。

translations.literal: Without awaiting memorial approval from the throne, Zhi seized Shi Wei, imprisoned him, and also seized his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Without awaiting memorial approval from the throne, Zhi arrested Shi Wei and threw him into prison, also seizing his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 獄具，曄死獄中，泰論斬，士偉等皆謫官，郎中武清、樂章，行人張廷綱，參政劉福等皆無故被收案。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Ye died in prison, Tai was sentenced to beheading, Shi Wei and the others were all demoted, and the section directors Wu Qing and Le Zhang, envoy Zhang Tinggang, and vice commissioner Liu Fu were all seized without cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, Ye died in prison, Tai was sentenced to beheading, Shi Wei and his kin were all demoted—and for no cause at all the section directors Wu Qing and Le Zhang, envoy Zhang Tinggang, and vice commissioner Liu Fu were also dragged into the affair.

sentences.zh: 自諸王府邊鎮及南北河道，所在校尉羅列，民間鬥詈雞狗瑣事，輒置重法，人情大擾。

translations.literal: From the princely establishments and frontier garrisons to the canal routes north and south, guard officers were posted everywhere; even minor commoner disputes over dogs and chickens were often dealt with under harsh law, and public feeling was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: From the princely establishments and frontier garrisons to the canal routes north and south, guard officers were posted everywhere; the most trivial squabbles over chickens and dogs were punished with harsh law, and public life was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 直每出，隨從甚眾，公卿皆避道。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhi went out, he was followed by a great retinue, and all the nobles and ministers cleared the road for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhi went abroad he was followed by a great train, and nobles and ministers alike cleared the road.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書項忠不避，迫辱之，權焰出東廠上。

translations.literal: Minister of War Xiang Zhong alone refused to yield; Zhi pressed upon and humiliated him—and Zhi's arrogance now surpassed even the Eastern Depot's.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Xiang Zhong alone would not yield; Zhi pressed upon and humiliated him—and Zhi's arrogance now outstripped even the Eastern Depot's.

sentences.zh: 五月，大學士商輅與萬安、劉珝、劉吉奏其狀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Grand Secretaries Shang Lu, Wan An, Liu Xu, and Liu Ji submitted a memorial reporting his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Grand Secretaries Shang Lu, Wan An, Liu Xu, and Liu Ji memorialized the throne with an account of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，命司禮太監懷恩、覃吉、黃高至閣下，厲色傳旨，言：「疏出誰意？」

translations.literal: The emperor was thunderstruck and ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial Service eunuchs Huai'en, Qin Ji, and Huang Gao to go to the Grand Secretariat, where they sternly delivered the imperial order and said: "Who suggested this memorial?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was thunderstruck and sent the eunuchs Huai'en, Qin Ji, and Huang Gao from the Directorate of Ceremonial to the Grand Secretariat to deliver his wrathful order: "Whose idea was this memorial?

sentences.zh: 輅口數直罪甚悉，因言：「臣等同心一意，為國除害，無有先後。」

translations.literal: Lu recited Zhi's crimes in full, then said: "We are of one mind and one purpose, removing harm for the state, with no thought of rank or order."
translations.idiomatic: Lu recited Zhi's offenses in detail, then said: "We are of one mind, acting together to remove a menace to the state—there is no question of seniority among us."

sentences.zh: 珝慷慨泣下。

translations.literal: Xu burst into tears as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Xu spoke with passion and wept.

sentences.zh: 恩遂據實以奏。

translations.literal: Huai'en then reported the facts truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en then reported what had passed, truthfully and in full.

sentences.zh: 頃之，傳旨慰勞。

translations.literal: After a while, the imperial order came back expressing consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an order came back with words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 翼日，尚書忠及諸大臣疏亦入。

translations.literal: The next day, memorials from Minister Zhong and the various grandees also came in.
translations.idiomatic: The next day memorials from Minister Zhong and other grandees also arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，罷西廠，使懷恩數直罪而宥之，令歸御馬監，調韋瑛邊衛，散諸旗校還錦衣。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to abolish the Western Depot, had Huai'en list Zhi's crimes and pardon him, ordered him back to the Imperial Horse Directorate, reassigned Wei Ying to a frontier guard, and scattered the various banner guards back to the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to abolish the Western Depot, had Huai'en enumerate Zhi's crimes and then pardon him, ordered him back to the Imperial Horse Directorate, transferred Wei Ying to a frontier guard, and scattered the depot's banner officers back to the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 中外大悅。

translations.literal: Both court and commoners were overjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 然帝眷直不衰。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's favor toward Zhi did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor's affection for Zhi did not wane.

sentences.zh: 直因言閣疏出司禮監黃賜、陳祖生意，為楊曄報復。

translations.literal: Zhi then said that the Grand Secretariat's memorial had been prompted by the Directorate of Ceremonial Service eunuchs Huang Ci and Chen Zusheng, as revenge for Yang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi claimed the memorial had originated with Huang Ci and Chen Zusheng of the Directorate of Ceremonial, seeking revenge for Yang Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝即斥賜、祖生於南京。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately exiled Ci and Zusheng to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once exiled Ci and Zusheng to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 御史戴縉者，佞人也，九年秩滿不得遷。

translations.literal: The censor Dai Jin was a sycophant; when his nine-year term was up, he failed to get promoted.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Dai Jin was a flatterer; when his nine-year term expired he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 窺帝旨，盛稱直功。

translations.literal: He read the emperor's intentions and loudly praised Zhi's merits.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mood, he loudly praised Zhi's achievements.

sentences.zh: 詔復開西廠，以千戶吳綬為鎮撫，直焰愈熾。

translations.literal: An edict reopened the Western Depot, with the thousand-household officer Wu Shou made commander; Zhi's arrogance burned even more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reopened the Western Depot, with Wu Shou of the thousand-household rank appointed prison commander; Zhi's arrogance burned hotter than ever.

sentences.zh: 未幾，令東廠官校誣奏項忠，且諷言官郭鏜、馮貫等論忠違法事。

translations.literal: Soon he had the East Depot officials and guards falsely memorialize against Xiang Zhong, and also prompted the remonstrance officials Guo Tang, Feng Guan, and others to speak on Zhong's illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had Eastern Depot officers fabricate charges against Xiang Zhong, and also egged on the remonstrance officials Guo Tang, Feng Guan, and others to denounce Zhong for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝命三法司、錦衣衛會問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the three judicial offices and the Brocade Guard to meet and question him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the three judicial offices and the Brocade Guard to conduct a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 眾知出直意，無敢違，竟勒忠為民。

translations.literal: Everyone knew it was Zhi's intention and no one dared oppose it, so they ultimately reduced Zhong to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: All knew this was Zhi's doing and dared not resist; in the end Zhong was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 而左都御史李賓亦失直旨褫職，大學士輅亦罷去。

translations.literal: The Left Grand Censor Li Bin also lost his office for offending Zhi's wishes, and Grand Secretary Lu was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Censor Li Bin also lost his post for crossing Zhi's wishes, and Grand Secretary Lu was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 一時九卿劾罷者，尚書董方、薛遠及侍郎滕昭、程萬里等數十人。

translations.literal: Among the many high ministers impeached and dismissed at that time were the ministers Dong Fang and Xue Yuan, as well as vice ministers Teng Zhao, Cheng Wanli, and dozens of others.
translations.idiomatic: Among the high ministers impeached and removed at that time were the ministers Dong Fang and Xue Yuan, the vice ministers Teng Zhao and Cheng Wanli, and dozens more.

sentences.zh: 以所善王越為兵部尚書兼左都御史，陳鉞為右副都御史巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He put his close ally Wang Yue in office as Minister of War and concurrently Left Grand Censor, and Chen Yue was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to serve as governor of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi installed his favorites: Wang Yue as Minister of War and concurrent Left Grand Censor, and Chen Yue as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十五年秋，詔直巡邊，率飛騎日馳數百里，御史、主事等官迎拜馬首，箠撻守令。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year, an edict sent Zhi to inspect the border; he led fast cavalry and rode hundreds of li a day, while censors, section chiefs, and other officials came out to bow at his horse's head, and he flogged the border magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year an edict sent Zhi to inspect the frontier; he led swift cavalry and covered hundreds of li a day, while censors, section chiefs, and other officials bowed at his horse's head—and he flogged magistrates as he went.

sentences.zh: 各邊都御史畏直，服櫜迎謁，供張百里外。

translations.literal: The Grand Censors of the various borders feared Zhi, wore their armor and went out to greet him, and provided lavish hospitality more than a hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier grand censors feared him; they donned armor to greet him and laid on hospitality a hundred li out.

sentences.zh: 至遼東，陳鉞郊迎蒲伏，廚傳尤盛，左右皆有賄。

translations.literal: When he reached Liaodong, Chen Yue came out to greet him in the suburbs and lay prostrate before him; the kitchens and courier stations were especially lavish, and everyone around him accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Liaodong, Chen Yue came out to the suburbs, prostrated himself in the dust, and entertained him on the grandest scale; everyone at Zhi's side accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 直大悅。

translations.literal: Zhi was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 惟河南巡撫秦纮與直抗禮，而密奏直巡邊擾民。

translations.literal: Only Qin Hong, the governor of Henan, stood on ceremony with Zhi, and secretly memorialized that Zhi's border inspection was disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Only Henan governor Qin Hong treated him as an equal and secretly memorialized that Zhi's frontier tour was harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 帝弗省。

translations.literal: The emperor ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎馬文升方撫諭遼東，直至不為禮，又輕鉞，被陷坐戍，由是直威勢傾天下。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of War Ma Wensheng was pacifying Liaodong, Zhi arrived and did not treat him with courtesy, and he also slighted Chen Yue; Ma was framed and sentenced to frontier garrison duty, and from then on Zhi's power and influence overshadowed the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Ma Wensheng was then pacifying Liaodong; when Zhi arrived he offered no courtesy and also slighted Chen Yue—whereupon Ma was framed and sentenced to border garrison duty. From that point Zhi's power cast its shadow over the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 直年少喜兵。

translations.literal: Zhi was young and loved military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was young and loved military affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳鉞諷直征伏當加，立邊功自固。

translations.literal: Chen Yue urged Zhi to campaign against Fudangjia, seeking to establish border merit and secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue urged him to campaign against Fudangjia, arguing that frontier merit would secure his position.

sentences.zh: 直聽之，用撫寧侯朱永總兵，而自監其軍。

translations.literal: Zhi accepted it, using Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong as the overall commander and supervising the army himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi agreed, made Marquis Zhu Yong of Funing overall commander, and personally supervised the army.

sentences.zh: 師還，永封保國公，鉞晉右都御史，直加祿米。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of Baoguo, Yue was promoted to Right Grand Censor, and Zhi was given additional grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Yong was enfeoffed Duke of Baoguo, Chen Yue was promoted to Right Grand Censor, and Zhi received additional grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 又用王越言，詐稱亦思馬因犯邊。

translations.literal: He also followed Wang Yue's suggestion and falsely claimed that Yisimayin had raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Yue's advice, they also fabricated a report that Yisimayin had raided the border.

sentences.zh: 詔永同越西討，直為監軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yong to campaign west together with Yue, with Zhi serving as supervising officer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yong and Yue to campaign west together, with Zhi as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 越封威寧伯，直再加祿米。

translations.literal: Yue was enfeoffed as Marquis of Weining, and Zhi again received extra grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was enfeoffed Marquis of Weining, and Zhi again received extra grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 已，伏當加寇遼東，亦思馬因寇大同，殺掠甚眾。

translations.literal: Afterward, Fudangjia raided Liaodong, and Yisimayin raided Datong, killing and plundering many people.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fudangjia raided Liaodong and Yisimayin raided Datong, killing and plundering on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 遼東巡按強珍發鉞奸狀，直右鉞謫珍。

translations.literal: The surveillance censor Qiang Zhen in Liaodong exposed Yue's criminal conduct, and Zhi sided with Yue and demoted Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance censor Qiang Zhen in Liaodong exposed Chen Yue's misconduct; Zhi sided with Yue and demoted Zhen.

sentences.zh: 於是惡直者，指王越、陳鉞為二鉞。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who hated Zhi referred to Wang Yue and Chen Yue as the two Yues.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hated Zhi began to call Wang Yue and Chen Yue his "two battle-axes."

sentences.zh: 小中官阿醜工俳優，一日於帝前為醉者謾罵狀。

translations.literal: The junior eunuch Achou was skilled at comic performance; one day before the emperor he acted out the manner of a drunken man cursing.
translations.idiomatic: The junior eunuch Achou was skilled at comic mimicry; one day before the emperor he performed a drunk man hurling abuse.

sentences.zh: 人言駕至，謾如故。

translations.literal: When someone said the carriage had arrived, he kept cursing as before.
translations.idiomatic: When someone cried that the imperial carriage was coming, he kept on cursing as before.

sentences.zh: 言汪太監至，則避走。

translations.literal: When it was said that the arrival was Wang the eunuch, he ran off to hide.
translations.idiomatic: But at the words "Director Wang is here," he fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 曰：「今人但知汪太監也。」

translations.literal: He said: "Nowadays people only know Wang the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: "These days everyone knows only Director Wang.

sentences.zh: 又為直狀，操兩鉞趨帝前。

translations.literal: He also performed the role of Zhi, carrying two battle-axes and striding before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also impersonated Zhi, striding before the throne carrying two battle-axes.

sentences.zh: 旁人問之，曰：「吾將兵，仗此兩鉞耳。」

translations.literal: When others asked him about it, he said: "I am a soldier; I rely on these two axes.
translations.idiomatic: When asked what they were, he said: "I am a general—these two axes are all I rely on.

sentences.zh: 問何鉞，曰：「王越、陳鉞也。」

translations.literal: When asked which axes, he said: "Wang Yue and Chen Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Asked whose axes, he replied: "Wang Yue and Chen Yue."

sentences.zh: 帝聽然而笑，稍稍悟，然廷臣猶未敢攻直也。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled knowingly, but the court ministers still did not dare attack Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled at this and slowly took the hint—yet the court ministers still dared not move against Zhi.

sentences.zh: 會東廠尚銘獲賊得厚賞，直忌，且怒銘不告。

translations.literal: When the East Depot eunuch Shang Ming captured a bandit and received a rich reward, Zhi became jealous and also angry that Ming had not reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Ming of the Eastern Depot captured a bandit and won a rich reward, Zhi grew jealous—and angry that Ming had not told him first.

sentences.zh: 銘懼，乃廉得其所泄禁中秘語奏之，盡發王越交通不法事，帝始疏直。

translations.literal: Ming was afraid, so he secretly learned what confidential palace words had been leaked and reported them, fully exposing Wang Yue's unlawful dealings, and only then did the emperor begin to distance himself from Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ming, frightened, secretly traced the leaked palace confidences and reported them, fully exposing Wang Yue's unlawful dealings; only then did the emperor begin to turn away from Zhi.

sentences.zh: 十七年秋，命直偕越往宣府禦敵。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventeenth year, the emperor ordered Zhi to go with Yue to Xuanfu to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventeenth year the emperor ordered Zhi and Yue to Xuanfu to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵退，直請班師。

translations.literal: When the enemy retreated, Zhi requested that the army withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, Zhi asked to bring the army home.

sentences.zh: 不許，徙鎮大同，而盡召將吏還，獨留直、越。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; the garrison was moved to Datong, all the generals and officials were summoned back, and only Zhi and Yue were left.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was refused; the garrison was shifted to Datong, all officers were recalled—and only Zhi and Yue were left behind.

sentences.zh: 直既久鎮不得還，寵日衰。

translations.literal: After Zhi had remained at the garrison for a long time without being allowed to return, his favor gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi remained on the frontier for a long time without being allowed to return, and his favor steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 給事御史交章奏其苛擾，請仍罷西廠。

translations.literal: Assistant secretaries and censors jointly memorialized against his harsh disruption and requested that the Western Depot be abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretaries and censors bombarded the throne with memorials against his harsh disruptions and called for the Western Depot to be abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 閣臣萬安亦力言之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wan An also strongly argued for it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wan An argued forcefully for the same course.

sentences.zh: 而大同巡撫郭鏜復言直與總兵許寧不和，恐誤邊事。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator of Datong, Guo Tang, also reported that Wang Zhi and the regional commander Xu Ning were at odds and that this discord might jeopardize frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tang, grand coordinator of Datong, also reported that Wang Zhi and the regional commander Xu Ning were at loggerheads, and that their discord might jeopardize frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝乃調直南京御馬監，罷西廠不復設。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon transferred Wang Zhi to the Nanjing Imperial Horse Directorate and abolished the Western Depot, never to reestablish it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon transferred Wang Zhi to the Nanjing Imperial Horse Directorate and abolished the Western Depot, never to establish it again.

sentences.zh: 中外欣然。

translations.literal: Both court and commoners were delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 尋又以言官言，降直奉御，而褫逐其黨王越、戴縉、吳綬等。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on the advice of the remonstrance officials, Zhi was reduced to a fengyu officer, and his allies Wang Yue, Dai Jin, Wu Shou, and others were stripped and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at the urging of the censorial officials, Wang Zhi was demoted to the rank of fengyu, and his partisans Wang Yue, Dai Jin, Wu Shou, and others were stripped of office and driven out.

sentences.zh: 陳鉞已致仕，不問。

translations.literal: Chen Yue had already retired, so he was not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue had already retired and was not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 韋瑛後坐他事誅，人皆快之，然直竟良死。

translations.literal: Wei Ying was later executed for another offense, which everyone welcomed, though Zhi himself ultimately died a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ying was later executed on other charges, to general public satisfaction; Wang Zhi, however, died peacefully in the end.

sentences.zh: 縉由御史不數年至南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: Dai Jin, starting as a censor, became the Nanjing Minister of Works in only a few years.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Jin rose from censor to Minister of Works at Nanjing in only a few years.

sentences.zh: 越、鉞頗以材進。

translations.literal: Wang Yue and Chen Yue had considerable ability and were promoted on merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and Chen Yue had risen largely on genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 縉無他能，工側媚而已。

translations.literal: Dai Jin had no special talent, only a knack for flattering and currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Jin possessed no other ability—only a talent for fawning sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 西廠廢，尚銘遂專東廠事。

translations.literal: After the Western Depot was abolished, Shang Ming took sole charge of the East Depot.
translations.idiomatic: With the Western Depot abolished, Shang Ming came to monopolize the affairs of the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 聞京師有富室，輒以事羅織，得重賄乃已。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard of a wealthy family in the capital, he would frame them on some charge and stop only after extracting a heavy bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he learned of a wealthy household in the capital, he would manufacture charges against them and desist only after extorting a heavy bribe.

sentences.zh: 賣官鬻爵，無所不至。

translations.literal: Selling offices and titles, he stopped at nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He sold offices and peddled ranks, stopping at nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝尋覺之，謫充南京凈軍，籍其家，輦送內府，數日不盡。

translations.literal: The emperor soon discovered his abuses, demoted him to menial service among the Nanjing palace guards, confiscated his property, and had the goods carted into the inner treasury—in cartloads that took days to unload.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon discovered his abuses, demoted him to menial service among the Nanjing palace guards, confiscated his property, and had the goods carted into the inner treasury—in cartloads that took days to unload.

sentences.zh: 而陳準代為東廠。

translations.literal: Chen Zhun then replaced him at the East Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhun then replaced him at the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 準素善懷恩，既代銘，誡諸校尉曰：「有大逆，告我。

translations.literal: Zhun had long been friendly with Huai'en; after taking Ming's place, he warned the sergeants: "If there is a grave act of treason, report it to me.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhun had long been on good terms with Huai'en; after replacing Shang Ming, he admonished the depot guards: "If there is a grave act of treason, report it to me.

sentences.zh: 非是，若勿預也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, do not involve yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, do not involve yourselves.

sentences.zh: 都人安之。

translations.literal: The people of the capital felt at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital were relieved.

sentences.zh: 梁芳者，憲宗朝內侍也。

translations.literal: Liang Fang was an inner-chamber eunuch under the Chenghua Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fang was an inner-chamber eunuch under the Chenghua Emperor.

sentences.zh: 貪黷諛佞，與韋興比。

translations.literal: He was greedy, rapacious, and flattering, and associated with Wei Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, corrupt, and sycophantic, he was a match for Wei Xing.

sentences.zh: 而諂萬貴妃，日進美珠珍寶悅妃意。

translations.literal: He also flattered Consort Wan, daily presenting fine pearls and jewels to please her.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered Consort Wan, daily presenting her with fine pearls and jewels to win her favor.

sentences.zh: 其黨錢能、韋眷、王敬等，爭假采辦名，出監大鎮。

translations.literal: His followers Qian Neng, Wei Juan, Wang Jing, and others all rushed to take on procurement missions and go out to supervise major garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His associates Qian Neng, Wei Juan, Wang Jing, and others vied to take on procurement missions and go out to supervise the major garrisons.

sentences.zh: 帝以妃故，不問也。

translations.literal: Because of the consort, the emperor did not investigate them.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the consort, the emperor made no inquiry into their conduct.

sentences.zh: 妖人李孜省、僧繼曉皆由芳進，共為奸利。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Li Zisheng and the monk Jixiao were both introduced by Fang and joined in corrupt profiteering.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Li Zisheng and the monk Jixiao were both brought in by Liang Fang, and together they engaged in corrupt profiteering.

sentences.zh: 取中旨授官，累數千人，名傳奉官，有白衣躐至太常卿者。

translations.literal: Using informal imperial commands, they conferred office on several thousand men, known as chuanfeng officials, and even commoners leaped directly to the rank of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Using informal imperial commands, they appointed several thousand men to office—they were called chuanfeng officials—and commoners leaped in a single bound to posts as lofty as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫鄭時論芳被黜，陜民哭送之。

translations.literal: When Zheng Shi, governor of Shaanxi, criticized Fang and was removed, the people of Shaanxi wept as they saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Shi, grand coordinator of Shaanxi, impeached Liang Fang and was dismissed, the people of Shaanxi wept as they saw him off.

sentences.zh: 帝聞頗悔，斥傳奉官十人，系六人獄，詔自後傳旨授官者俱覆奏，然不罪芳也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and somewhat regretted it; he dismissed ten transmission-offering officials and jailed six others, and issued an edict that from then on all appointments made by imperial instruction had to be reviewed and reported, though Fang himself was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was somewhat remorseful: he dismissed ten chuanfeng officials and imprisoned six others, and decreed that henceforth all appointments made by transmitted imperial command must be reported back for review—yet Liang Fang himself went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎林俊以劾芳及繼曉下獄。

translations.literal: When Lin Jun, a vice director in the Ministry of Justice, impeached Fang and Jixiao, he was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun, a vice director in the Ministry of Justice, was thrown into prison for impeaching Liang Fang and Jixiao.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝視內帑，見累朝金七窖俱盡，謂芳及韋興曰：「糜費帑藏，實由汝二人。」

translations.literal: After some time, when the emperor inspected the inner treasury and saw that the seven gold vaults of successive reigns were all emptied, he said to Fang and Wei Xing: "You two are truly the ones who have wasted the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, when the emperor inspected the inner treasury and saw that the seven gold vaults accumulated under successive reigns had all been emptied, he said to Liang Fang and Wei Xing: "You two are the ones who have squandered the treasury.

sentences.zh: 興不敢對。

translations.literal: Xing did not dare answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xing did not dare answer.

sentences.zh: 芳曰：「建顯靈宮及諸祠廟，為陛下祈萬年福耳。」

translations.literal: Fang said: "We built the Xianling Palace and the various shrines only to pray for Your Majesty's ten-thousand-year blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fang said: "We built the Xianling Palace and the various shrines only to pray for Your Majesty's long life and boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌曰：「吾不汝瑕，後之人將與汝計矣」。

translations.literal: The emperor said unhappily: "I do not fault you now, but later people will settle accounts with you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, displeased: "I will not hold you to account now—but those who come after will settle the score with you."

sentences.zh: 芳大懼，遂說貴妃勸帝廢太子，而立興王。

translations.literal: Fang was deeply frightened and then persuaded the consort to urge the emperor to depose the crown prince and install the Prince of Xing instead.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fang was deeply frightened and then persuaded Consort Wan to urge the emperor to depose the crown prince and install the Prince of Xing in his place.

sentences.zh: 會泰山累震，占者言應在東朝。

translations.literal: Then Mount Tai shook repeatedly, and the diviners said the omen pointed to the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Mount Tai was shaken by repeated earthquakes, and diviners declared the omen concerned the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor became afraid and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, alarmed, abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，謫芳居南京，尋下獄，興亦斥退。

translations.literal: When the Hongzhi Emperor ascended the throne, Fang was banished to Nanjing and soon imprisoned; Xing was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi Emperor acceded, Liang Fang was banished to Nanjing and soon imprisoned; Wei Xing was also dismissed.

sentences.zh: 正德初，群閹復薦興司香太和山，兼分守湖廣行都司地方。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengde, the eunuchs once again recommended Xing for the incense office at Mount Taihe and, in addition, for joint defense of the Huguang regional command area.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Zhengde reign, the eunuch faction again recommended Wei Xing to oversee incense offerings at Mount Taihe and, concurrently, to help administer the Huguang Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉大夏、給事中周璽、御史曹來旬諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Daxia, supervising secretary Zhou Xi, and censor Cao Laixun remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Daxia, supervising secretary Zhou Xi, and censor Cao Laixun remonstrated, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 興遂復用，而芳卒廢以死。

translations.literal: Xing was then again brought back into use, while Fang eventually was dismissed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xing was restored to office, while Liang Fang ultimately lived out his days in disgrace and died.

sentences.zh: 錢能，芳黨也。

translations.literal: Qian Neng was a follower of Liang Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng was another of Liang Fang's faction.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，鄭忠鎮貴州，韋朗鎮遼東，能鎮雲南，並恣縱，而能尤橫。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign, Zheng Zhong supervised Guizhou, Wei Lang supervised Liaodong, and Neng supervised Yunnan; all abused their authority, but Neng was the most imperious.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, Zheng Zhong supervised Guizhou, Wei Lang supervised Liaodong, and Qian Neng supervised Yunnan; all abused their authority, but Neng was the most imperious.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫陳宣劾忠，因請盡撤諸鎮監，帝不允。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan, grand coordinator of Guizhou, impeached Zhong and requested that all garrison eunuchs be withdrawn; the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan, grand coordinator of Guizhou, impeached Zheng Zhong and requested that all garrison eunuchs be withdrawn; the emperor did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 而雲南巡按御史郭陽顧上疏譽能，請留之雲南。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Guo Yanggu, the touring censor of Yunnan, submitted a memorial praising Neng and asking that he remain in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guo Yanggu, the touring censor of Yunnan, submitted a memorial praising Qian Neng and asking that he remain in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 舊制，安南貢道出廣西，後請改由雲南，弗許也。

translations.literal: By established practice the Annamese tribute route ran through Guangxi; a later request to reroute it through Yunnan was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice the Annamese tribute route ran through Guangxi; a later request to reroute it through Yunnan was not approved.

sentences.zh: 能詐言安南捕盜兵入境，請遣指揮使郭景往諭其王，詔從之。

translations.literal: Neng falsely reported that Annamese troops pursuing bandits had crossed the border, and requested that Commander Guo Jing be sent to instruct their king; an imperial command approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng falsely reported that Annamese troops pursuing bandits had crossed the border, and requested that Commander Guo Jing be sent to instruct their king; an imperial command approved it.

sentences.zh: 能遂令景以玉帶、彩繒、犬馬遺王，紿其貢使改道雲南。

translations.literal: Neng then had Jing present the king with jade belts, colored silks, dogs, and horses, deceiving the tribute envoys into altering their route through Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng then had Guo Jing present the king with jade belts, colored silks, dogs, and horses, deceiving the tribute envoys into altering their route through Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 邊吏格之不得入，乃去。

translations.literal: Border officials blocked them and would not permit entry, so they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials blocked them and would not permit entry, so they departed.

sentences.zh: 復遣景與指揮盧安等索寶貨於幹崖、孟密諸土司，至逼淫曩罕弄女孫，許為奏授宣撫。

translations.literal: Neng again sent Jing together with Commander Lu An and others to extort treasures from the native chiefs of Ganyai, Mengmi, and elsewhere, going so far as to forcibly violate the granddaughter of the tribal leader Mang Hanong, promising in exchange to memorialize the throne for her appointment as native prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng again sent Guo Jing together with Commander Lu An and others to extort treasures from the native chiefs of Ganyai, Mengmi, and elsewhere, going so far as to forcibly violate the granddaughter of the tribal leader Mang Hanong, promising in exchange to memorialize the throne for her appointment as native prefect.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，事發。

translations.literal: More than three years later the affair came to light.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later the affair came to light.

sentences.zh: 詔巡撫都御史王恕廉之，捕景，景赴井死。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Wang Shu to investigate; Jing was arrested and drowned himself in a well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Wang Shu to investigate; Guo Jing was arrested and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 再遣刑部郎中鍾蕃往按，事皆實。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice director Zhong Fan was sent to conduct a further inquiry, and the charges were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice director Zhong Fan was sent to conduct a further inquiry, and every charge was verified.

sentences.zh: 帝宥能，而致其黨九人於法。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Neng but punished nine of his associates according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Qian Neng but punished nine of his associates according to law.

sentences.zh: 指揮姜和、李祥不就逮，能復上疏為二人求宥，帝曲從之。

translations.literal: Commanders Jiang He and Li Xiang refused to submit to arrest; Neng again submitted a memorial asking clemency for the two men, and the emperor reluctantly acceded.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Jiang He and Li Xiang refused to submit to arrest; Qian Neng again submitted a memorial asking clemency for the two men, and the emperor reluctantly acceded.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史甄希賢復劾能杖守礦千戶一人死，亦不罪。

translations.literal: Touring censor Zhen Xixian again impeached Neng for beating a thousand-household mine guard to death, yet he was again not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Zhen Xixian again impeached Qian Neng for beating a thousand-household mine guard to death, yet he was again not punished.

sentences.zh: 召歸，安置南京。

translations.literal: Neng was recalled and settled in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng was recalled and settled in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 復夤緣得南京守備。

translations.literal: Through connections he again secured the post of Nanjing garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through connections he again secured the post of Nanjing garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 時恕為南京參贊尚書，能心憚恕不敢肆。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shu served as coordinating minister at Nanjing; Neng inwardly feared him and did not dare run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Shu served as coordinating minister at Nanjing; Qian Neng inwardly feared him and did not dare run rampant.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long interval he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he died.

sentences.zh: 韋眷、王敬亦芳黨。

translations.literal: Wei Juan and Wang Jing were also members of Liang Fang's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juan and Wang Jing were also members of Liang Fang's faction.

sentences.zh: 眷為廣東市舶太監，縱賈人通諸番，聚珍寶甚富。

translations.literal: As Guangdong superintendent of maritime trade, Juan allowed merchants to trade with the foreign kingdoms and amassed enormous stores of jewels and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: As Guangdong superintendent of maritime trade, Wei Juan allowed merchants to trade with the foreign kingdoms and amassed enormous stores of jewels and treasures.

sentences.zh: 請以廣南均徭戶六十隸市舶。

translations.literal: He requested that sixty corvée households from Guangnan be placed under the maritime trade office.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that sixty corvée households from Guangnan be placed under the maritime trade office.

sentences.zh: 布政使彭韶爭之，詔給其半。

translations.literal: Regional administrator Peng Shao contested the request; an edict granted half.
translations.idiomatic: Regional administrator Peng Shao contested the request; an edict granted half.

sentences.zh: 眷又誣奏布政使陳選，被逮道卒，自是，人莫敢逆眷者。

translations.literal: Juan also fabricated charges against Regional Administrator Chen Xuan; Chen was arrested and died on the road, and from that time onward no one dared oppose Juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juan also fabricated charges against regional administrator Chen Xuan; Chen was arrested and died on the road, and from that time onward no one dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，眷因結蔡用妄舉李父貴冒紀太后族，降左少監，撤回京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, Juan, through his association with Cai Yong, falsely promoted Li Fugui as a kinsman of Empress Dowager Ji; he was demoted to assistant director of the Left and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongzhi, Wei Juan, through his association with Cai Yong, falsely promoted Li Fugui as a kinsman of Empress Dowager Ji; he was demoted to assistant director of the Left and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 事詳《紀太后傳》。

translations.literal: Details are given in the Biography of Empress Dowager Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the Biography of Empress Dowager Ji.

sentences.zh: 王敬好左道，信妖人王臣。

translations.literal: Wang Jing was devoted to heterodox practices and put his faith in the sorcerer Wang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing was devoted to heterodox practices and put his faith in the sorcerer Wang Chen.

sentences.zh: 使南方，挾臣同行。

translations.literal: When he was sent south on a mission, he took Chen along with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent south on a mission, he took Wang Chen along with him.

sentences.zh: 偽為詔，括書畫、古玩，聚白金十萬餘兩。

translations.literal: Forging an imperial edict, he requisitioned paintings, antiquities, and curios, amassing more than a hundred thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Forging an imperial edict, he requisitioned paintings, antiquities, and curios, amassing more than a hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 至蘇州，召諸生使錄妖書，且辱之。

translations.literal: At Suzhou he summoned the local scholars and forced them to copy out heterodox writings, humiliating them in the process.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzhou he summoned the local scholars and forced them to copy out heterodox writings, humiliating them in the process.

sentences.zh: 諸生大嘩。

translations.literal: The students were in great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王恕以聞。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Shu reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Shu reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 東廠尚銘亦發其事。

translations.literal: The East Depot eunuch Shang Ming also exposed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ming of the Eastern Depot also exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 詔斬臣，而黜敬充孝陵衛凈軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Chen executed and Wang Jing demoted to menial service in the Xiaoling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Chen executed and Wang Jing demoted to menial service in the Xiaoling Guard.

sentences.zh: 何鼎

translations.literal: He Ding
translations.idiomatic: He Ding

sentences.zh: 何鼎，餘杭人，一名文鼎，性忠直。

translations.literal: He Ding (Deng Yuan) was a man of Yuhang, also known as Wending, and was loyal and straightforward by nature.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding, also called Deng Yuan, was from Yuhang and was by nature loyal and straightforward.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，為長隨，上疏請革傳奉官，為儕輩所忌。

translations.literal: At the start of Hongzhi, as a lowly attendant, he submitted a memorial asking that transmission-offering officials be abolished, and was disliked by his peers for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongzhi, while still a lowly attendant, he submitted a memorial calling for the abolition of chuanfeng officials and was resented by his peers for it.

sentences.zh: 壽寧侯張鶴齡兄弟出入宮禁，嘗侍內庭宴。

translations.literal: The brothers of the Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, came and went within the palace precincts and once attended a banquet in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heling and his brothers, kin of the Marquis of Shouning, came and went within the palace precincts and once attended a banquet in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 帝如廁，鶴齡倚酒戴帝冠，鼎心怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to the privy, Heling, drunk, put on the emperor's crown; Ding was furious.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stepped out to the privy, Heling, drunk, put on the imperial crown; He Ding was incensed.

sentences.zh: 他日鶴齡復窺禦帷，鼎持大瓜欲擊之，奏言：「二張大不敬，無人臣禮。」

translations.literal: Another day Heling again peered behind the imperial curtain; Ding seized a large melon intending to strike him and memorialized: "The two Zhang brothers are grossly disrespectful and utterly devoid of a subject's decorum.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Heling again peered behind the imperial curtain; He Ding seized a large melon intending to strike him and memorialized: "The two Zhang brothers are grossly disrespectful and utterly devoid of a subject's decorum.

sentences.zh: 皇后激帝怒，下鼎錦衣獄。

translations.literal: The empress stirred the emperor's anger, and Ding was sent to the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: The empress inflamed the emperor's wrath, and He Ding was thrown into the Brocade Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 問主使，鼎曰：「有。」

translations.literal: When asked who had instructed him, Ding said: "There was one.
translations.idiomatic: When asked who had instructed him, He Ding said: "There was one.

sentences.zh: 問為誰，曰：「孔子、孟子也。」

translations.literal: When asked who it was, he said: "Confucius and Mencius."
translations.idiomatic: When asked who it was, he said: "Confucius and Mencius."

sentences.zh: 給事中龐泮、御史吳山及尚書周經、主事李昆、進士吳宗周先後論救，帝以後故，俱不納。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Pang Pan, censor Wu Shan, Minister Zhou Jing, chief clerk Li Kun, and the jinshi Wu Zongzhou all successively pleaded for his life, but because of the empress, the emperor would not accept any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Pang Pan, censor Wu Shan, Minister Zhou Jing, chief clerk Li Kun, and the jinshi Wu Zongzhou all successively pleaded for his life, but because of the empress the emperor would not accept any of it.

sentences.zh: 後竟使太監李廣杖殺鼎。

translations.literal: In the end the emperor had the eunuch Li Guang beat Ding to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor had the eunuch Li Guang beat He Ding to death with the rod.

sentences.zh: 帝追思之，賜祭勒其文於碑。

translations.literal: Later the emperor remembered him, granted sacrificial rites, and had his memorial text carved on a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor remembered him fondly, granted him posthumous sacrificial rites, and had his memorial text carved on a stele.

sentences.zh: 是時，中官多守法，奉詔出鎮者，福建鄧原、浙江麥秀、河南藍忠、宣府劉清，皆謙潔愛民。

translations.literal: At that time many palace eunuchs kept within the law; those sent out to garrison posts included Deng Yuan of Fujian, Mai Xiu of Zhejiang, Lan Zhong of Henan, and Liu Qing of Xuanfu, all of whom were modest, upright, and caring toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many palace eunuchs kept within the bounds of the law; those sent out to garrison posts included Deng Yuan in Fujian, Mai Xiu in Zhejiang, Lan Zhong in Henan, and Liu Qing in Xuanfu—all modest, upright, and caring toward the people.

sentences.zh: 兵部上其事，賜敕旌勵。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War reported their conduct, and they were rewarded with an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War reported their conduct, and they were rewarded with an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 又有司禮太監蕭敬者，歷事英宗、憲宗，諳習典故，善鼓琴。

translations.literal: There was also the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Xiao Jing, who served through the reigns of Yingzong and Chenghua, knew the precedents well, and was skilled at playing the qin.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Xiao Jing, who served through the reigns of Yingzong and Chenghua, knew the precedents thoroughly, and was skilled at playing the qin.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語劉大夏曰：「蕭敬朕所顧問，然未嘗假以權也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once told Liu Daxia: "Xiao Jing is the one I consult with, but I have never given him power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Liu Daxia: "Xiao Jing is the man I consult, yet I have never entrusted him with power.

sentences.zh: 獨李廣、蔣琮得帝寵任，後二人俱敗，而敬至世宗朝，年九十餘始卒。

translations.literal: Only Li Guang and Jiang Cong won the emperor's favor and trust; later both men fell, while Jing lived on into the time of the Jiajing Emperor and only died at more than ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Guang and Jiang Cong won the emperor's favor and trust; later both men fell, while Xiao Jing lived on into the Jiajing reign and did not die until he was more than ninety.

sentences.zh: 李廣，孝宗時太監也。

translations.literal: Li Guang was an eunuch under the Hongzhi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang was an eunuch under the Hongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 以符箓禱祀蠱帝，因為奸弊，矯旨授傳奉官，如成化間故事，四方爭納賄賂。

translations.literal: He used talismans and prayers to bewitch the emperor, then engaged in fraud and corruption, forged edicts to appoint chuanfeng officials as in the Chenghua era, and people from all quarters rushed to bribe him.
translations.idiomatic: He used talismans and prayers to bewitch the emperor, then engaged in fraud and corruption, forged edicts to appoint chuanfeng officials as in the Chenghua era, and people from all quarters rushed to bribe him.

sentences.zh: 又擅奪畿內民田，專鹽利巨萬。

translations.literal: He also seized commoner lands within the capital region and monopolized the salt profits to a vast degree.
