translations.idiomatic: He also seized commoner lands within the capital region and monopolized the salt profits to the tune of vast sums.

sentences.zh: 起大第，引玉泉山水，前後繞之。

translations.literal: He built a great mansion and drew water from Jade Spring Hill to surround it on every side.
translations.idiomatic: He built a great mansion and drew water from Jade Spring Hill to surround it on every side.

sentences.zh: 給事葉紳、御史張縉等交章論劾，帝不問。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Ye Shen and censor Zhang Jin and others repeatedly memorialized against him, but the emperor did not question it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Ye Shen, censor Zhang Jin, and others repeatedly memorialized against him, but the emperor made no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廣勸帝建毓秀亭於萬歲山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Guang urged the emperor to build Yuxiu Pavilion on Longevity Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Li Guang urged the emperor to build Yuxiu Pavilion on Longevity Hill.

sentences.zh: 亭成，幼公主殤，未幾，清寧宮災。

translations.literal: When the pavilion was finished, a young princess died, and not long after the Qingning Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: When the pavilion was finished, a young princess died; not long afterward the Qingning Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 日者言廣建亭犯歲忌，太皇太后恚曰：「今日李廣，明日李廣，果然禍及矣。」

translations.literal: The astrologers said Guang's building of the pavilion violated the year's taboos. The Grand Empress Dowager angrily said: "Today Li Guang, tomorrow Li Guang—sure enough, disaster has come of it.
translations.idiomatic: The astrologers said Li Guang's building of the pavilion had violated the year's taboos. The Grand Empress Dowager said in anger: "Today Li Guang, tomorrow Li Guang—sure enough, disaster has followed.

sentences.zh: 廣懼自殺。

translations.literal: Guang, afraid, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, terrified, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 帝疑廣有異書，使使即其家索之，得賂籍以進，多文武大臣名，饋黃白米各千百石。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Guang had secret writings and sent envoys to search his house, where they found a register of bribes to be presented, with many names of civil and military ministers, and gifts of yellow and white rice in quantities of hundreds of shi each.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Li Guang possessed secret writings and sent envoys to search his house; they found a bribe register for presentation to the throne, listing many civil and military ministers and gifts of "yellow and white rice" in quantities of hundreds of shi each.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「廣食幾何，乃受米如許。」

translations.literal: The emperor was shocked and said: "How much can Guang eat, that he would receive so much rice?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and said: "How much can Li Guang eat, that he should receive so much rice?

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「隱語耳，黃者金，白者銀也。」

translations.literal: Those around him said: "It is coded language; the yellow stands for gold and the white stands for silver."
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said: "It is coded language—yellow for gold, white for silver."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下法司究治。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and sent the case to the judicial offices for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the judicial offices to investigate and punish the matter.

sentences.zh: 諸交結廣者，走壽寧侯張鶴齡求解，乃寢勿治。

translations.literal: Those who had associated with Guang went to Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling to ask for help, and then the matter was put aside and not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had dealings with Guang went to the Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, to beg for intercession, and the case was quietly shelved.

sentences.zh: 廣初死時，司設監太監為請祠額葬祭，及是以大學士劉健等言，罷給祠額，猶賜祭。

translations.literal: When Guang first died, the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service had requested a shrine plaque and funeral rites; at this point, on the advice of Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others, the grant of a shrine plaque was canceled, though sacrificial rites were still bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang had first died, the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial had requested a shrine plaque and funeral rites for him; now, on the advice of Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others, the grant of a shrine plaque was revoked, though sacrificial offerings were still bestowed.

sentences.zh: 蔣琮，大興人。

translations.literal: Jiang Cong was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cong was a native of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，守備南京。

translations.literal: During the Xiaozong reign, he served in the Nanjing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Xiaozong, he served as garrison commander at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 沿江蘆場，舊隸三廠。

translations.literal: The reed fields along the river had formerly belonged to the three depots.
translations.idiomatic: The reed fields along the river had formerly been under the jurisdiction of the three depots.

sentences.zh: 成化初，江浦縣田多沈於江，而瀕江生沙洲六，民請耕之，以補沈江田額。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, much of the land in Jiangpu County had sunk into the river, and six sandbars had formed along the bank; the people asked to farm them in order to make up for the lost riverland quota.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, much farmland in Jiangpu County had been swallowed by the river, while six sandbars had formed along the banks; the people petitioned to cultivate them so as to make up the quota of land lost to the river.

sentences.zh: 洲與蘆場近，又瓦屑壩廢地及石城門外湖地，故不隸三廠。

translations.literal: The sandbars were near the reed fields, and so were the wasteland of Waxie Dam and the lake land outside Shicheng Gate; therefore they were not placed under the three depots.
translations.idiomatic: Those sandbars lay close to the reed fields, as did the wasteland of Waxie Dam and the lakeside land outside Shicheng Gate; for this reason they had not been placed under the three depots.

sentences.zh: 太監黃賜為守備時，受奸民獻，俱指為蘆場，盡收其利。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Huang Ci served as garrison supervisor, he accepted what wicked locals offered and called all of it reed fields, taking all the profits for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Ci served as garrison commander, he accepted what scoundrels offered him, declared all of it to be reed fields, and kept every profit for himself.

sentences.zh: 民已失業，而歲額租課仍責償之民。

translations.literal: The people had already lost their livelihood, yet the annual rent and levies were still demanded from them.
translations.idiomatic: The people had already lost their livelihoods, yet the annual rents and levies were still extracted from them.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，縣民相率醞於朝，下南京御史姜綰等覆按。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, the county people went to court in a group, and the Nanjing censors Jiang Wan and others were sent to re-examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne, the county people went up to the capital together to petition; the Nanjing censors Jiang Wan and others were dispatched to reinvestigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，綰等劾琮與民爭利，且用揭帖抗詔旨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, Wan and the others impeached Cong for competing with the people for profit and for using a memorial slip to oppose the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi, Wan and the others impeached Cong for contending with the people over profit and for using an informal memorial to defy an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 琮條辨綰疏，而泛及御史劉愷、方嶽等及南京諸司違法事。

translations.literal: Cong itemized his rebuttal to Wan's memorial and broadly implicated censor Liu Kai, Fang Yue, and the illegal conduct of the various Nanjing offices.
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied point by point to Wan's memorial and broadly dragged in censor Liu Kai, Fang Yue, and others, along with illegal conduct in the various Nanjing offices.

sentences.zh: 給事中韓重因星變請斥琮及太監郭鏞等，以弭天怒，未報。

translations.literal: Assistant secretary Han Zhong, citing a celestial anomaly, asked that Cong and eunuch Guo Yong be removed from office to appease Heaven's wrath, but no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Han Zhong, citing a celestial anomaly, asked that Cong and the eunuch Guo Yong be removed from office to appease Heaven's wrath, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 而太監陳祖生復奏戶部主事盧錦、給事中方向私種南京後湖田事。

translations.literal: Then eunuch Chen Zusheng also reported that Ministry of Revenue chief clerk Lu Jin and assistant secretary Fang Yang had privately planted crops on the Nanjing Houhu Lake land.
translations.idiomatic: Then the eunuch Chen Zusheng also reported that Ministry of Revenue chief clerk Lu Jin and assistant secretary Fang Xiang had privately cultivated land on the Houhu Lake in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 後湖者，洪武時置黃冊庫其中，令主事、給事中各一人守之，百司不得至。

translations.literal: Houhu Lake had held the Yellow Register repository since Hongwu's time; one chief clerk and one assistant secretary were assigned to guard it, and the hundred offices were forbidden to approach it.
translations.idiomatic: Houhu Lake had since Hongwu's day housed the Yellow Register archive; one chief clerk and one assistant secretary were assigned to guard it, and the rest of the bureaucracy was forbidden to enter.

sentences.zh: 歲久湖塞，錦、向於湖灘稍種蔬伐葦，給公用，故為祖生所奏。

translations.literal: Over the years the lake had silted up; Lu Jin and Fang Xiang had planted vegetables and cut reeds on the lakeshore for public use, and so Zusheng reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the lake had silted up; Lu Jin and Fang Xiang had planted vegetables and cut reeds on the lakeshore for public use, and for this Zusheng reported them.

sentences.zh: 事下南京法司。

translations.literal: The case was sent to the Nanjing judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Nanjing judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 適郭鏞奉使兩廣，道南京，往觀焉。

translations.literal: At that moment Guo Yong, on a mission to the two Guang regions, passed through Nanjing and went to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Guo Yong, on a mission to the two Guang provinces, passed through Nanjing and went to see the lake for himself.

sentences.zh: 御史纮等因劾鏞擅遊禁地。

translations.literal: Censor Jiang Wan and the others therefore impeached Yong for unlawfully entering a forbidden place for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Wan and the others therefore impeached Guo Yong for trespassing into a forbidden area for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 鏞怒，歸醞於帝，言府尹楊守隨勘錦、向失出，御史不劾奏，獨繩內臣。

translations.literal: Yong was angry and, on returning to court, reported to the emperor that prefect Yang Shunsui had mishandled the investigation of Lu Jin and Fang Xiang, that the censors had failed to impeach and report it, and that only the inner officials had been disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong was furious; on returning to court he reported to the emperor that prefect Yang Shunsui had mishandled the investigation of Lu Jin and Fang Xiang, that the censors had failed to impeach the case, and that only inner officials were being punished.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣太監何穆、大理寺少卿楊謐再勘後湖田，並覆綰、琮訐奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent eunuch He Mu and Vice Minister of the Court of Judicature Yang Mi to re-examine the Houhu Lake land case and also to review the memorials accusing Wan and Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent the eunuch He Mu and Vice Minister of the Court of Judicature Yang Mi to reinvestigate the Houhu Lake land and also to review the mutual accusations of Wan and Cong.

sentences.zh: 明年，奏上，褫錦職，謫守隨、向以下官有差。

translations.literal: The next year the report was submitted; Lu Jin was stripped of office, and Yang Shunsui, Fang Xiang, and the other officials below them were demoted by various degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The following year their report was submitted; Lu Jin was stripped of office, and Yang Shunsui, Fang Xiang, and the other officials below them were demoted by varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 又勘琮不當受獻地，私囑勘官，所訐事皆誣，綰等劾琮亦多不實，並宜逮治。

translations.literal: It was also determined that Cong should not have accepted the donated land, that he had privately instructed the investigators, that all the accusations he made were false, and that the memorials against Cong by Wan and the others were likewise mostly untrue; they should all be arrested and investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators also found that Cong ought not to have accepted donated land, that he had privately instructed the examining officials, that everything he had accused others of was false, and that the impeachments against Cong by Wan and the others were likewise mostly unfounded; all parties, they said, ought to be arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 詔逮綰等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Wan and the others be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering the arrest of Wan and the others.

sentences.zh: 御史伊宏、給事中陳矞等皆言不宜以一內臣而置御史十人於獄，不聽。

translations.literal: The censors Yi Hong and assistant secretary Chen Yu and others all said that it was improper to imprison ten censors because of one inner servant, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yi Hong, assistant secretary Chen Yu, and others all argued that it was wrong to imprison ten censors on account of one inner official, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 綰等鐫級調外，而宥琮不問。

translations.literal: Wan and the others were demoted and sent out, while Cong was pardoned and left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and the others were demoted and transferred elsewhere, while Cong was pardoned and not punished.

sentences.zh: 時劉吉竊柄，素惡南京御史劾己，故興此獄。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Ji secretly held power, and because he had long hated the Nanjing censors for impeaching him, he stirred up this case.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Ji held power behind the scenes and had long resented the Nanjing censors for impeaching him, so he stirred up this case.

sentences.zh: 尚書王恕、李敏，給事中趙竑，御史張賓先後言琮、綰同罪異罰，失平，亦不納。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Shu, Li Min, assistant secretary Zhao Hong, and censor Zhang Bin successively said that Cong and Wan should receive the same punishment and that the unequal penalties were unjust, but the emperor still would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Shu, Minister Li Min, assistant secretary Zhao Hong, and censor Zhang Bin in turn argued that Cong and Wan were guilty of the same offenses yet punished differently—that justice had not been even—but the emperor still would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 琮由是益無忌。

translations.literal: From this point on Cong became even more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Cong became all the more unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 久之，廣洋衛指揮石文通奏琮僭侈殺人，掘聚寶山傷皇陵氣，及毆殺商人諸罪。

translations.literal: After some time, Shi Wentong, commander of the Guangyang Guard, memorialized that Cong was extravagant and cruel, that he had killed people, dug into Mount Jubao and injured the imperial tomb's vital energy, and beaten and killed merchants and others.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Shi Wentong, commander of the Guangyang Guard, memorialized that Cong lived in unlawful extravagance and murdered people, that he had dug into Mount Jubao and damaged the vital energy of the imperial tombs, and that he had beaten merchants to death, among other crimes.

sentences.zh: 琮竟免死，充孝陵凈軍。

translations.literal: In the end Cong escaped death and was assigned to be a pure-duty eunuch at Xiaoling Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Cong escaped execution and was assigned to menial labor at the Xiaoling Tomb.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾，興平人。

translations.literal: Liu Jin was a man of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was a man of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 本談氏子，依中官劉姓者以進，冒其姓。

translations.literal: He was originally the son of the Tan family; he entered office by relying on an inner official surnamed Liu and took that surname himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally a son of the Tan family; he rose through the patronage of a eunuch surnamed Liu and adopted that surname as his own.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，坐法當死，得免。

translations.literal: During the Xiaozong reign he was convicted under the law and should have died, but escaped.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaozong's reign he was convicted under the law and should have been put to death, but was spared.

sentences.zh: 已，得侍武宗東宮。

translations.literal: Afterward he was able to serve the future Emperor Wuzong in the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came to serve the crown prince, the future Emperor Wuzong, in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，掌鐘鼓司，與馬永成、高鳳、羅祥、魏彬、丘聚、谷大用、張永並以舊恩得幸，人號「八虎」，而瑾尤狡狠。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he took charge of the Clock and Drum Bureau. With Ma Yongcheng, Gao Feng, Luo Xiang, Wei Bin, Qiu Ju, Gu Dayong, and Zhang Yong, all favored through old ties, he was one of the so-called Eight Tigers, and Jin in particular was sly and ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Jin took charge of the Clock and Drum Directorate. Together with Ma Yongcheng, Gao Feng, Luo Xiang, Wei Bin, Qiu Ju, Gu Dayong, and Zhang Yong—all favored for old ties—he was counted among the so-called Eight Tigers, and Jin in particular was sly and ruthless.

sentences.zh: 嘗慕王振之為人，日進鷹犬、歌舞、角觝之戲，導帝微行。

translations.literal: He used to admire the way Wang Zhen behaved, and every day he introduced hawks, dogs, singing, dancing, and wrestling to lead the emperor into secret outings.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the example of Wang Zhen and every day introduced hawks and hounds, singing and dancing, and wrestling bouts to the emperor, leading him into secret outings.

sentences.zh: 帝大歡樂之，漸信用瑾，進內官監，總督團營。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly delighted by it, gradually trusted Jin, promoted him to the Inner Office Directorate, and put him in overall command of the group armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in these diversions, gradually placed his trust in Jin, promoted him to the Inner Palace Directorate, and put him in overall command of the regimented armies.

sentences.zh: 孝宗遺詔罷中官監槍及各城門監局，瑾皆格不行，而勸帝令內臣鎮守者各貢萬金。

translations.literal: Xiaozong's deathbed edict abolished the gun corps of the Inner Palace Directorate and the supervisory offices at each city gate; Jin blocked every provision from being carried out and instead urged the emperor to require every eunuch serving as garrison commander to pay tribute of ten thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong's deathbed edict abolished the gun corps of the Inner Palace Directorate and the supervisory offices at each city gate; Jin blocked every provision from being carried out and instead urged the emperor to require every eunuch serving as garrison commander to pay tribute of ten thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 又奏置皇莊，漸增至三百餘所，畿內大擾。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to establish imperial estates, which in time grew to more than three hundred, throwing the capital region into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to establish imperial estates, which in time grew to more than three hundred, throwing the capital region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 外廷知八人誘帝遊宴，大學士劉健、謝遷、李東陽驟諫，不聽。

translations.literal: When the outer court learned that the Eight were luring the emperor into pleasure outings and banquets, Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang remonstrated urgently, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the outer court learned that the Eight were luring the emperor into pleasure outings and banquets, Grand Secretaries Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang remonstrated urgently, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尚書張升，給事中陶諧、胡煜、楊一瑛、張襘，御史王渙、趙佑，南京給事御史李光翰、陸昆等，交章論諫，亦不聽。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Sheng, assistant secretaries Tao Xie, Hu Yu, Yang Yiying, and Zhang Gui, censors Wang Huan and Zhao You, and the Nanjing remonstrance officials Li Guanghan, Lu Kun, and others submitted one memorial after another, but again he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Sheng, assistant secretaries Tao Xie, Hu Yu, Yang Yiying, and Zhang Gui, censors Wang Huan and Zhao You, and the Nanjing remonstrance officials Li Guanghan, Lu Kun, and others submitted one memorial after another, but again he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 五官監候楊源以星變陳言，帝意頗動。

translations.literal: Yang Yuan, a registrar of the Five Offices, memorialized on the basis of a celestial anomaly, and the emperor's mind was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan, a registrar of the Five Offices, memorialized on account of a celestial anomaly, and the emperor was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 健、遷等復連疏請誅瑾，戶部尚書韓文率諸大臣繼之。

translations.literal: Jian and Qian and the others again sent repeated memorials asking that Jin be executed, and the Minister of Revenue Han Wen led the other ministers in following suit.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Qian and the others again sent repeated memorials calling for Jin's execution, and Han Wen, the Minister of Revenue, led the rest of the ministers in pressing the same request.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，使司禮太監陳寬、李榮、王嶽至閣，議遣瑾等居南京。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice, so he sent the eunuchs Chen Kuan, Li Rong, and Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonial to the Grand Secretariat to discuss sending Jin and the others to live in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice, so he sent the eunuchs Chen Kuan, Li Rong, and Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonial to the Grand Secretariat to discuss sending Jin and the others to live in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三反，健等執不可。

translations.literal: After it had been rejected three times, Jian and the others still insisted that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds of rejection, Jian and the others still insisted that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 尚書許進曰：「過激將有變。」

translations.literal: Minister Xu Jin said, 'If you push this too hard, there will be trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Jin warned, 'If you push this too hard, there will be trouble.

sentences.zh: 健不從。

translations.literal: Jian would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 王嶽者，素謇直，與太監範亨、徐智心嫉八人，具以健等語告帝，且言閣臣議是。

translations.literal: Wang Yue was a man of habitual frankness and rectitude, and together with the eunuchs Fan Heng and Xu Zhi, who all hated those eight men, he reported Jian and the others' words in full to the emperor and said that the Grand Secretariat had approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had always been straightforward and upright. Together with the eunuchs Fan Heng and Xu Zhi, all of whom hated the eight men, he reported Jian and the others' words to the emperor in full and said the Grand Secretariat had agreed.

sentences.zh: 健等方約文及諸九卿詰朝伏闕面爭，而吏部尚書焦芳馳白瑾。

translations.literal: Jian and the others were just arranging with Han Wen and the other Nine Ministers to kneel at the palace gate at dawn and argue face to face, when the Minister of Personnel Jiao Fang hurried off to report to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and the others were just arranging with Han Wen and the other Nine Ministers to kneel at the palace gate at dawn and confront him in person, when the Minister of Personnel Jiao Fang hurried to report to Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾大懼，夜率永成等伏帝前環泣。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly afraid, and that night he led Yongcheng and the others to kneel before the emperor and weep all around him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was terrified, and that night he led Yongcheng and the others to kneel before the emperor and cry around him.

sentences.zh: 帝心動，瑾因曰：「害奴等者王嶽。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was moved, and Jin then said, 'The one harming us slaves is Wang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved, and Jin then said, 'The one harming your slaves is Wang Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶽結閣臣欲制上出入，故先去所忌耳。

translations.literal: Yue had tied himself to the Grand Secretariat and wanted to control the emperor's comings and goings, so he had first to remove those he feared.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had aligned himself with the Grand Secretariat and wanted to control the emperor's movements, so he was first trying to remove those he disliked.

sentences.zh: 且鷹犬何損萬幾。

translations.literal: Besides, what harm could hawks and hounds do to the great affairs of state?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, how could mere hawks and hounds harm the great affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 若司禮監得人，左班官安敢如是。」

translations.literal: If the Directorate of Ceremonial had the right man, how would the officials on the left dare act like this?
translations.idiomatic: If the Directorate of Ceremonial had the right man, how would the officials on the left dare act like this?

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，立命瑾掌司禮監，永成掌東廠，大用掌西廠，而夜收嶽及亨、智充南京凈軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and at once ordered Jin to head the Directorate of Ceremonial, Yongcheng to head the Eastern Depot, and Dayong to head the Western Depot, and that night had Yue and Heng and Zhi arrested and consigned to the Nanjing eunuch corps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and at once ordered Jin to head the Directorate of Ceremonial, Yongcheng to head the Eastern Depot, and Dayong to head the Western Depot, and that night had Yue and Heng and Zhi arrested and consigned to the Nanjing eunuch corps.

sentences.zh: 旦日諸臣入朝，將伏闕，知事已變，於是健、東陽皆求去。

translations.literal: The next day the ministers came to court, intending to kneel at the palace gate, but when they learned the matter had changed, Jian and Dongyang both asked to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the ministers came to court intending to kneel at the palace gate, but when they learned the situation had changed, Jian and Dongyang both asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 帝獨留東陽，而令焦芳入閣，追殺嶽、亨於途，箠智折臂。

translations.literal: The emperor kept Dongyang alone, and ordered Jiao Fang into the Grand Secretariat, while men were sent after Yue and Heng and killed them on the road, and Zhi was beaten until his arm broke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept Dongyang alone, and ordered Jiao Fang into the Grand Secretariat, while men were sent after Yue and Heng and killed them on the road, and Zhi was beaten until his arm broke.

sentences.zh: 時正德元年十月也。

translations.literal: This was the tenth month of the first year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: This was the tenth month of Zhengde's first year.

sentences.zh: 瑾既得志，遂以事革韓文職，而杖責請留健、遷者給事中呂翀、劉郤及南京給事中戴銑等六人，御史薄彥徽等十五人。

translations.literal: Once Jin had his way, he used the matter to remove Han Wen from office, and beat and punished the six men who had petitioned to keep Jian and Qian, including the giving-attendance officials Lü Chong and Liu Que and the Nanjing giving-attendance officials Dai Xian and the others, as well as fifteen censors such as Bo Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin had his way, he used the matter to remove Han Wen from office and beat the six men who had petitioned to keep Jian and Qian, including the giving-attendance officials Lü Chong and Liu Que and the Nanjing giving-attendance officials Dai Xian and the others, as well as fifteen censors such as Bo Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 守備南京武靖伯趙承慶、府尹陸珩、尚書林瀚，皆以傳翀、郤疏得罪，珩、瀚勒致仕，削承慶半祿。

translations.literal: The Nanjing garrison commander, Earl of Wujing Zhao Chengqing, the prefect Lu Heng, and Minister Lin Han were all implicated because of memorials by Chong and Que; Heng and Han were forced to retire, and Chengqing's stipend was cut in half.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing garrison commander, Earl of Wujing Zhao Chengqing, the prefect Lu Heng, and Minister Lin Han were all implicated because of memorials by Chong and Que; Heng and Han were forced to retire, and Chengqing's stipend was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 南京副都御史陳壽，御史陳琳、王良臣，主事王守仁，復以救銑等謫杖有差。

translations.literal: The deputy Censor-in-chief Chen Shou of Nanjing, the censors Chen Lin and Wang Liangchen, and the principal secretary Wang Shouren were again punished by beating and demotion in varying degrees for having tried to save Xian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy Censor-in-chief Chen Shou of Nanjing, the censors Chen Lin and Wang Liangchen, and the principal secretary Wang Shouren were again punished by beating and demotion in varying degrees for having tried to save Xian and the others.

sentences.zh: 瑾勢日益張，毛舉官僚細過，散布校尉，遠近偵伺，使人救過不贍。

translations.literal: Jin's power grew stronger by the day. He picked out the smallest faults in officials, spread his junior guards out to spy near and far, and made it impossible for people to repair their own mistakes.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's power grew stronger by the day. He picked out the smallest faults in officials, spread his junior guards out to spy near and far, and made it impossible for people to repair their own mistakes.

sentences.zh: 因顓擅威福，悉遣黨閹分鎮各邊。

translations.literal: He thus monopolized power and favor and sent all his eunuch followers to be stationed at the various frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He thus monopolized power and favor and sent all his eunuch followers to be stationed at the various frontiers.

sentences.zh: 敘大同功，遷擢官校至一千五百六十餘人，又傳旨授錦衣官數百員。

translations.literal: For his achievements at Datong, more than 1,560 officers and guards were promoted, and an imperial order also appointed several hundred Brocade Guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements at Datong, more than 1,560 officers and guards were promoted, and an imperial order also appointed several hundred Brocade Guard officers.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒纂要》成，瑾誣諸翰林纂修官謄寫不謹，皆被譴，而命文華殿書辦官張駿等改謄，超拜官秩。

translations.literal: When the Compendium of Governance was completed, Jin falsely accused the Hanlin compilation officers of careless copying, and they were all reprimanded, while the palace copyist Zhang Jun and others were ordered to recopy it and were promoted far beyond their rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Compendium of Governance was completed, Jin falsely accused the Hanlin compilers of careless copying; they were all punished, while copyists Zhang Jun and others were ordered to recopy the work and were promoted far above their station.

sentences.zh: 駿由光祿卿擢禮部尚書，他授京卿者數人，裝潢匠役悉授官。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was promoted from Guanglu Minister to Minister of Rites; several others who had been given the rank of metropolitan minister were also elevated, and the craftsmen and attendants who did the finishing work were all granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was raised from Minister of Imperial Entertainments to Minister of Rites; several others were given metropolitan ministerial ranks as well, and even the craftsmen who bound the volumes were granted official posts.

sentences.zh: 創用枷法，給事中吉時，御史王時中，郎中劉繹、張瑋，尚寶卿顧璿，副使姚祥，參議吳廷舉等，並摭小過，枷瀕死，始釋而戍之。

translations.literal: He introduced the cangue punishment. Assistant secretary Ji Shi, censor Wang Shizhong, the langzhong Liu Yi and Zhang Wei, Shangbao minister Gu Xuan, vice commissioner Yao Xiang, and councilor Wu Tingju were all seized for small offenses, cangued nearly to death, and only then released and sent to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced the cangue. Assistant secretary Ji Shi, censor Wang Shizhong, the secretaries Liu Yi and Zhang Wei, Minister of Credentials Gu Xuan, vice commissioner Yao Xiang, and councilor Wu Tingju were all seized on petty grounds, cangued almost to death, and only then released and sent to border garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 其餘枷死者無數。

translations.literal: Countless others died under the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others died under the cangue as well.

sentences.zh: 錦衣獄徽纆相屬。

translations.literal: The Brocade Guard prisons were packed with shackles and cords.
translations.idiomatic: The prisons of the Brocade Guard were crowded with shackled prisoners one after another.

sentences.zh: 惡錦衣僉事牟斌善視獄囚，杖而錮之。

translations.literal: Because he disliked Brocade Guard assistant commissioner Mou Bin for treating prisoners well, he had him beaten and confined.
translations.idiomatic: Because he hated Brocade Guard assistant commissioner Mou Bin for treating prisoners humanely, he had him beaten and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 府丞周璽、五官監候楊源杖至死。

translations.literal: The prefectural vice magistrate Zhou Xi and the Five Offices registrar Yang Yuan were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural vice magistrate Zhou Xi and the Five Offices registrar Yang Yuan were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 源初以皇變陳言，罪瑾者也。

translations.literal: Yang had originally memorialized about a celestial anomaly to accuse Jin; he was one of those who had denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had originally taken advantage of a celestial anomaly to speak out against Jin; he was precisely one of those who had denounced him.

sentences.zh: 瑾每奏事，必偵帝為戲弄時。

translations.literal: Whenever Jin came to report on affairs, he first ascertained when the emperor was at play.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jin had business to report, he first found out when the emperor was occupied with amusement.

sentences.zh: 帝厭之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew tired of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of this.

sentences.zh: 亟麾去曰：「吾用若何事，乃混我！」

translations.literal: He quickly waved him away, saying: "I use you for what purpose, and yet you muddle me!
translations.idiomatic: He would wave him away at once, saying, "What do I keep you for—only to confuse me!

sentences.zh: 自此遂專決，不復白。

translations.literal: From that point Jin decided matters entirely on his own and no longer reported them to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jin made decisions on his own and no longer sought the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，瑾召群臣跪金水橋南，宣示奸黨，大臣則大學士劉健、謝遷，尚書則韓文、楊守隨、張敷華、林瀚，部曹則郎中李夢陽，主事王守仁、王綸、孫磐、黃昭，詞臣則檢討劉瑞，言路則給事中湯禮敬、陳霆、徐昂、陶諧、劉郤、艾洪、呂翀、任惠、李光翰、戴銑、徐蕃、牧相、徐暹、張良弼、葛嵩、趙士賢，御史陳琳、貢安甫、史良佐、曹閔、王弘、任諾、李熙、王蕃、葛浩、陸昆、張鳴鳳、蕭乾元、姚學禮、黃昭道、蔣欽、薄彥徽、潘鏜、王良臣、趙佑、何天衢、徐玨、楊璋、熊卓、朱廷聲、劉玉等，皆海內號忠直者也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Jin summoned the ministers to kneel south of the Jinshui Bridge and announced the treacherous faction: the grand secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian; the ministers Han Wen, Yang Shunsui, Zhang Fuhua, and Lin Han; the ministry officials, including the langzhong Li Mengyang and the chief clerks Wang Shouren, Wang Lun, Sun Pan, Huang Zhao, and others; the literary officials, including the compiler Liu Rui; the remonstrance officials, including assistant secretaries Tang Lijing, Chen Ting, Xu Ang, Tao Xie, Liu Qie, Ai Hong, Lü Chong, Ren Hui, Li Guanghan, Dai Xian, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Xu Xian, Zhang Liangbi, Ge Song, and Zhao Shixian; and the censors Chen Lin, Gong Anfu, Shi Liangzuo, Cao Min, Wang Hong, Ren Nuo, Li Xi, Wang Fan, Ge Hao, Lu Kun, Zhang Mingfeng, Xiao Qianyuan, Yao Xueli, Huang Zhaodao, Jiang Qin, Bo Yanhui, Pan Tang, Wang Liangchen, Zhao You, He Tianqu, Xu Jue, Yang Zhang, Xiong Zhuo, Zhu Tingsheng, Liu Yu, and others, all of whom were known throughout the empire as loyal and upright men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, Jin summoned the ministers to kneel south of the Jinshui Bridge and proclaimed the treacherous faction: among the grand secretaries, Liu Jian and Xie Qian; among the ministers, Han Wen, Yang Shunsui, Zhang Fuhua, and Lin Han; among the ministry officials, the secretary Li Mengyang and chief clerks Wang Shouren, Wang Lun, Sun Pan, Huang Zhao, and others; among the literary officials, the compiler Liu Rui; among the remonstrance officials, assistant secretaries Tang Lijing, Chen Ting, Xu Ang, Tao Xie, Liu Qie, Ai Hong, Lü Chong, Ren Hui, Li Guanghan, Dai Xian, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Xu Xian, Zhang Liangbi, Ge Song, Zhao Shixian, and the censors Chen Lin, Gong Anfu, Shi Liangzuo, Cao Min, Wang Hong, Ren Nuo, Li Xi, Wang Fan, Ge Hao, Lu Kun, Zhang Mingfeng, Xiao Qianyuan, Yao Xueli, Huang Zhaodao, Jiang Qin, Bo Yanhui, Pan Tang, Wang Liangchen, Zhao You, He Tianqu, Xu Jue, Yang Zhang, Xiong Zhuo, Zhu Tingsheng, Liu Yu, and others—men famed throughout the empire for their loyalty and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 又令六科寅入酉出，使不得息，以困苦之。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Six Departments to enter at the hour of yin and leave at the hour of you, denying them rest and wearing them down.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Six Departments to enter at the yin hour and leave at the you hour, denying them rest in order to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 令文臣毋輒予封誥，痛繩文吏。

translations.literal: He ordered that civil officials were not to be granted seals and patents at random, and he harshly restrained the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade civil officials from receiving seals and patents at will and harshly disciplined the clerical staff.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠圖不軌，賂瑾求復護衛，瑾予之，濠反謀遂成。

translations.literal: When Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao plotted rebellion, he bribed Jin and asked to have his guards restored; Jin granted it, and Chenhao's later revolt was then fully set in motion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning, Zhu Chenhao, plotted rebellion, he bribed Jin to have his guard restored; Jin granted it, and Chenhao's revolt thereafter took shape.

sentences.zh: 瑾不學，每批答章奏，皆持歸私第，與妹婿禮部司務孫聰、華亭大猾張文冕相參決，辭率鄙冗，焦芳為潤色之，東陽頫首而已。

translations.literal: Jin was unlearned; whenever he annotated memorials and reports, he carried them back to his private residence and discussed them with his brother-in-law Sun Cong, a clerk in the Ministry of Rites, and with Zhang Wenmian, a great rogue of Huating. His language was crude and clumsy, so Jiao Fang polished it, and Dongyang could only bow his head and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was unlettered; whenever he drafted responses to memorials he took them home to his private residence and settled them in consultation with his brother-in-law Sun Cong, a clerk in the Ministry of Rites, and Zhang Wenmian, a notorious scoundrel of Huating. His wording was crude and verbose, so Jiao Fang polished it, while Li Dongyang could only bow his head in assent.

sentences.zh: 當是時，瑾權擅天下，威福任情。

translations.literal: At that time Jin held power over the whole realm and dispensed favor and punishment as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Jin wielded sole power over the empire, dispensing favor and punishment entirely as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 有罪人溺水死，乃坐御史匡翼之罪。

translations.literal: When a criminal drowned and died, the blame was placed on the censor Kuang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When a criminal drowned, the censor Kuang Yizhi was punished for it.

sentences.zh: 嘗求學士吳儼賄，不得，又聽都御史劉宇讒，怒御史楊南金，乃以大計外吏奏中，落二人職。

translations.literal: He once sought a bribe from the scholar Wu Yan and got none; then, listening to the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he became angry with the censor Yang Nanjin and used the annual evaluation of outside officials to have the two of them removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He once demanded a bribe from academician Wu Yan and did not get it; then, heeding the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he turned on censor Yang Nanjin and, in the annual evaluation of outside officials, had both men removed from office.

sentences.zh: 授播州土司楊斌為四川按察使。

translations.literal: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chief of Bozhou, as Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chieftain of Bozhou, surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 令奴婿閭潔督山東學政。

translations.literal: He ordered his son-in-law Lü Jie to supervise the school administration of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He put his son-in-law Lü Jie in charge of the school administration of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 公侯勛戚以下，莫敢鈞禮，每私謁，相率跪拜。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, meritorious officers, and relatives by marriage all dared not insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they all knelt and bowed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes, marquises, meritorious nobles, and imperial in-laws downward, none dared insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they knelt and bowed in succession.

sentences.zh: 章奏先具紅揭投瑾，號紅本，然後上通政司，號白本，皆稱劉太監而不名。

translations.literal: Memorials had first to be prepared as red slips and submitted to Jin, known as the red memorials; only then were they sent on to the Court of State Affairs as white memorials. In all cases he was called Eunuch Liu and not by name.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials had first to be prepared on red paper and submitted to Jin—the "red memorials"—and only afterward sent on to the Directorate of Communications as "white memorials"; everywhere he was addressed as Eunuch Liu, never by name.

sentences.zh: 都察院奏讞誤名瑾，瑾怒詈之，都御史屠滽率屬跪謝乃已。

translations.literal: When the Censorate referred to Jin by name in a judgment report, Jin cursed them in anger, and Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate named Jin in a judgment report by mistake, he flew into a rage and cursed them; Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he would let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 遣使察核邊倉，都御史周南、張鼐、馬中錫、湯全、劉憲，布政以下官孫祿、冒政、方矩、華福、金獻民、劉遜、郭緒、張翼，郎中劉繹、王藎等，並以赦前罪，下獄追補邊粟，憲至瘐死。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to inspect the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with the provincial officials Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and the ministry officials Liu Yi, Wang Jin, and others, were all imprisoned for crimes supposedly covered by amnesty and made to repay border grain; Xian died in prison of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to audit the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with provincial administrators Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and secretaries Liu Yi and Wang Jin, were all imprisoned on pre-amnesty offenses and forced to make restitution in border grain; Liu Xian died of illness in prison.

sentences.zh: 又察鹽課，杖巡鹽御史王潤，逮前運使寧舉、楊奇等。

translations.literal: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged the salt-surveillance censor Wang Run, and arrested the former transport commissioners Ning Ju and Yang Qi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged salt censor Wang Run, and arrested former transport commissioners Ning Ju, Yang Qi, and others.

sentences.zh: 察內甲字庫，謫尚書王佐以下百七十三人。

translations.literal: He inspected the Inner Armor Character Treasury and demoted 173 people, including Minister Wang Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the Inner Armor and Character Treasury and demoted one hundred seventy-three officials, including Minister Wang Zuo.

sentences.zh: 復創罰米法，嘗忤瑾者，皆擿發輸邊。

translations.literal: He also invented the penalty of grain fines again; anyone who had offended Jin was all exposed and sent to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He revived the penalty of grain fines as well; anyone who had ever offended Jin was hunted out and made to deliver grain to the border.

sentences.zh: 故尚書雍泰、馬文升、劉大夏、韓文、許進，都御史楊一清、李進、王忠，侍郎張縉，給事中趙士賢，任良弼，御史張津，陳順、喬恕、聶賢、曹來旬等數十人悉破家，死者繫其妻孥。

translations.literal: Thus ministers such as Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Ministers Zhang Jin; Assistant Secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens of others all lost their homes, and those who died left their wives and children bound up with them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus former ministers Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Minister Zhang Jin; assistant secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens more were ruined; where the accused died, their wives and children were held liable as well.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，御道有匿名書詆瑾所行事，瑾矯旨召百官跪奉天門下。

translations.literal: That summer, an anonymous letter was found on the imperial road attacking Jin's conduct, and Jin forged an edict summoning all the officials to kneel below Fengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That summer an anonymous placard attacking Jin's conduct appeared along the imperial avenue; Jin forged an edict summoning all officials to kneel beneath Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 瑾立門左詰責，日暮收五品以下官盡下獄。

translations.literal: Jin stood at the left side of the gate and interrogated them; by evening he had all the officials of fifth rank and below taken into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stood at the left of the gate and interrogated them; by evening every official of fifth rank and below had been thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 明日，大學士李東陽申救，瑾亦微聞此書乃內臣所為，始釋諸臣。

translations.literal: The next day Grand Secretary Li Dongyang spoke up in their defense, and Jin also heard faintly that the letter had been written by inner officials, so he finally released the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Grand Secretary Li Dongyang pleaded for them; Jin also heard faintly that the placard had been written by inner officials, and at last he released the ministers.

sentences.zh: 而主事何釴、順天推官周臣、進士陸伸已暍死。

translations.literal: But the chief clerk He Yi, the magistrate of Shuntian, Zhou Chen, and the jinshi Lu Shen had already died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: But chief clerk He Yi, Shuntian magistrate Zhou Chen, and jinshi Lu Shen had already died of heatstroke.

sentences.zh: 是日酷暑，太監李榮以冰瓜啖群臣，瑾惡之。

translations.literal: That day was oppressively hot; the eunuch Li Rong offered iced melons to the ministers, and Jin disliked it.
translations.idiomatic: The day was fiercely hot; the eunuch Li Rong offered the ministers iced melons, and Jin resented it.

sentences.zh: 太監黃偉憤甚，謂諸臣曰：「書所言皆為國為民事，挺身自承，雖死不失為好男子，奈何枉累他人。」

translations.literal: The eunuch Huang Wei was furious and said to the ministers: "What the letter says is all for the state and the people. To step forward and take responsibility, even if one dies, is still the conduct of a good man. How can you falsely implicate others?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huang Wei was incensed and said to the ministers, "Everything written in that placard concerned the state and the people. To step forward and confess, even at the cost of your lives, would not dishonor you as men—but how can you falsely implicate others?

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，即日勒榮閑住，而逐偉南京。

translations.literal: Jin was enraged, immediately ordered Rong to stand aside, and banished Wei to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious; that same day he forced Li Rong into retirement and banished Huang Wei to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時東廠、西廠緝事人四出，道路惶懼。

translations.literal: At that time the investigators of the East and West Depots were spread everywhere, and the roads were filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the investigators of the Eastern and Western Depots ranged everywhere, and terror filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 瑾復立內行廠，尤酷烈，中人以微法，無得全者。

translations.literal: Jin also established an Internal Operating Depot, even more cruel and fierce; anyone who was caught by a minor offense was never let go whole.
translations.idiomatic: Jin established an Internal Operating Depot as well, more cruel still; no one caught in even a minor offense escaped whole.

sentences.zh: 又悉逐京師客傭，令寡婦盡嫁，喪不葬者焚之，輦下洶洶幾致亂。

translations.literal: He also expelled all hired laborers from the capital, ordered all widows to remarry, and burned the bodies of those whose burials had not been completed; the capital seethed and nearly fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He also drove every hired laborer out of the capital, ordered all widows to remarry, and burned the unburied dead; the capital seethed and nearly descended into disorder.

sentences.zh: 都給事中許天錫欲劾瑾，懼弗克，懷疏自縊。

translations.literal: The chief secretary of the capital administration, Xu Tianxi, wanted to impeach Jin but feared he would fail, so he kept the memorial with him and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chief assistant secretary Xu Tianxi wished to impeach Jin but feared he would fail; he kept the memorial on his person and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 瑾故急賄，凡入覲、出使官皆有厚獻。

translations.literal: Jin was especially eager for bribes; all officials who came to pay respects at court or were sent on missions had to make lavish offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was insatiably greedy for bribes; every official arriving for audience or departing on mission was expected to make a lavish gift.

sentences.zh: 給事中周鑰勘事歸，以無金自殺。

translations.literal: Assistant secretary Zhou Yao returned from investigating a case and killed himself because he had no money.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Zhou Yao returned from an investigatory mission and killed himself because he had no gold to offer.

sentences.zh: 其黨張綵曰：「今天下所饋遺公者，非必皆私財，往往貸京師，而歸則以庫金償。

translations.literal: His faction Zhang Cai said: "These gifts brought to you from across the realm are not necessarily all personal funds; often they are borrowed in the capital and repaid with treasury money on the return trip.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Zhang Cai said, "What the realm sends you is not always private wealth; often they borrow in the capital and repay from treasury funds on the road home.

sentences.zh: 公奈何斂怨貽患。」

translations.literal: Why bring hatred on yourself and breed trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Why heap up resentment and store up disaster for yourself?

sentences.zh: 瑾然之。

translations.literal: Jin agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin thought he had a point.

sentences.zh: 會御史歐陽雲等十餘人以故事入賂，瑾皆舉發致罪。

translations.literal: When censors Ouyang Yun and more than ten others entered with bribes as usual, Jin exposed them all and brought them to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When censors Ouyang Yun and more than ten others presented bribes as custom required, Jin exposed them all and brought them to punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃遣給事、御史十四人分道盤察，有司爭厚斂以補帑。

translations.literal: He then sent fourteen assistant secretaries and censors out along different routes to inspect and seize, and the officials there all competed in heavy exactions to make up the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched fourteen assistant secretaries and censors along different routes to audit and seize assets, and local officials vied to levy heavy taxes to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 所遣人率阿瑾意，專務搏擊，劾尚書顧佐、侶鐘、韓文以下數十人。

translations.literal: The men he sent all catered to Jin's wishes and focused on striking at others; they impeached ministers such as Gu Zuo, Lü Zhong, and Han Wen and dozens more.
translations.idiomatic: Those he sent invariably carried out Jin's wishes and devoted themselves to prosecutions; they impeached Ministers Gu Zuo, Lü Zhong, Han Wen, and dozens more.

sentences.zh: 浙江鹽運使楊奇逋課死，至鬻其女孫。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang salt transport commissioner Yang Qi fell into arrears on the quota and died, and even his daughter and granddaughter were sold off.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang salt transport commissioner Yang Qi fell behind in his quota, died under the pressure, and even his daughter and granddaughter were sold off.

sentences.zh: 而給事中安奎、潘希曾，御史趙時中、阮吉、張彧、劉子厲，以無重劾下獄。

translations.literal: Assistant secretaries An Kui and Pan Xizeng, and censors Zhao Shizhong, Ruan Ji, Zhang Yu, and Liu Zili, were all imprisoned for not making a heavy enough accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretaries An Kui and Pan Xizeng and censors Zhao Shizhong, Ruan Ji, Zhang Yu, and Liu Zili were imprisoned for failing to bring serious charges.

sentences.zh: 奎、彧枷且死，李東陽疏救，始釋為民。

translations.literal: Kui and Yu were cangued until they nearly died; only after Li Dongyang memorialized in their defense were they released to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An Kui and Zhang Yu were cangued nearly to death; only after Li Dongyang memorialized in their defense were they released as commoners.

sentences.zh: 希曾等亦皆杖斥，忤意者謫斥有差。

translations.literal: Pan Xizeng and the others were also beaten and dismissed, and those who offended Jin's wishes were demoted in various degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xizeng and the others were also beaten and dismissed, and those who displeased Jin were demoted to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 又矯旨籍故都御史錢鉞、禮部侍郎黃景、尚書秦纮家。

translations.literal: He also forged an edict to confiscate the homes of former Grand Censor Qian Yue, Minister of Rites Huang Jing, and Minister Qin Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged an edict to confiscate the estates of former Grand Censor Qian Yue, Vice Minister of Rites Huang Jing, and Minister Qin Hong.

sentences.zh: 凡瑾所逮捕，一家犯，鄰里皆坐，或瞰河居者，以河外居民坐之。

translations.literal: Anyone Jin seized was treated as guilty together with his neighbors if one household offended; if someone lived by the river bank, he was counted together with those living beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: In every arrest Jin ordered, one household's offense implicated the neighbors; if someone lived facing the river, those on the far bank were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 屢起大獄，冤號遍道路。

translations.literal: He repeatedly stirred up major cases, and cries of injustice filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly opened great criminal cases, and cries of injustice rang along every road.

sentences.zh: 《孝宗實錄》成，翰林預纂修者當遷秩，瑾惡翰林官素不下己，調侍講吳一鵬等十六人南京六部。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong were completed, the Hanlin editors who had taken part were supposed to be promoted, but Jin disliked the Hanlin officials for always looking down on him, so he transferred sixteen men including lecturer Wu Yipeng to the Nanjing ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong were completed, the Hanlin compilers who had taken part were due for promotion; Jin, who resented the Hanlin for never deferring to him, transferred sixteen of them, including lecturer Wu Yipeng, to the Nanjing ministries.

sentences.zh: 是時，內閣焦芳、劉宇，吏部尚書張綵，兵部尚書曹元，錦衣衛指揮楊玉、石文義，皆為瑾腹心。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretariat members Jiao Fang and Liu Yu, Minister of Personnel Zhang Cai, Minister of War Cao Yuan, and Brocade Guard commanders Yang Yu and Shi Wenyin were all Jin's trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Secretariat members Jiao Fang and Liu Yu, Minister of Personnel Zhang Cai, Minister of War Cao Yuan, and Brocade Guard commanders Yang Yu and Shi Wenyin were all Jin's trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 變更舊制，令天下巡撫入京受敕，輸瑾賂。

translations.literal: He changed the old system and made all provincial governors come to the capital to receive edicts and hand over bribes to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He altered the old system, requiring every provincial governor to come to the capital to receive edicts and pay bribes to Jin.

sentences.zh: 延綏巡撫劉宇不至，逮下獄。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, governor of Yansui, failed to appear and was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, governor of Yansui, failed to appear and was arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 宣府巡撫陸完後至，幾得罪，既賂，乃令試職視事。

translations.literal: Lu Wan, governor of Xuanfu, arrived later and nearly incurred punishment; after bribing them, he was allowed to take office and act in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan, governor of Xuanfu, arrived late and nearly fell under punishment; after paying a bribe, he was allowed to resume office on probation.

sentences.zh: 都指揮以下求遷者，瑾第書片紙曰「某授某官」，兵部即奉行，不敢復奏。

translations.literal: When guard commanders and those below sought promotion, Jin would merely write a note saying, 'So-and-so is granted such-and-such office,' and the Ministry of War would carry it out without daring to report again.
translations.idiomatic: When guard commanders and those below sought promotion, Jin need only write a slip saying, "So-and-so is granted such-and-such an office," and the Ministry of War would carry it out without daring to memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 邊將失律，賂入，即不問，有反升擢者。

translations.literal: If border generals failed in discipline but paid bribes, nothing would be done; some were even promoted.
translations.idiomatic: If frontier generals broke discipline but paid bribes, no action was taken; some were even promoted instead.

sentences.zh: 又遣其黨丈邊塞屯地，誅求苛刻。

translations.literal: He also sent his faction to measure the frontier garrisons and camps, demanding and extorting with extreme harshness.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his followers to survey frontier garrison lands and extort payments with merciless severity.

sentences.zh: 邊軍不堪，焚公廨，守臣諭之始定。

translations.literal: The frontier troops could not endure it, burned the government offices, and only calmed down after the local commanders persuaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier troops could bear it no longer and burned the government offices; only when local commanders reasoned with them did the unrest subside.

sentences.zh: 給事中高淓丈滄州，所劾治六十一人，至劾其父高銓以媚瑾。

translations.literal: Assistant secretary Gao Qing surveyed Cangzhou, and among the sixty-one people he impeached, he even impeached his own father Gao Quan to curry favor with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Gao Qing surveyed Cangzhou and impeached sixty-one people, even denouncing his own father Gao Quan to curry favor with Jin.

sentences.zh: 又以謝遷故，令餘姚人毋授京官。

translations.literal: Because of Xie Qian, he ordered that people from Yuyao were not to be appointed to court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xie Qian, he barred natives of Yuyao from appointment to metropolitan office.

sentences.zh: 以占城國使人亞劉謀逆獄，裁江西鄉試額五十名，仍禁授京秩如餘姚，以焦芳惡彭華故也。

translations.literal: In the treason case involving the Champa envoy A Liu, he cut the quota for the Jiangxi provincial examination by fifty names and still forbade appointment to court office just as he had for Yuyao; this was because Jiao Fang hated Peng Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the treason case involving the Champa envoy A Liu, he cut Jiangxi's provincial examination quota by fifty places and likewise barred appointment to metropolitan rank as he had for Yuyao—this because Jiao Fang hated Peng Hua.

sentences.zh: 瑾又自增陜西鄉試額至百名，亦為芳增河南額至九十五名，以優其鄉士。

translations.literal: Jin also raised the Shaanxi provincial examination quota to one hundred, and likewise had Fang increase the Henan quota to ninety-five, to favor men from his own region.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also raised Shaanxi's provincial quota to one hundred and had Fang increase Henan's to ninety-five, to favor men from their home regions.

sentences.zh: 其年，帝大赦，瑾峻刑自如。

translations.literal: That year the emperor issued a general amnesty, but Jin continued his harsh punishments as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty, yet Jin continued his harsh punishments as before.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書劉璟無所彈劾，瑾詬之。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Liu Jing failed to find anything to impeach, and Jin cursed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Liu Jing found nothing to impeach, and Jin reviled him for it.

sentences.zh: 璟懼，劾其屬王尚賓等三人，乃喜。

translations.literal: Liu Jing was frightened and impeached three of his own subordinates, Wang Shangbin and others, and Jin was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing, in fear, impeached three of his own subordinates, Wang Shangbin and others, and Jin was pleased.

sentences.zh: 給事中郗夔核榆林功，懼失瑾意，自縊死。

translations.literal: Assistant secretary Xi Kui, while examining the merits at Yulin, feared losing Jin's favor and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Xi Kui, while reviewing merits at Yulin, feared losing Jin's favor and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 給事中屈銓、祭酒王雲鳳請編瑾行事，著為律令。

translations.literal: Assistant secretary Qu Quan and Grand Academy rector Wang Yunfeng asked that Jin's conduct be compiled and made into law.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Qu Quan and Grand Academy rector Wang Yunfeng asked that Jin's conduct be compiled and enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，安化王寘鐇反，檄數瑾罪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, in the fourth month, the Anhua prince Zhifan rebelled and posted a proclamation listing Jin's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, Prince of Anhua Zhu Zhifan rebelled and issued a proclamation enumerating Jin's crimes.

sentences.zh: 瑾始懼，匿其檄，而起都御史楊一清、太監張永為總督，討之。

translations.literal: Jin finally became afraid, hid the proclamation, and appointed Grand Censor Yang Yiqing and eunuch Zhang Yong as commanders to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin at last grew afraid, concealed the proclamation, and appointed Grand Censor Yang Yiqing and eunuch Zhang Yong as overall commanders to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，與瑾同為八虎者，當瑾專政時，有所請多不應，永成、大用等皆怨瑾。

translations.literal: At first, among the Eight Tigers who were with Jin, when Jin monopolized the administration their requests were often not granted, and Yongcheng and Dayong and the others all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Eight Tigers who had risen with Jin, many found their requests denied once he monopolized power; Yongcheng, Dayong, and the others all resented him.

sentences.zh: 又欲逐永，永以譎免。

translations.literal: He also wanted to drive Yong away, but Yong escaped through trickery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also tried to drive Yong away, but Yong escaped through cunning.

sentences.zh: 及永出師還，欲因誅瑾，一清為畫策，永意遂決。

translations.literal: When Yong's army returned from the campaign, he wanted to use the opportunity to kill Jin; Yang Yiqing drew up the plan, and Yong's resolve was then set.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong returned from campaign, he resolved to use the opportunity to bring Jin down; Yang Yiqing devised the plan, and Yong's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 瑾好招致術士，有俞日明者，妄言瑾從孫二漢當大貴。

translations.literal: Jin liked to gather sorcerers. There was one Yu Riming who falsely claimed that Jin's grandnephew Erhan was destined for great nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Jin liked to gather sorcerers. One Yu Riming falsely declared that Jin's grandnephew Erhan was destined for great nobility.

sentences.zh: 兵仗局太監孫和數遺以甲仗，兩廣鎮監潘午、蔡昭又為造弓弩，瑾皆藏於家。

translations.literal: Eunuch Sun He of the Weapons Bureau repeatedly sent him armor and weapons, and the garrison supervisors Pan Wu and Cai Zhao of the two Guang regions also made bows and crossbows for him, all of which Jin stored in his home.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, eunuch of the Armaments Bureau, repeatedly sent him armor and weapons, while frontier supervisors Pan Wu and Cai Zhao of the two Guang provinces also made bows and crossbows for him, all of which Jin hoarded at home.

sentences.zh: 永捷疏至，將以八月十五日獻俘，瑾使緩其期。

translations.literal: When Yong's urgent memorial arrived, saying the prisoners would be presented on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, Jin had the date postponed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong's victory memorial arrived, scheduling the presentation of captives for the fifteenth day of the eighth month, Jin had the date postponed.

sentences.zh: 永慮有變，遂先期入，獻俘畢，帝置酒勞永，瑾等皆侍。

translations.literal: Yong feared there might be a change, so he entered ahead of schedule; after the prisoners were presented, the emperor set out wine to reward Yong, and Jin and the others all attended.
translations.idiomatic: Yong feared a plot and entered the capital ahead of schedule; after the captives were presented, the emperor set out wine to reward him, with Jin and the others in attendance.

sentences.zh: 及夜，瑾退，永出寘鐇檄，因奏瑾不法十七事。

translations.literal: That evening, after Jin withdrew, Yong produced Zhifan's proclamation and then memorialized seventeen crimes of Jin's unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, after Jin withdrew, Yong produced Zhifan's proclamation and memorialized seventeen counts of Jin's unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝已被酒，俯首曰：「瑾負我。」

translations.literal: The emperor had already been drinking, and with his head bowed he said: "Jin has betrayed me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already drunk, bowed his head and said, "Jin has betrayed me.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「此不可緩。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "This cannot be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "This cannot wait."

sentences.zh: 永成等亦助之。

translations.literal: Yongcheng and the others also helped him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng and the others lent their support as well.

sentences.zh: 遂執瑾，繫於菜廠，分遣官校封其內外私第。

translations.literal: They then seized Jin and bound him in the vegetable depot, and sent officials and guards to seal up his private residences inside and outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized Jin and bound him at the vegetable depot, dispatching officials and guards to seal his residences inside and outside the city.

sentences.zh: 次日晏朝後，帝出永奏示內閣，降瑾奉御，謫居鳳陽。

translations.literal: The next day, after the late court audience, the emperor brought out Yong's memorial and showed it to the Grand Secretariat, demoted Jin to fengyu, and banished him to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, after the late audience, the emperor showed Yong's memorial to the Grand Secretariat, demoted Jin to palace attendant, and banished him to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 帝親籍其家，得偽璽一，穿宮牌五百及衣甲、弓弩、袞衣、玉帶諸違禁物。

translations.literal: The emperor personally inventoried his household and found a forged seal, five hundred palace passes, and forbidden items such as armor, bows, embroidered robes, and jade belts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally searched his household and found a forged seal, five hundred palace passes, and forbidden items including armor, bows, embroidered robes, and jade belts.

sentences.zh: 又所常持扇，內藏利匕首二。

translations.literal: In his usual fan there were also hidden two sharp daggers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fan he habitually carried were hidden two sharp daggers.

sentences.zh: 始大怒曰：「奴果反。」

translations.literal: The emperor at last flew into a great rage, saying: "The slave really has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At last the emperor flew into a rage, saying, "The slave truly meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 趣付獄。

translations.literal: He hastily sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jin sent straight to prison.

sentences.zh: 獄具，詔磔於市，梟其首，榜獄詞處決圖示天下。

translations.literal: When the case was completed, an edict ordered him torn to pieces in the market, his head displayed on a pike, and the prison verdicts posted so the whole world could see the execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, an edict ordered him dismembered in the market, his head displayed, and the prison verdicts posted throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 族人、逆黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: His clan and the rebel faction were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen and fellow conspirators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 張綵獄斃，磔其屍。

translations.literal: Zhang Cai died in prison, and his corpse was torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai died in prison, and his corpse was dismembered.

sentences.zh: 閣臣焦芳、劉宇、曹元而下，尚書畢亨、朱恩等，共六十餘人，皆降謫。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat ministers Jiao Fang, Liu Yu, and Cao Yuan, as well as ministers such as Bi Heng and Zhu En, more than sixty in all, were all demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat members Jiao Fang, Liu Yu, and Cao Yuan, together with ministers such as Bi Heng and Zhu En—more than sixty in all—were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 已，廷臣奏瑾所變法，吏部二十四事，戶部三十餘事，兵部十八事，工部十三事，詔悉厘正如舊制。

translations.literal: Afterward the court ministers memorialized on Jin's altered laws: twenty-four changes in the Ministry of Personnel, more than thirty in the Ministry of Revenue, eighteen in the Ministry of War, and thirteen in the Ministry of Works; an edict ordered all of them corrected back to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter court ministers memorialized on Jin's altered regulations: twenty-four in the Ministry of Personnel, more than thirty in the Ministry of Revenue, eighteen in the Ministry of War, and thirteen in the Ministry of Works; an edict ordered all restored to the old system.

sentences.zh: 張永，保定新城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong was a man of Xincheng in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong was a native of Xincheng in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 正德初，總神機營，與瑾為黨。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengde he commanded the Divinely Mechanized Camp and was part of Jin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde he commanded the Divinely Mechanized Camp and was at first allied with Jin.

sentences.zh: 已而惡其所為，瑾亦覺其不附己也，言於帝，將黜之南京。

translations.literal: Soon he came to dislike Jin's conduct, and Jin also sensed that he was no longer loyal; Jin spoke to the emperor and was about to dismiss Yong to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to detest Jin's conduct, and Jin in turn sensed that he no longer stood with him; Jin spoke to the emperor and was about to have Yong dismissed to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 永知之，直趨帝前，訴瑾陷己。

translations.literal: Yong learned of it, went straight before the emperor, and complained that Jin was framing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong learned of it, went straight before the emperor, and accused Jin of framing him.

sentences.zh: 帝召瑾與質，方爭辯，永輒奮拳毆瑾。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Jin to confront him, and while they were arguing, Yong suddenly threw a punch and hit Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Jin to confront him, and in the midst of their argument Yong suddenly struck Jin with his fist.

sentences.zh: 帝令谷大用等置酒為解，由是二人益不合。

translations.literal: The emperor had Gu Dayong and the others set out wine to resolve it, and from that point the two were even less able to get along.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Gu Dayong and the others set out wine to reconcile them, but from that point the two were even less able to coexist.

sentences.zh: 及寘鐇反，命永及右都御史楊一清往討。

translations.literal: When Zhifan rebelled, Yong and the Right Grand Censor Yang Yiqing were ordered to go and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhifan rebelled, Yong and Right Censor-in-chief Yang Yiqing were ordered to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服送之東華門，賜關防、金瓜、鋼斧以行，寵遇甚盛。

translations.literal: The emperor sent them off in military dress at Donghua Gate and gave them passes, golden melons, and steel axes for the journey, showing them extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw them off in military dress at Donghua Gate and bestowed passes, golden melons, and steel axes for the journey—a mark of extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 瑾亦忌之，而帝方永，不能間也。

translations.literal: Jin also envied him, but the emperor favored Yong so much that he could not create discord.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envied him as well, but the emperor was so devoted to Yong that he could not drive them apart.

sentences.zh: 師出，寘鐇已擒，永遂率五百騎撫定余黨。

translations.literal: Before the army had gone far, Zhifan had already been captured, and Yong then led five hundred cavalry to pacify the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army had gone far, Zhifan had already been captured; Yong then led five hundred cavalry to pacify the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 還次靈州，與一清言，欲奏瑾不法事。

translations.literal: When he reached Lingzhou on the return march, he spoke with Yang Yiqing and wanted to memorialize Jin's unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he halted at Lingzhou on the return march, he spoke with Yang Yiqing about memorializing Jin's crimes.

sentences.zh: 一清曰：「彼在上左右，公言能必入乎？

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing said, 'He is around the emperor. Are you sure your words can get in?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing said, "He is at the emperor's side. Can you be sure your words will reach him?

sentences.zh: 不如以計誅之。」

translations.literal: It would be better to kill him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to destroy him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 因為永畫策，永大喜，語詳一清傳。

translations.literal: Then he drew up a plan for Yong, who was greatly pleased. The details are in Yang Yiqing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out a plan for Yong, who was greatly pleased; the details are given in Yang Yiqing's biography.

sentences.zh: 是時，瑾兄都督同知景祥死，京師籍籍謂瑾將以八月十五日俟百官送葬，因作亂。

translations.literal: At that time, Jin's elder brother, the deputy regional commander Jing Xiang, died, and rumors spread in the capital that Jin would wait until the fifteenth day of the eighth month, when the officials came to escort the funeral, and then stage a revolt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jin's elder brother, deputy regional commander Jing Xiang, died, and rumor spread through the capital that Jin would wait until the fifteenth day of the eighth month, when officials came to escort the funeral, and then rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 適永捷疏至，將以是日獻俘，瑾使緩其期，欲俟事成並擒永。

translations.literal: Just then Yong's urgent memorial arrived, saying that he would present the captives on that day. Jin ordered the date postponed, hoping to wait until the matter succeeded and seize Yong as well.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yong's victory memorial arrived, scheduling the presentation of captives for that very day; Jin ordered the date postponed, hoping to wait until his plan succeeded and seize Yong as well.

sentences.zh: 或以告永，永先期入獻俘，是夜遂奏誅瑾。

translations.literal: Someone informed Yong. Yong entered early to present the captives, and that night he memorialized the throne to have Jin executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Yong; he entered early to present the captives, and that very night memorialized for Jin's execution.

sentences.zh: 於是英國公張懋、兵部尚書王敞等，奏永輯寧中外，兩建奇勛，遂封永兄富為泰安伯、弟容為安定伯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of War Wang Chang, and others memorialized that Yong had pacified the court and the realm and had achieved two extraordinary merits, and so Yong's elder brother Fu was enfeoffed as Earl of Tai'an and his younger brother Rong as Earl of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of War Wang Chang, and others memorialized that Yong had pacified court and realm and won two extraordinary victories; Yong's elder brother Fu was enfeoffed as Earl of Tai'an and his younger brother Rong as Earl of Anding.

sentences.zh: 涿州男子王豸嘗刺龍形及「人王」字於足，永以為妖人，擒之。

translations.literal: A man from Zhuozhou named Wang Zhi had once tattooed a dragon shape and the characters 'human king' on his foot. Yong took him for an evil sorcerer and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Zhuozhou named Wang Zhi had once tattooed a dragon and the characters "Human King" on his foot; Yong took him for a sorcerer and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書何鑒乞加永封，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: Minister of War He Jian petitioned to add to Yong's title, and the matter was sent down for discussion by the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War He Jian petitioned to add to Yong's honors, and the matter was referred to the court for discussion.

sentences.zh: 永欲身自封侯，引劉永誠、鄭和故事風廷臣，內閣以非制格之。

translations.literal: Yong wanted to be enfeoffed personally as a marquis, citing the precedent of Liu Yongcheng and Zheng He to pressure the ministers, but the Grand Secretariat blocked it as contrary to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wished to be enfeoffed as marquis in his own person, citing the precedents of Liu Yongcheng and Zheng He to pressure the ministers, but the Grand Secretariat blocked it as contrary to regulation.

sentences.zh: 永意沮，乃辭免恩澤。

translations.literal: Yong's intention was discouraged, so he declined the bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Discouraged, Yong declined the bounty.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書楊一清言宜聽永讓，以成其賢，事竟已。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing said that Yong should be allowed to yield, so as to complete his virtue, and the matter ended there.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing argued that Yong should be allowed to yield, thereby completing his reputation for virtue, and the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 久之，坐庫官盜庫銀事，閑住。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was placed on inactive duty because of the case of a treasury official stealing silver from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was placed on inactive duty because a treasury official had stolen silver from the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 九年，北邊有警，命永督宣府、大同、延綏軍禦之，寇退乃還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, there was trouble on the northern frontier. Yong was ordered to command the armies of Xuanfu, Datong, and Yansui against it, and he returned only after the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when trouble broke out on the northern frontier, Yong was ordered to command the armies of Xuanfu, Datong, and Yansui against the enemy; he returned only after the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，帝南征，永率邊兵二千先行。

translations.literal: When Prince Ning Chenhao rebelled, the emperor campaigned south, and Yong led 2,000 border troops ahead.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao rebelled, the emperor marched south, and Yong led two thousand frontier troops ahead.

sentences.zh: 時王守仁已擒宸濠，檻車北上。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shouren had already captured Chenhao and was sending him north in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wang Shouren had already captured Chenhao and was escorting him north in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 永以帝意遮守仁，欲縱宸濠於鄱陽湖，俟帝至與戰。

translations.literal: Yong, relying on the emperor's intention, blocked Wang Shouren, wanting to release Chenhao at Poyang Lake and wait for the emperor to arrive and fight him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, acting on the emperor's presumed wish, blocked Shouren and wanted to release Chenhao on Poyang Lake so the emperor could arrive and fight him personally.

sentences.zh: 守仁不可，至杭州詣永。

translations.literal: Shouren would not agree, and when he reached Hangzhou he went to see Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren refused; when he reached Hangzhou he went to see Yong.

sentences.zh: 永拒不見，守仁叱門者徑入，大呼曰：「我王守仁也，來與公議國家事，何拒我！」

translations.literal: Yong refused to receive him. Shouren shouted at the gatekeeper and went straight in, calling out, 'I am Wang Shouren. I have come to discuss state affairs with you. Why refuse me!
translations.idiomatic: Yong refused to receive him. Shouren shouted down the gatekeeper and went straight in, calling out, "I am Wang Shouren! I have come to discuss affairs of state with you—why turn me away?

sentences.zh: 永為氣懾。

translations.literal: Yong was cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was overawed.

sentences.zh: 守仁因言江西荼毒已極，王師至，亂將不測。

translations.literal: Shouren then said that Jiangxi had already been ravaged to the limit, and when the imperial army arrived, the disorder would be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren then said that Jiangxi had already been ravaged beyond endurance and that once the imperial army arrived, the disorder would be incalculable.

sentences.zh: 永大悟，乃曰：「群小在側，永來，欲保護聖躬耳，非欲攘功也。」

translations.literal: Yong then realized it and said, 'With those petty men around me, I came only to protect the sacred person, not to seize the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Yong saw it at once and said, "With petty men at my side, I came only to protect the emperor's person—not to steal the credit.

sentences.zh: 因指江上檻車曰：「此宜歸我。」

translations.literal: Then he pointed to the caged cart on the river and said, 'This should be returned to me.'
translations.idiomatic: He then pointed to the caged cart on the river and said, "That should be mine."
