sentences.zh: 守仁曰：「我何用此。」

translations.literal: Shouren said, 'What use would I have for this?'
translations.idiomatic: Shouren replied, "What use would I have for it?"

sentences.zh: 即付永，而與永偕還江西。

translations.literal: He immediately gave it to Yong, and the two returned together to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately handed it over to Yong, and the two returned together to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時太監張忠等已從大江至南昌，方窮治逆黨，見永至，大沮。

translations.literal: At that time, the eunuch Zhang Zhong and others had already come from the Yangzi River to Nanchang and were busy investigating the rebel party; when they saw Yong arrive, they were greatly frustrated.
translations.idiomatic: By then the eunuch Zhang Zhong and others had already come up the Yangzi to Nanchang and were ruthlessly prosecuting the rebel party; when they saw Yong arrive, they were deeply dismayed.

sentences.zh: 永留數旬，促忠同歸，江西賴以安。

translations.literal: Yong stayed for several tens of days and urged Zhong to return with him, and Jiangxi relied on him to remain at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yong remained several weeks and pressed Zhong to return with him; Jiangxi owed its calm to him.

sentences.zh: 忠等屢讒守仁，亦賴永營解獲免。

translations.literal: Zhong and the others repeatedly slandered Shouren, but Shouren was spared thanks to Yong's mediation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the others repeatedly slandered Shouren, but Shouren was spared thanks to Yong's intercession.

sentences.zh: 武宗崩，永督九門防變。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, Yong was put in charge of the Nine Gates to guard against disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, Yong was put in charge of the Nine Gates to guard against unrest.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，御史蕭淮奏谷大用、丘聚輩蠱惑先帝，黨惡為奸，並及永。

translations.literal: After the Shizong came to the throne, the censor Xiao Huai memorialized that Gu Dayong, Qiu Ju and their ilk had bewitched the former emperor, formed a gang of evil and done wrong, and included Yong as well.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong came to the throne, censor Xiao Huai memorialized that Gu Dayong, Qiu Ju, and their ilk had bewitched the late emperor, formed a wicked faction, and implicated Yong as well.

sentences.zh: 詔永閑住。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yong to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yong to retire from active duty.

sentences.zh: 已而淮復劾永在江西不法事，再降永奉御，司香孝陵，然永在江西，實非有不法也。

translations.literal: Soon after, Huai again accused Yong of illegal acts in Jiangxi, and Yong was again demoted to palace service and assigned to the incense service at the Ming Tombs. But in fact Yong's conduct in Jiangxi had not been unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai again accused Yong of misconduct in Jiangxi, and Yong was further demoted to palace attendant and assigned to tend incense at the imperial tombs—though in truth his conduct in Jiangxi had not been unlawful.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，大學士楊一清等言，永功大，不可泯，乃起永掌御用監，提督團營。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, the Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and others said Yong's merit was great and could not be erased, so Yong was brought back to manage the Directorate of Imperial Household and supervise the Corps Camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing, Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and others argued that Yong's merit was too great to be erased; he was recalled to head the Directorate of Imperial Household and supervise the regimented armies.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: He died soon after.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 谷大用

translations.literal: Gu Dayong
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dayong

sentences.zh: 谷大用者，瑾掌司禮監時提督西廠，分遣官校遠出偵事。

translations.literal: Gu Dayong, when Jin was in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial, supervised the Western Depot and sent officials and guards far and wide to spy on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dayong, when Jin was in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial, oversaw the Western Depot and sent officials and guards out to gather intelligence.

sentences.zh: 江西南康民吳登顯等，五月五日為競渡，誣以擅造龍舟，籍其家，天下皆重足屏息。

translations.literal: When the people of Wu Dengxian and others in Nankang, Jiangxi, held dragon-boat races on the fifth day of the fifth month, he falsely accused them of making dragon boats without permission and confiscated their households, so that all under heaven stood on tiptoe and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Nankang in Jiangxi held dragon-boat races on the fifth day of the fifth month, he falsely accused them of building dragon boats without authorization and confiscated their property, until all under heaven walked in fear and held their breath.

sentences.zh: 建鷹房草場於安州，奪民田無數。

translations.literal: He built an Eagle House and pasture grounds in Anzhou and seized countless people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: He built hawk houses and pasture grounds at Anzhou and seized countless fields from the people.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，大用辭西廠。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Dayong resigned from the Western Depot.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Dayong resigned from the Western Depot.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝復欲用之，大學士李東陽力諫乃止。

translations.literal: Not long after, the emperor again wanted to use him, but the Grand Secretary Li Dongyang strongly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the emperor again wished to employ him, but Grand Secretary Li Dongyang remonstrated forcefully and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉六、劉七反，命大用總督軍務，偕伏羌伯毛銳、兵部侍郎陸完討之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Liu Liu and Liu Qi rebelled. Dayong was ordered to take overall command of the military affairs and, together with Earl of Fuqiang Mao Rui and Vice Minister of War Lu Wan, suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Liu Liu and Liu Qi rebelled, Dayong was ordered to take overall command of military affairs and, together with Earl of Fuqiang Mao Rui and Vice Minister of War Lu Wan, suppress them.

sentences.zh: 大用駐臨清，召邊將許泰、郤永、江彬、劉暉等入內地，聽調遣。

translations.literal: Dayong was stationed at Linqing and summoned the frontier generals Xu Tai, Que Yong, Jiang Bin, Liu Hui, and others into the interior to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Dayong was stationed at Linqing and summoned frontier generals Xu Tai, Que Yong, Jiang Bin, Liu Hui, and others into the interior to await his orders.

sentences.zh: 久之無功，會賊過鎮江狼山，遇颶風舟覆，陸完兵至殲之，遂封大用弟大亮為永清伯。

translations.literal: After a long time no result was achieved. Then the rebels passed Mount Lang in Zhenjiang, where a gale overturned their boats. Lu Wan's troops arrived and annihilated them, and Dayong's younger brother Daliang was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongqing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stalemate, the rebels passed Mount Lang in Zhenjiang, where a hurricane overturned their boats; Lu Wan's troops arrived and annihilated them, and Dayong's younger brother Daliang was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 而先是平寘鐇時，其兄大寬已封高平伯矣，義子冒升賞者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhifan was pacified, his elder brother Dakuan had already been enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoping, and the number of adopted sons and men fraudulently promoted for reward cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhifan was suppressed, his elder brother Dakuan had already been enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoping, and the number of adopted sons and men fraudulently promoted for reward was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，以迎立功賜金幣。

translations.literal: When the Shizong came to the throne, he was rewarded with gold and silk for having helped bring about the accession.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne, Dayong was rewarded with gold and silk for his service in bringing about the succession.

sentences.zh: 給事中閻閎極論之，尋降奉御，居南京。

translations.literal: The giving-attendance censor Yan Hong made a strong memorial against him, and soon after he was demoted to palace service and sent to live in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant secretary Yan Hong memorialized against him in the strongest terms, and soon he was demoted to palace attendant and sent to live in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 已，召守康陵。

translations.literal: After that, he was summoned to guard the Kangling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to guard the Kangling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年籍其家。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiajing his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 魏彬，當瑾時，總三千營。

translations.literal: Wei Bin, during Jin's time, was in charge of the Three Thousand Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bin, during Jin's time, commanded the Three Thousand Battalion.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，代掌司禮監。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he took over the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Bin took over the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 其年，敘寧夏功，封弟英鎮安伯，馬永成兄山亦封平涼伯。

translations.literal: That year, in the account of the merits in Ningxia, his younger brother Ying was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhen'an, and Ma Yongcheng's elder brother Shan was also enfeoffed as Earl of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Ningxia campaign was rewarded, his younger brother Ying was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhen'an, and Ma Yongcheng's elder brother Shan was also made Earl of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，彬不自安，為英辭伯爵。

translations.literal: After the Shizong came to the throne, Bin felt uneasy and resigned the earldom on Ying's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong emperor came to the throne, Bin grew uneasy and had Ying resign the earldom.

sentences.zh: 詔改都督同知，世襲錦衣指揮使。

translations.literal: An edict changed him to deputy regional commander and made him a hereditary Guard Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reduced him to deputy regional commander with hereditary rank as Brocade Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊秉義、徐景嵩、吳嚴皆言彬附和逆瑾，結姻江彬，宜置極典。

translations.literal: The giving-attendance officials Yang Bingyi, Xu Jingsong, and Wu Yan all said Bin had followed and echoed the rebel Jin and had formed a marriage alliance with Jiang Bin, and should be punished with the severest law.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Yang Bingyi, Xu Jingsong, and Wu Yan all urged that Bin had echoed the rebel Jin and allied by marriage with Jiang Bin, and deserved the utmost penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝宥不問。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned him and did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 已而御史復論之，始令閑住。

translations.literal: Soon after, the censors again memorialized against him, and he was at last ordered to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the censors memorialized again, and at last he was ordered to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 張忠，霸州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong was a man of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong was a native of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 正德時御馬太監，與司禮張雄、東廠張銳並侍豹房用事，時號三張，性皆凶悖。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, he was a eunuch of the imperial stables. Along with Zhang Xiong of the Directorate of Ceremonial and Zhang Rui of the Eastern Depot, he served in the Leopard Quarter and wielded power; the three were called the Three Zhangs, and all were ferocious and perverse in temperament.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign he was eunuch director of the imperial stables; with Zhang Xiong of the Directorate of Ceremonial and Zhang Rui of the Eastern Depot he served in the Leopard Quarter and wielded power—the three were called the Three Zhangs, all savage and lawless in character.

sentences.zh: 忠利大盜張茂財，結為弟，引入豹房，侍帝蹴鞠。

translations.literal: He took advantage of the great bandit Zhang Mao's wealth, made him a brother, brought him into the Leopard Quarter, and had him attend the emperor at polo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong coveted the wealth of the great bandit Zhang Mao, took him as a sworn brother, brought him into the Leopard Quarter, and had him attend the emperor at kickball.

sentences.zh: 而雄至怨其父不愛己致自宮，拒不見。

translations.literal: As for Xiong, he bitterly resented his father for not loving him and causing him to castrate himself, and he refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, meanwhile, bitterly resented his father for driving him to castration and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 同儕勸之，乃垂簾杖其父，然後相抱泣，其無人理如此。

translations.literal: His companions urged him, so he lowered a curtain and beat his father with a staff, and only then did they embrace and weep; such was his lack of humanity.
translations.idiomatic: When his fellows urged him, he drew a curtain and beat his father with a staff, then embraced him and wept—such was his perversity.

sentences.zh: 銳以捕妖言功，加祿至一百二十石。

translations.literal: Rui gained merit by arresting sorcerous talk, and his salary was raised to 120 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Rui won promotion of salary to one hundred twenty piculs for arresting those who spread sorcerous talk.

sentences.zh: 每緝事，先令邏卒誘人為奸，乃捕之，得賄則釋，往往以危法中人。

translations.literal: Whenever he conducted investigations, he first ordered patrolmen to lure people into committing crimes, then arrested them; if they took bribes, he released them, often ensnaring people through harsh laws.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he investigated a case he first had patrolmen lure people into crime, then arrested them; if bribes were paid he released them—thus he often trapped men with harsh laws.

sentences.zh: 三人並交通宸濠，受臧賢、錢寧等賄，以助成其叛。

translations.literal: The three all had dealings with Chenhao and accepted bribes from Zang Xian, Qian Ning, and others in order to help complete the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: All three had dealings with the Prince of Ning and took bribes from Zang Xian, Qian Ning, and others to help the rebellion along.

sentences.zh: 寧王反，忠勸帝親征。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning rebelled, Zhong urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning rebelled, Zhong urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 其遮王守仁捷，欲縱宸濠鄱陽，待帝自戰，皆忠之謀也。

translations.literal: Their blocking of Wang Shouren's victory report and their plan to release Chenhao at Poyang and wait for the emperor to fight him were all Zhong's schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Their intercepting Wang Shouren's victory report and their plan to release the prince at Poyang and let the emperor fight him himself were all Zhong's schemes.

sentences.zh: 是時，又有吳經者，尤親匿。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a man named Wu Jing, who was especially close to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was also Wu Jing, whom the emperor favored above all others.

sentences.zh: 帝南征，經先至揚州。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south, Jing arrived in Yangzhou first.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Jing went ahead to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜半燃炬通衢，遍入寡婦、處女家，掠以出，號哭震遠近，許以金贖，貧者多自經。

translations.literal: At midnight he would light torches on the main streets, enter the homes of widows and maidens one by one, seize them and carry them off. Their crying shook near and far, and he promised they could ransom themselves with gold; many of the poor hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He would light torches in the main streets at midnight, enter the homes of widows and maidens one by one, seize them and carry them off; their cries shook the countryside. He promised ransom in gold, and many of the poor hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 先是，又有劉允者，以正德十年奉敕往迎烏斯藏僧，所賫金寶以百餘萬計。

translations.literal: Earlier there had also been a man named Liu Yun, who in the tenth year of Zhengde received an edict to go and welcome Tibetan monks, carrying gold and treasure worth more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been Liu Yun, who in the tenth year of Zhengde was ordered to go welcome Tibetan monks, carrying gold and treasure worth more than a million.

sentences.zh: 廷臣交章諫，不聽。

translations.literal: The ministers repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers remonstrated in memorial after memorial, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 允至成都，治裝歲餘，費又數十萬，公私匱竭。

translations.literal: When Yun reached Chengdu, it took more than a year to prepare, costing several hundred thousand more, and both public and private funds were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun reached Chengdu it took more than a year to prepare the mission, costing several hundred thousand more; public and private funds alike were drained dry.

sentences.zh: 既至，為番人所襲。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was attacked by the fan people.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived he was attacked by the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 允走免，將士死者數百人，盡亡其所賫。

translations.literal: Yun escaped, but several hundred soldiers and officers died, and everything he had brought was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yun escaped, but several hundred officers and men were killed and everything he had brought was lost.

sentences.zh: 及歸，武宗已崩，世宗用御史王鈞等言，張忠、吳經發孝陵衛充軍，張雄、張銳下都察院鞫治、允亦得罪。

translations.literal: When he returned, the Wuzong had already died. The Shizong, taking the words of the censor Wang Jun and others, sent Zhang Zhong and Wu Jing to the Xiaoling Guard to serve as soldiers, sent Zhang Xiong and Zhang Rui to the Censorate for investigation and punishment, and Yun also incurred punishment.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned the Wuzong emperor had died. The Shizong, acting on censors such as Wang Jun, sent Zhang Zhong and Wu Jing to military service at the Xiaoling Guard, had Zhang Xiong and Zhang Rui tried by the Censorate, and punished Yun as well.

sentences.zh: 世宗習見正德時宦侍之禍，即位後御近侍甚嚴，有罪撻之至死，或陳屍示戒。

translations.literal: The Shizong had long witnessed the disasters caused by eunuch attendants in the Zhengde reign, and after his accession he kept a very strict hand on close attendants. Those who were guilty he beat to death, or displayed their bodies as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong had seen close at hand the disasters eunuch attendants brought in the Zhengde years; after his accession he kept them under strict control, beating the guilty to death or displaying their corpses as a warning.

sentences.zh: 張佐、鮑忠，麥福、黃錦輩，雖由興邸舊人掌司禮監，督東廠，然皆謹飭不敢大肆。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo, Bao Zhong, Mai Fu, Huang Jin, and the like, though they were old retainers of the Xing residence and held the Directorate of Ceremonial and supervised the Eastern Depot, were all cautious and disciplined and did not dare to run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo, Bao Zhong, Mai Fu, Huang Jin, and the like—though old retainers from the Xing mansion who headed the Directorate of Ceremonial and supervised the Eastern Depot—were all cautious and did not dare run riot.

sentences.zh: 帝又盡撤天下鎮守內臣及典京營倉場者，終四十餘年不復設，故內臣之勢，惟嘉靖朝少殺云。

translations.literal: The emperor also completely removed the inner eunuchs stationed throughout the empire and those in charge of the Beijing Camp granaries and stores; for more than forty years thereafter they were never restored. Thus the power of the inner eunuchs was diminished only slightly in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also removed entirely the eunuch garrison commissioners throughout the empire and those who managed the capital camps and granaries; for more than forty years thereafter such posts were not restored. Thus eunuch power abated somewhat only in the Jiajing reign, as the account concludes.
